a_rows_sample.anchor: The Annotated Bilattice Kernel (ABK-1) extends First-Degree Entailment (FDE / Belnap-Dunn 4-valued logic) to eliminate the structural distinction collapses identified in prior kernel evaluations ... ABK-1 resolves these deficiencies by embedding the standard 4-valued truth space BF_4 into an Annotated Bilattice Frame B_ABK. Each proposition is represented as an annotated truth tuple that pairs an FDE valuation with a justification graph, a temporal validity window, and modal/scope metadata.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces ABK-1: an architecture that embeds standard 4-valued FDE (BF_4) into an Annotated Bilattice Frame, pairing each proposition's FDE valuation with a justification graph, temporal validity window, and modal/scope metadata, explicitly targeting the lineage/temporal/underdetermined collapses previously measured against bare FDE (this batch's r-req-fde-kernel-test-vectors-result).

a_rows_sample.anchor: State(phi) = <nu(phi), J(phi), tau(phi), mu(phi)> ... FDE Truth Valuation nu in BF_4 ... Justification Graph J = <V_J, E_J, m> ... Temporal Validity Window tau = <t_start, t_end, v_D, TTL> ... Modal and Boundary Metadata mu = <Type, Modality, ScopeMask>
a_rows_sample.statement: Formal definition of the ABK-1 state 4-tuple State(phi)=<nu,J,tau,mu>: nu is the FDE truth valuation in the powerset of {T,F}; J=<V_J,E_J,m> is a justification DAG (premise nodes, derivation edges, justification mode in {Evidenced,Inferred,Reported,Assumed}); tau=<t_start,t_end,v_D,TTL> is a temporal validity window with a dependency version vector; mu=<Type,Modality,ScopeMask> carries Analytic/Synthetic, Necessary/Contingent, and a scope bitmask.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Order (<=_k): S1 <=_k S2 iff (nu1 subseteq nu2) and (J1 sqsubseteq_DAG J2) ... Truth Order (<=_t): S1 <=_t S2 iff (T in nu1 implies T in nu2) and (F in nu2 implies F in nu1) ... Conjunction (x_t) ... Disjunction (+_t) ... combining FDE valuation, justification-DAG union, temporal intersection, and metadata AND (mu1 (dot) mu2).
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines ABK-1's algebraic lattice structure over B_ABK = BF_4 x J x T x M: a Knowledge Order (<=_k, comparing valuation-subset and DAG-substructure) and a Truth Order (<=_t, standard FDE truth ordering), plus lattice conjunction and disjunction operators that combine FDE valuations via standard FDE meet/join, union justification DAGs, intersect temporal validity windows, and combine modal metadata via a metadata-AND operator.

type_signature.codomain: boolean order relations, or a combined ABK-1 state

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suite 1.2 Underdetermined vs. Unknown | FAIL | PASS (via J.nodes.length > 0) | PASS ... Suite 2.1 Inferred vs. Assumed | FAIL | PASS (via J.mode) | PASS ... Suite 3.1 Stale vs. Expired | FAIL | PASS (via tau.tEnd and v_D) | PASS ... The Annotated Bilattice Kernel (ABK-1) achieves a 100% Pass Rate across all Tier P1 and Tier P2 distinction verification suites, qualifying it for ratification as a fully R_req-compliant KnowledgeOS kernel engine.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports that ABK-1, re-run against the SPEC-RREQ-TEST-2026-V1 suite, converts all three of the bare-FDE test failures found earlier in this batch (Underdetermined-vs-Unknown via presence of justification-graph nodes; Inferred-vs-Assumed via J.mode; Stale-vs-Expired via temporal window and dependency-version comparison) into PASSes, alongside the two bare-FDE PASSes it retains (Contradiction-vs-Unknown; Absence-vs-Evidence-of-Absence), yielding a claimed 100% pass rate across Tier P1/P2 and a recommendation to ratify ABK-1 as R_req-compliant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: export class ABKState { public val: FDEValue; public justification: JustificationGraph; public temporal: TemporalWindow; public metadata: ModalMetadata; ... resolveKnowledgeStatus(currentTime, upstreamVersions): KnowledgeStatus { if (this.resolveCurrency(...) === 'Expired') return 'NotAssessed'; switch(this.val) { case 'B': return 'Contradictory'; ... case 'N': { if (this.justification.nodes.length > 0) return 'Underdetermined'; return 'Unknown'; } } }
a_rows_sample.statement: Provides a full TypeScript reference implementation of ABK-1: an ABKState class carrying val/justification/temporal/metadata fields with resolveKnowledgeStatus (currency-checks first, then value-switches, distinguishing Underdetermined from Unknown by non-empty justification nodes), resolveCurrency (Expired if past tEnd, Stale if any dependency version has advanced, else Current), and resolveJustificationMode methods; and an ABKAlgebra class with a hard-coded FDE conjunction truth table and a meet() operation merging justification DAGs (node/edge union), temporal windows (intersection), and metadata (conjunctive AND, scope-mask bitwise AND).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Architectural Specification: ABK-1 / Contr Bridge Interface (ABK-CONTR-INT-v1) ... The Contr Isolation Module operates directly on top of the Annotated Bilattice Kernel (ABK-1) to handle non-explosion, contradiction trap frames, and resolution state tracking for paraconsistent evaluations. ... When an inbound assertion or lattice operation produces a contradictory valuation (nu(phi)=B), the ABK-1 engine delegates contradiction containment to ABKContrBridge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a bridge architecture (SPEC-ABK-CONTR-2026-V1) between ABK-1 and a Contr contradiction-isolation engine: whenever an ABK-1 lattice operation produces a contradictory valuation (nu=B), the engine delegates containment to an ABKContrBridge that traps the state in a local frame, sets ResolutionStatus=Unresolved, and initializes an evidential polarity edge graph, ensuring downstream inference cannot propagate the contradiction beyond a bounded contextual scope.

a_rows_sample.anchor: export interface IABKContrBridge { shouldIsolate(state): boolean; isolateContradiction(...): ContrIsolationPayload; updateResolutionStatus(...): ContradictionTrapFrame; evaluateResolution(frameId): ABKState; } ... evaluateResolution ... if (totalWeight > 0.5) { resolvedVal='T'; resolution='Resolved'; } else if (totalWeight < -0.5) { resolvedVal='F'; resolution='Resolved'; } else { resolvedVal='B'; resolution='Irresolvable'; }
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the IABKContrBridge TypeScript interface (shouldIsolate, isolateContradiction, updateResolutionStatus, evaluateResolution) and its ABKContrBridge implementation: contradiction resolution sums signed evidential-polarity weights across conflicting sources and resolves to True (Resolved) if the sum exceeds +0.5, False (Resolved) if below -0.5, or remains contradictory (Irresolvable) if the weights are near-balanced -- a simple threshold-based weighted-voting resolution rule for the contradiction lifecycle.

type_signature.domain: a contradiction trap frame with polarity-weighted evidence edges
type_signature.codomain: a resolved (or still-contradictory) ABKState plus a ResolutionStatus

a_rows_sample.anchor: describe('ABK-1 / Contr Bridge Integration Suite' ... it('should detect contradictory valuations (B) and trigger isolation' ... it('should mark frame as Irresolvable when evidence weights cancel out' ...
a_rows_sample.statement: Provides a runnable Jest end-to-end integration test suite (abk-contr-integration.test.ts) covering contradiction detection and trap-frame creation, non-explosion verification (an isolated contradictory proposition does not pollute an unrelated proposition's algebra), and resolution-lifecycle management (transition through InProgress/Resolved, resolving to True when positive evidence dominates, and remaining Irresolvable when weights cancel).

a_rows_sample.anchor: There is one additional missing bridge ... Adequacy -> Executability ... we need one more formal relation: ExecutableAdequacy. EA(K,O,Q,Gamma) meaning: the representation and operations together can answer the required questions while preserving every required distinction and producing an auditable transition. b_rows_sample.anchor: Theorem (Closure and Structural Completeness): ... R_req is structurally complete if and only if every minimal information requirement I(tau) for all tau in T is mapped to a non-collapsing partition in R_req. Proof Construction (By Information-Theoretic Partitioning): 1. Sufficiency ... 2. Minimality ... 3. Closure: R_req is closed under Boolean operations on equivalence relations.
b_rows_sample.statement: States and sketches a proof for a Structural Completeness Theorem for R_req: R_req is structurally complete iff every minimal information requirement of every minimal operational task (contradiction isolation, Zero-state checking, epistemic query resolution, temporal garbage collection) maps to a non-collapsing partition. The proof construction has three parts: Sufficiency (append any distinction found missing by a task-output divergence), Minimality (keep only distinctions with a witnessing test vector), and Closure (R_req closed under Boolean operations on equivalence relations, sim_{d_i AND d_j} = sim_{d_i} intersect sim_{d_j}).

type_signature.domain: task set T and distinction set R_req

b_rows_sample.statement: Adds D-1.3 Explicit-vs-Implicit Knowledge to the R_req inventory (Tier P1): Explicit(phi) iff phi in K; Implicit(phi) iff phi not-in K and K entails phi; explicit lookup is O(1), implicit deduction is NP-hard in general -- connecting this batch's FR-1/K^exp-K^der distinction into the R_req formal distinction inventory with a stated complexity class.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 4.1 Integration with Contr ... When two incoming streams present e1 |- P and e2 |- not-P: 1. Contr sets KnowledgeStatus(P) = Contradictory (B={T,F} in FDE). 2. It prevents total logical explosion by trapping the assertion within an isolated contradiction frame. 3. It initializes ResolutionStatus(P) = Unresolved. 4. If d in R_req were collapsed, Contr would either trigger classical explosion or falsely collapse the state into Unknown.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the required integration between R_req and the Contr contradiction-isolation subsystem: on conflicting evidence e1|-P and e2|-not-P, Contr must set KnowledgeStatus(P)=Contradictory, trap the assertion in an isolated frame to prevent explosion, and initialize ResolutionStatus(P)=Unresolved; explicitly states that collapsing any of D-1.1/D-3.1/D-4.1 would force either classical explosion or a false collapse into Unknown.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 4.2 Integration with Zero Lens Specification ... 0_KnowledgeOS iff for all P in K: (Status(P) not-in {Contradictory, Underdetermined} and Currency(P) == Current)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a formal Zero-state predicate for KnowledgeOS: 0_KnowledgeOS holds iff every proposition P in K has KnowledgeStatus(P) not in {Contradictory, Underdetermined} and Currency(P)==Current, i.e. no unsatisfied requirements or unhandled contradictions and no stale dependencies; requires all R_req distinctions to remain expressible without loss.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 4.3 Integration with Evaluation Engine ... Loss_{R_req}(pi) = sum_{d_i in R_req} w_i * I(Collapse(d_i,pi)) ... An adequate kernel projection requires Loss_{R_req}(pi) == 0 for all P1 distinctions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a quantitative Loss function for the Evaluation Engine using R_req as its metric: Loss_{R_req}(pi) = sum over d_i in R_req of w_i times an indicator of whether pi collapses d_i, with priority weights w_i (P1=1.0, P2=0.5); an adequate kernel projection must achieve Loss_{R_req}(pi)==0 for every Tier-P1 distinction -- a concrete quantification of the Representation Adequacy principle.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ADR-AIP-04 -- Capability Discovery Proposal, seventeen sections: Context ... Capability Inventory ... Ownership Analysis ... Invariants ... Role/Stewardship Analysis ... Candidate Contexts or Stewardships ... Open Questions ... PO/ARB Decisions Required.
a_rows_sample.statement: A fixed seventeen-section deliverable structure is mandated for the ADR-AIP-04 discovery proposal, spanning context through to PO/ARB decisions required.

a_rows_sample.statement: Overall verdict: the discovery proposal is returned for material correction on two evidence claims (six-role hypothesis, C-14 status) while its DDD discipline, mechanism evidence, and refusal to promote C-19 to a bounded context are found to survive independent falsification.

a_rows_sample.statement: Because the discovery's Section 13 stewardship reading materially matches the untracked document's 'Option B', but I-did-not-read-it is a self-declared and unattestable claim, the question of independent convergence vs reconstruction from an unread source is classified OPEN, and the convergence must not be counted as corroboration.

a_rows_sample.statement: Finding W-4: Amendment 1 violates its own lane's requirement to disclose a producing process; its authorship is only inferable, and no correction assignment was ever registered for its production -- a governance/provenance defect distinct from the content defects.

a_rows_sample.anchor: THE CORRECTION SUCCEEDED. THE DECISION SURFACE IS NOT YET CLEAN.
a_rows_sample.statement: Overall verdict on Amendment 1: the corrective discipline succeeded in substance (no finding strengthened, no capability invented, nothing outside the proposal touched) but two defects (W-1's own recurrence of the truncated-search error; W-2's misplaced pointer) must land before the decision surface is clean for PO/ARB.

a_rows_sample.statement: The capability-first ordering is restated as the binding method for the entire discovery: capability -> ownership -> bounded context/stewardship -> human role -> agent -> platform service -> technology, with the explicit prohibition on beginning from role creation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: every invariant BC-7 owns is MECHANICALLY enforced; almost every invariant outside BC-7 is DECLARED ONLY. INFERRED: the platform's assurance is strong exactly where it is executable and weak exactly where it is prose -- and a role model is prose.
a_rows_sample.statement: The discovery's core structural result: BC-7's invariants (I-1 single mutation owner, I-2 HANDOFF+human START, I-3 sticky STOPPED, G-1 closure is a governance act, G-2 single writer for the Authority State) are all mechanically enforced, while almost every invariant outside BC-7 (R-34 producer!=acceptor, INV-ATTR-2 separation, AIP-11 frozen-artifact supersession, AIP-14 Product Primacy) is declared only, with no enforcement mechanism.

a_rows_sample.anchor: One process occupied verification -> architecture-review -> architecture-drafting -> domain roles in sequence, and in each lane recorded its own START -- a governance act -- because no separate governance process was present
a_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-9/F-9a: the drafting process itself, first-hand, occupied verification, architecture-review, architecture-drafting and domain roles in sequence within one process, self-recording its own STARTs each time -- evidence that 'Governance' as practised is a cross-cutting capability set with only ONE strictly-separated duty (acceptance/closure via COMPLETE, mechanically refused to non-governance/human writers), not a distinct actor.

a_rows_sample.anchor: an absence claim requires an exhaustive, untruncated search AND an explicit statement of what was searched. ... a search that can be truncated is not a survey.
a_rows_sample.statement: Amendment 1's root-cause finding (A1.0): both verified defects (V-1, V-2) share one mechanism -- an absence claim resting on a truncated search or an ungeneralised narrow claim -- proposing a durable discipline that an absence claim requires an exhaustive, untruncated search plus an explicit statement of what was searched.

a_rows_sample.statement: Correction #2's self-assessment: across the discovery, Amendment 1 and Correction #2, the same evidence-survey error class recurred three times, while the DDD reasoning method itself (capability-before-agent, parsimony, refusing role-inferred-capability) held; no finding is strengthened by Correction #2 and two (C-14, SB-3) end weaker than before.

a_rows_sample.statement: Overall verdict: the discovery/Amendment 1/Correction 2 package is READY FOR PO/ARB DECISION -- ungoverned material is properly routed to OQ-I, inferred ownership is refused at every convenient point, and eleven actual architectural decisions remain, none pre-empted; two low-severity residuals (missing supersession markers) do not block.

b_rows_sample.statement: Testing all four forbidden role-capability pairings (C-5->Verification, C-10->Knowledge, C-14->Governance, C-19->Communication) against evidence, none is established: consumer is not necessarily owner (C-5), the gap is delivery-mechanism not content (C-10, two-sided BC-1/BC-6), the live instance sits in BC-3 not Governance (C-14), and adoption of a role is explicitly not evidence a capability exists (C-19) -- framed as the discipline working correctly rather than failing to find an answer.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Governance is not only a gatekeeper. Governance also creates the operating environment in which the other roles can work safely. Therefore, Communication Engineer and Knowledge Engineer should not be treated as 'extra helpers'. They are platform capabilities.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues for extending a four-role production-lifecycle engineering model (Governance/Architecture/Implementation/Verification, mapping to Decide→Design→Build→Assure) with two cross-cutting platform roles, Communication Engineer (owns human↔AI communication quality/handovers/actor instructions) and Knowledge Engineer (owns knowledge lifecycle/evidence linking/architectural memory), analogized as the platform's nervous system and memory system respectively.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observations become capabilities only after repeated evidence and bounded responsibility. You now have enough evidence to propose them, but not to interrupt current decisions.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a DDD-derived legitimacy rule for promoting an observation into a platform capability: repeated evidence plus bounded responsibility must precede promotion, and this evidence bar being met is sufficient only to PROPOSE the capability, not to interrupt an in-flight architectural decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not add Communication Engineer and Knowledge Engineer into the active KOS-ATTR-ARCH-001 Stage 2 decision flow. First finish the current bounded-context decision. Then integrate them into the AI Engineering Platform as a platform evolution (ADR-AIP-04 or similar).
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends sequencing: do not integrate the two new roles into the active bounded-context decision flow now; finish that decision, freeze current architecture, then formalize the six-role model via a dedicated future ADR-AIP-04, applying the same discipline used with BC-7 ('do not redesign the platform while using the platform to discover the platform').

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 2 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: "what was said · what was observed · what was valid · what became effective · what was evaluated · what remains disputed" — and *"different temporal roles **must not be collapsed into one timestamp**."*
a_rows_sample.statement: S1-F036 proposes a six-way split of temporal roles that must not be collapsed into one timestamp: what was said, what was observed, what was valid, what became effective, what was evaluated, what remains disputed. Law carries TemporalValidity (valid-from/valid-until/superseded-by), which is 'what was valid' and attaches to the claim; History orders transitions; the other roles are not visibly members, though the Zero lens (absence typology) means this is not itself claimed as a gap -- v1.1 is the core domain model, not the whole architecture, and the other roles may live in surrounding contexts. What it does supply is a shape for the authority-temporal-validity gap (S1-F001/S2-R-F001): if six temporal roles must not collapse and validity is one of them, authority validity needs its own carrier -- precisely the gap measured at 0/20 grants and named by 'sufficient state' (S1-F034) as needing to be retainable. Three routes now converge on one hole; S2-R-F001 is updated with the verdict unchanged but the shape now specified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ***"What did we know at 13:47?"*** ... the fifth specified-and-unrun instrument ... and the only one whose result would change verdicts in this register directly.
a_rows_sample.statement: The acceptance test 'what did we know at 13:47?' (a checkable, temporal reconstruction question) is elevated by this review to the single most decision-relevant, highest-value unrun action in the entire register: running it is the cheapest available action that could resolve the register's central cluster, since five of six open IMPLEMENTATION QUESTIONs concern what a claim or evidence reference must carry, or when. A failed 13:47 reconstruction would convert those open questions into a demonstrated failure (licensing IMPLEMENT); a successful one would collapse most of them to DO NOT IMPLEMENT. It is named the fifth specified-and-unrun instrument in the corpus (alongside Tarka, the decidability test, the representability test, and the 18-case suite), and the only one of the five whose actual result would change verdicts in this register directly. Recorded as the primary input to the eventual synthesis; not itself run by this review.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Counting-as differs from the other three in **who confers**: not the context, but **collective acceptance**. That makes it an **authority** claim wearing a context label
a_rows_sample.statement: Searle's institutional counting-as (institutions determine what something counts as) is recorded as a fourth, distinct position on context, alongside: context may constitute knowledge (S1-F022), identity is relational to context (S1-F031 axis 2), and context is a constitutive prerequisite (<Z-1>) -- confirmed as distinct and unreconciled with the other three, not routed to adjudication. This review adds that counting-as differs from the other three in who confers status: not the context itself, but collective acceptance -- making it an authority claim wearing a context label, and bearing directly on the S2-R-F001 authority-temporal cluster, since institutionally-conferred status has a validity period by construction. Separately, a genuine three-way, unresolved tension is noted between Brandom (permits divergence in commitment across projections), S1-F038 (forbids divergence in content across projections), and S1-F037 (participants transform, not merely view, the space) -- Brandom's weaker constraint relaxes the F037/F038 tension while creating a new one with F038 itself, recorded at S2-R-F038.5.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **Five of the six are about what an evidence or claim reference must carry, or when.** That is a single cluster, not six separate questions
a_rows_sample.statement: The six IMPLEMENTATION QUESTION verdicts across the register are: S2-R-F001 (authority-over-time), S2-R-F024 (source-type retention), S2-R-F029 (evidence roles), S2-R-F033 (context sufficiency), S2-R-F036 (six temporal roles), plus an S2-F024 event-completeness candidate at NEEDS EVIDENCE. Five of the six concern what an evidence or claim reference must carry, or when -- named a single cluster rather than six separate questions, and four of them are said to turn on the same unresolved semantic question: what EvidenceLinks' 'acquisition method' and 'reliability conditions', and ContextTuple's 'delimiting conditions', actually denote.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **Not one finding in 40 artifacts would change the Kernel's extent.** Zero A-class results. ... `IMPLEMENT = 0`, and that is not a NO-GO. ... The decisive experiment exists, is cheap, and has never been run
a_rows_sample.statement: The review's four headline takeaways: (1) not one of 40 reviewed findings would change the Kernel's extent -- zero A-class results, every surviving gap is a contents or surrounding-architecture question; (2) IMPLEMENT=0 is not a NO-GO, since most surfaced gaps are already protected by existing law and the six live questions are gated on facts this review session cannot reach; (3) a decisive, cheap experiment exists and has never been run -- 'what did we know at 13:47?' (S1-F038), which would resolve five of six open questions in one direction or the other; (4) the research base is known materially incomplete by Session 1's own measurement -- approximately 3-5% of the corpus was actually read, and the single deepest read available recovered ten previously-missed findings.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **The strongest of them is authority-over-time**, and it is the only one where the loss under non-implementation is **irreversible** ... **Three independent routes reach this hole**
a_rows_sample.statement: The register's six IMPLEMENTATION QUESTIONs form one cluster, five concerning what a claim or evidence reference must carry or when: authority validity over time (does the Authority context hold grant validity intervals?); evidence roles/construction-vs-validation (does 'reliability conditions' already encode role?); source-type retention (does 'acquisition method' denote epistemic kind?); context sufficiency (does 'delimiting conditions' carry sufficiency or only delimitation?); six temporal roles (do surrounding contexts hold the roles v1.1 does not name?); and event-completeness of admission (is an unrecorded <Z-1> refusal admissible?) -- four of the first five turn on the same kind of question, what existing law phrases actually denote, a semantic question no grep can settle. Authority-over-time is named the strongest of the six and the only one where the loss under non-implementation is irreversible: after any revocation, every past admission by that authority becomes permanently ambiguous because the interval was never captured. Its duplicate-control check cleared (Authority is a bare Reference; TemporalValidity attaches to the claim; INV-KOS-AUTHORITY-001 has no temporal clause; 'revok*' has zero occurrences in v1.1), and three independent routes converge on this one hole: S1-F001 measured it, S1-F034 supplied the sufficiency criterion, and S1-F036 supplied its shape (validity is one of six temporal roles that must not collapse).

a_rows_sample.anchor: **Action 1 — run the 13:47 reconstruction test.** ... **Action 2 — answer the four denotation questions** ... **Not NO-GO** ... **Not GO** ... **Not CONDITIONAL GO**
a_rows_sample.statement: Final recommendation: DEFER, bounded, with two named decisive actions rather than open-ended further research. Action 1: run the 13:47 reconstruction test against a real situated commitment -- it is the corpus's own test, checkable, needs no new architecture; if it fails, the cluster of six converts from open questions into a demonstrated capability gap (the one thing that would license IMPLEMENT); if it passes, most of the cluster collapses to DO NOT IMPLEMENT; either outcome resolves five of six open questions, and no other available action has that yield. Action 2: answer four denotation questions (what do 'acquisition method', 'reliability conditions', and 'delimiting conditions' denote in law, and does the Authority context hold grant validity intervals) by asking whoever owns the relevant port contract and Authority context -- explicitly framed as lookups, not research. Three alternative recommendations are explicitly rejected with reasons: not NO-GO (would over-claim on a 3-5%-read base with 38 of 39 K3/K4 documents still unread at depth and the one completed deep read having recovered ten findings); not GO (there is no demonstrated capability gap, only questions -- converting an unanswered question into a requirement is exactly the failure mode this whole review has been catching); not CONDITIONAL GO (presupposes a thing to build conditionally, but until Action 1 runs there is no candidate whose necessity is established).

a_rows_sample.anchor: **✅ SESSION 2 COMPLETE — 41 / 41 reviewed, synthesis delivered.** **Recommendation: DEFER**, bounded by two named actions. ... **Final synthesis** `S2-FINAL-KERNEL-REVIEW.md` is written only after all 41 are reviewed. Writing it earlier would be the premature adjudication this session exists to prevent.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms Session 2 complete at 41/41 items reviewed (40 Session-1 findings plus the coverage report), with the final synthesis delivered and its recommendation (DEFER, bounded by two named actions) recorded as a recommendation only -- no adjudication performed. States the standing sequencing rule that governed the whole process: the final synthesis document is written only after all 41 items are reviewed, since writing it earlier would itself be the premature adjudication this two-session review design exists to prevent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: "The current language is not yet completely stabilized. **This is itself an architectural finding.**"
b_rows_sample.statement: The project's own 2026-08-21 architecture document tabulates 20 terms with recorded ambiguity (e.g. Knowledge: 'broad, current representation boundaries unclear'; Authority: 'current mechanism records it rather than creating it'; Human Act: 'current mechanism cannot create it'; Artifact: 'broad, not equivalent to knowledge'), and separately finds 'Rule' used for seven materially different concepts (engineering standards, rulings, architecture principles, recommendation heuristics, quality-gate rules, document-validation rules, permission rules), concluding this is a DDD vocabulary problem, not a naming problem, and prescribing 'preserve these distinctions rather than prematurely normalizing them.' This method rule anticipated, four days early, the vocabulary collisions this reconstruction programme later found independently (projection in three senses, agent in two, UNKNOWN at two altitudes).

b_rows_sample.anchor: the mechanism **records** authority rather than **creating** it ... cannot **create** a Human Act ... **Three independent arrivals** at: *the system can record, not manufacture.*
b_rows_sample.statement: Two entries bear directly on authority: the mechanism records authority rather than creating it, and cannot create a Human Act — the same limit as KCON-018 ('no authority manufacture') and KCON-013 (recorded difference ≠ actual independence), reached independently — three independent arrivals at 'the system can record, not manufacture.' Also: 'Artifact not equivalent to knowledge' is an early statement of representation≠knowledge, consistent with formal law's Representation≠Identity/Expression≠Meaning (§15).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The current authority record is strong in provenance but weak in temporal semantics.
b_rows_sample.statement: Measured over 20 observed authority grants: grants with human-act reference 20/20, registeredBy=governance 20/20, grants with immutable commit addressing 13/20, using descriptive artifact references 7/20 — but grants with validity information 0/20, delegation information 0/20, ownership information 0/20. Consequence, in the source's own words: the system 'can establish that authority was registered against a human act, but cannot reliably answer: was this authority valid at a particular historical point in time' — explicitly 'a current-state limitation, not a future-architecture opinion.' By the project's own evidence hierarchy (20260801-1231 §3) this is implementation/persistence-derived evidence (priority 1-3), the strongest evidence class encountered in the corpus so far.

b_rows_sample.anchor: can the system reconstruct the validity of an authority at a past instant?" — currently, no, at 0/20.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the corpus's temporal question, previously philosophical (knowledge-at-a-time, projection, evolving Knowledge Space, all Phase 2 hypothesis), into a narrower measured one: 'can the system reconstruct the validity of an authority at a past instant?' — currently no, at 0/20. Sharpens KCON-017 (record existence ≠ authority establishment, same day 20260821-2032): registration is recorded, but validity over time is not — independently arrived at. Classifies against formal law: W:C-18 (constitutional-version binding is precisely a temporal validity claim, currently lacking); W:C-3 (authority adequacy at which time is undefined); W:C-15 (retraction/withdrawal, same family — what the record says later); v1.1 comparison: NOT ADDRESSED, since v1.1 does not speak to authority validity intervals.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If the grant record has no field in which validity could be expressed, then `0/20` is not twenty observations. It is a single structural fact — the schema cannot represent validity — encountered twenty times.
b_rows_sample.statement: S1-F001's '0/20' validity-information figure reads as a measured empirical rate, inviting 'would a larger sample find some?' — but since the grant record schema has no field capable of expressing validity, 0/20 is one structural fact (schema cannot represent validity) encountered twenty times, not twenty independent observations. Evidence: three independent properties (validity, delegation, ownership) all land at exactly zero across twenty records — the signature of representational absence, not measurement — while properties that ARE representable vary normally (human-act reference 20/20, immutable commit addressing 13/20, descriptive references 7/20); the variation pattern itself distinguishes the two kinds of zero. Connects to the Zero lens: 'absence of the means of expression' is a different thing from 'absence of a value', and S1-F001's original framing conflates them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: These are three different temporal questions with three different subjects. Grouping them invites a single answer to what needs three.
b_rows_sample.statement: S1-F001 groups W:C-18 (version binding), W:C-3 (authority adequacy), and W:C-15 (retraction) as one family on the ground that all concern 'what the record says later' — but these are three different questions with three different subjects: was the authority valid at T (the grant's own validity interval); was the claim valid at T (TemporalValidity, already modelled); does the claimant still assert it (the agent's stance, neither of the above). Evidence the three vary independently: a claim may remain within valid-from/valid-until, admitted under a never-lapsed authority, and still be withdrawn by its asserter; conversely an authority may lapse while the claimant's stance is unchanged — the standard test for one-concept-vs-three.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The corpus's own recorded method rule — quoted in `S1-F002` — is "**preserve these distinctions rather than prematurely normalizing them**"... **S1-F001 groups where S1-F002 warns against grouping.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Flags that S1-F001 (S0588) and S1-F002 (S0587) — the same source document, the same day — are in tension on method: S1-F002 records the rule 'preserve distinctions rather than prematurely normalizing them' and names over-grouping a DDD vocabulary problem, yet S1-F001 groups three independently-varying temporal questions into one family, violating the rule its sibling finding just recorded. Recommends recording the 'family' as three adjacent questions sharing a lens, not one family sharing an answer. Explicitly does not overwrite Session 1's grouping — records the challenge as OPEN.

b_rows_sample.anchor: v1.1 *does* carry temporal validity — for the **claim**... So the model provides a validity interval for **what is asserted**, and none for **the authority under which it was asserted**.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects S1-F001's classification of the v1.1 comparison as 'NOT ADDRESSED — v1.1 does not speak to authority validity intervals': that is right about authority but misses the asymmetry. v1.1's TemporalValidity (valid-from/valid-until/superseded-by, Article 11, 'freshness never truth, expiry never absence') is an aggregate member giving the CLAIM an explicit validity interval, while Authority is merely a reference ('a recorded reference to a human act; held by the Authority context, referenced by the aggregate') carrying no interval — 'A claim can be asked were you valid at T? The authority that admitted it cannot.' S1-F001's measured 0/20 baseline exhibits the same asymmetry the target model itself has.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The gap is therefore **not a baseline defect that the target model fixes**. It is present in both, which changes its status: from "the current system is behind" to "neither the current system nor the target model time-indexes authority."
b_rows_sample.statement: Reclassifies the finding from NOT ADDRESSED to 'ADDRESSED FOR THE CLAIM, NOT FOR THE AUTHORITY': the temporal-validity gap is not a baseline defect the target model fixes but a property present in both — the question is not whether the model CAN express intervals (it demonstrably can, for claims) but why the concept is applied to one side of an admission (the claim) and not the other (the authority). Explicit governance boundary: 'This finding must not be routed into the active adjudication. The corpus is sealed for that purpose; this is a review record' — research relevance only, no element proposed, Session 1's document not modified.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **`Knowledge`** — *"Broad; current representation boundaries unclear"*
b_rows_sample.statement: S1-F002's table records, as its first row, that 'Knowledge' itself has 'unclear representation boundaries', with two adjacent rows compounding it (Observation: relationship to evidence/knowledge not fully formalized; Artifact: broad, not equivalent to knowledge) — meaning the baseline cannot cleanly bound Knowledge against evidence, observation, or artifact. S1-F002 draws out only the Artifact≠Knowledge row and does not connect it back to the Knowledge row it qualifies.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A project whose central term is recorded by its own baseline as having unclear representation boundaries has stated something more consequential than that `Rule` is overloaded.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reading the table with the Knowledge row foregrounded changes what the table is: from evidence of vocabulary instability (a method finding) to evidence about the subject matter itself — the baseline could not say where knowledge ends and evidence, observation, or artifact begin. This also supplies the strongest available support for S1-F002's own 'preserve, do not prematurely normalize' method rule, since the term at stake (Knowledge) is more consequential than the term S1-F002 argued from (Rule).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Only Evidence and Provenance survive both lists.
b_rows_sample.statement: Two Phase 1 Kernel member-list proposals 36 minutes apart (20:32 and 21:08, 2026-08-21): Document A — kernel as 'a deterministic runtime for governed knowledge state, authority, evidence, lifecycle and provenance' (members: authority mechanics, generic evidence mechanics, lifecycle, provenance); Document B — kernel as 'observation/evaluation mechanics with rules pushed out to a port' (members: Observation, Evidence, Rule evaluation protocol, Assessment, Result, Provenance). Only Evidence and Provenance appear in both; Authority and Lifecycle are in A only, Observation/Assessment/Result/Rule-evaluation are in B only. B is a self-declared revision of A after consulting an older baseline document, not an independent arrival. Caution recorded: the {Evidence, Provenance} intersection is a historical fact about two proposals, not a minimality result or a finding about the Kernel.

b_rows_sample.anchor: may be a particularly important kernel abstraction
b_rows_sample.statement: ChangeSet, from Document B, deliberately separates event detection from observation execution and is source-agnostic (does not care whether the change originated from VS Code, Claude Code, Git, or another tool) — an implemented mechanism, evidence priority 1-3 rather than 7. Explicit caution: 'implemented ≠ Kernel-authoritative' — implementation raises evidence class but confers no architectural standing; a mechanism can be real, useful, source-agnostic, and still belong outside the Kernel boundary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the kernel holds the port; EKS and PKS supply the rules
b_rows_sample.statement: Rule Port, from Document B: Kernel → Observation → Rule Port → {EKS engineering rules | PKS product rules}; concrete rules (LCOM4, test-presence, architecture, DDD) and the engineering-recommendation engine are explicitly kept outside the kernel. Classified as CONSISTENT with v1.1's later Verification Port and its mechanism-altitude separation (§16), reached independently one day earlier; recorded as a convergence to accumulate, not a ruling.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What is the actual relationship between the existing EKS runtime, the existing AI Engineering Platform, PKS, and the proposed KnowledgeOS kernel?
b_rows_sample.statement: Document B corrects the framing question from 'what parts of EKS can we move into the KnowledgeOS kernel?' to 'what is the actual relationship between the existing EKS runtime, AIP, PKS, and the proposed kernel?', on the ground that multiple architectural mechanisms already look like kernel primitives; also states '.claude definitely should not become the kernel' and 'the correct next phase is therefore NOT EP-01.' The reviewer notes the corpus was already resisting deriving the Kernel by relocating existing code rather than by identifying what must be protected.

b_rows_sample.anchor: No mature research field appears to define a universally accepted: `knowledge kernel` · `epistemic kernel` · `organizational memory kernel`.
b_rows_sample.statement: An independent external-research review (20260821-2351, self-declared P2 external evidence base, not a KnowledgeOS architecture proposal) finds the term 'knowledge kernel' exists mostly as metaphor, prototype vocabulary, or isolated conceptual work, and concludes KnowledgeOS is 'not entering an established category.' Consequence: every Kernel property must be justified internally, since there is no external field to appeal to for validation, and nothing established to converge on.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Weak Analogy Areas" because "Knowledge systems lack: deterministic execution
b_rows_sample.statement: Material contradiction (candidate): Position A (20260821-2032, P1, 20:32) claims the kernel is 'closer to: a deterministic runtime for governed knowledge state, authority, evidence, lifecycle and provenance'; Position B (20260821-2351, P2, 23:51, same evening, 3h19m later) rates the Unix/Linux analogy as weak because 'knowledge systems lack: deterministic execution, strict process isolation, universal semantics.' A possible reconciliation (governance-determinism vs. execution-determinism) is explicitly NOT accepted since neither document draws the distinction; v1.1's silence on determinism leaves workbook item W:C-2 (determinism: property, test, or DEF-1?) open and unruled.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Research suggests the trustworthy core of organizational knowledge is primarily about preserving epistemic accountability over time, not retrieval performance.
b_rows_sample.statement: The external review explicitly excludes RAG, ontologies, workflow engines, analytics, visualization, and event sourcing from the trustworthy core, and rates knowledge graphs as Strong for integration/query/semantic model but Weak as Kernel and Mixed as persistence ('no evidence supports Knowledge System = Knowledge Graph'). Framed as a third independent arrival (with S1-F001's 0/20 authority-validity measurement and the Phase 2 temporal thread) at 'over time' as the load-bearing dimension, and as largely agreeing with two other independent rejection sets (KCON-016; v1.1 §17).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The artifact in hand is not the persistence record. It is a Phase-1 narrative document, located in `brainstorming/`, that *describes* measurements over persistence records.
b_rows_sample.statement: S1-F001 assigns its source the strongest evidence class in the corpus ('implementation/persistence-derived evidence — priority 1-3, not priority-7 brainstorming'), but the cited document (brainstorming/20260821-2033-what-eks-is-today.md) is a brainstorming-corpus narrative describing measurements, not the persistence record itself, and no grant identifier, record path, or query is quoted — the measurement is asserted, not exhibited. Proposed remedy: record as 'secondary report of persistence-derived measurement', mark underlying grants verifiable-on-request rather than verified.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is an **implemented** mechanism, not a proposal — evidence priority 1–3, not 7.
b_rows_sample.statement: The same one-band evidence-class elevation recurs in S1-F003's ChangeSet claim ('an implemented mechanism, not a proposal') with no code path, module, test or commit cited; two instances from the same corpus location, both elevating, make this a pattern rather than a single slip — a systematic upward bias that is harder to detect than one misclassification since each instance looks locally reasonable. Explicitly does not doubt either substantive claim (S1-F001's 0/20 grants or S1-F003's ChangeSet), only their evidence-class labeling.

lineage_claims_a_to_b.quote: checkable, temporal, and aimed exactly at the gap `S1-F001` measured

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'S1-F001'

a_rows_sample.anchor: A set Gamma is stable iff [FOL-closed, K-introspective, negative-introspective] ... Theorem: Stable sets correspond exactly to basic belief sets. ... e\models O\alpha iff the basic belief set of e is a stable expansion of \{\alpha\}. ... the closed world assumption as only-knowing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Connects Only-Knowing to autoepistemic logic via stable sets (FOL-closed + positively/negatively K-introspective) and stable expansions, with a propositional computation algorithm (enumerate subwffs, test each truth-valuation for self-consistency); explicitly proposes the Closed-World Assumption itself can be understood as a case of only-knowing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: new facts can invalidate previous beliefs... Bird(Tweety) => Flies(Tweety) ... Emu(Tweety) causes the previous conclusion to be withdrawn
b_rows_sample.statement: Nonmonotonic reasoning (classical Tweety/Emu example) is established as a legitimate formal phenomenon relevant to the unresolved lifecycle/retirement/supersession TODO (distinguishing contradiction, revision, supersession, retirement, expiration): K_t |= p does not imply K_{t+1} |= p after new information arrives, i.e. Entailment at t != Permanent validity. The book gives the phenomenon and formalisms (e.g. default logic) but not KnowledgeOS's own lifecycle semantics.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t^{I,\mathcal S}\models\alpha ... K_{t+1}^{I,\mathcal S'}\models\alpha ... Current\ derivability \neq permanent\ epistemic\ standing
b_rows_sample.statement: Not every reasoning regime is monotonic; defeasible/nonmonotonic reasoning (classical bird/emu withdrawal pattern) means K_t^{I,S} |= alpha does not establish K_{t+1}^{I,S'} |= alpha, i.e. current derivability != permanent epistemic standing — a formal research basis for revision, retraction and supersession, though it does not yet define the KnowledgeOS lifecycle relation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C(x):D(x) / E(x) ... Problem: Precedence of more specific defaults over more general ones must be handled ... Default reasoning provides the formal basis for: Defeasible inheritance, Nonmonotonic reasoning, Lifecycle/retirement semantics
b_rows_sample.statement: DL default rule (C(x):D(x) / E(x), i.e. if C(a) believed and D(a) consistent, conclude E(a)), with the specificity-precedence problem noted; claimed by the extraction to give KnowledgeOS a formal basis for defeasible inheritance, nonmonotonic reasoning, and lifecycle/retirement semantics.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What This Book Confirms: R_req=TBox, Sat(K_t,r)=Instance checking, Contradiction=Concept inconsistency detection, Boundary=Frame axioms, Taxonomy=Classification hierarchy, Specialized reasoning=Tableau/structural subsumption, Nonmonotonicity=Default reasoning extension, Uncertainty=Probabilistic/fuzzy extensions, Composition=Role/concept composition, delta=Successor state axioms
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidated 'what this book confirms' mapping table asserting the handbook validates a large set of unqualified KnowledgeOS identifications: R_req=TBox, Sat(K_t,r)=Instance checking, Contradiction=Concept inconsistency, Boundary=Frame axioms, Taxonomy=Classification hierarchy, Specialized reasoning=Tableau algorithms/structural subsumption, Incremental knowledge=ABox assertions, Explanation=Subsumption explanation, Nonmonotonicity=Default reasoning, Uncertainty=Probabilistic/fuzzy extensions, Composition=Role/concept composition, delta=Successor state axioms.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Nonmonotonic Reasoning (Brewka) / Nonmonotonic Logic (Marek & Truszczynski) ... KB\models p but KB\cup\{q\}\not\models p ... Default Logic: Bird(x)\Rightarrow Flies(x) ... Circumscription: Minimize abnormality ... Autoepistemic Logic ... K_t\models p\not\Rightarrow K_{t+1}\models p ... Lifecycle \supset Nonmonotonicity
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes nonmonotonic-reasoning texts (Brewka; Marek & Truszczynski) as fourth-priority reading, restating the nonmonotonicity principle K_t|=p not=>K_{t+1}|=p, and cataloguing default logic, circumscription, and autoepistemic logic as candidate mechanisms, giving Lifecycle ⊃ Nonmonotonicity.

b_notations: K_t |= p does not imply K_{t+1} |= p

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'autoepistemic-stable-expansion-formalism' POSSIBLY relates to 'nonmonotonicity-lifecycle-principle' (batch B0061). Note: Formal stable-set (closed under FOL consequence, K-introspective, negative-introspective) and stable-expansion definitions connecting Only-Knowing to autoepistemic logic (e|=O-alpha iff e's basic belief set is a stable expansion of {alpha}), with a propositional computation algorithm; proposed as the formal basis for computing 'only-known' content, nonmonotonic defaults, and CWA-as-only-knowing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the same process shaped both sides of the E2 ↔ D5 interface.
a_rows_sample.statement: INFO-2: the producing process of E2 also authored the D5 establishment-criteria proposal and the canonical C-10 analysis, meaning the same process shaped both sides of the E2↔D5 interface; recorded as non-blocking but as a residual for future acts to weigh.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Adopting a completeness model is not evidence of capability existence — under D5's own scheme a definition is Class C (future/architectural) evidence, which cannot establish existence by itself.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adopting a completeness/design model for a capability is explicitly distinguished from establishing that the capability exists; such adoption is Class C (future/architectural) evidence under the D5 scheme and cannot by itself establish existence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: L1 · PROTOTYPE ESTABLISHMENT ... L2 · OPERATIONAL ESTABLISHMENT ... L3 · AUTHORITATIVE ESTABLISHMENT
a_rows_sample.statement: A three-level assurance framework for capability establishment: L1 (one realized instance, a named milestone that does NOT flip existence), L2 (≥2 independent governed acts showing the outcome is owned rather than incidental — the level at which D2/existence flips), L3 (L2 plus exercised claim-authority plus a change history — the level at which the capability may carry authoritative claims).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Option A is rejected — and on evidence, not preference: the full conjunction includes E10, which requires a history that cannot exist at establishment time. Adopting it would make C-10 permanently unestablishable.
a_rows_sample.statement: The full-conjunction Option A for establishment criteria is rejected as structurally unsatisfiable, because it requires a criterion (E10, distinct reason to change / history) that by definition cannot exist at the moment of establishment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A summary must never silently replace the governing artifact.
a_rows_sample.statement: An appended PO/ARB act resolves a divergence between a proposal's decided §4.2 text and the adoption act's own restated summary of L3, ruling the proposal's text governs; states the general principle that a summary must never silently replace the governing artifact, and closes the divergence in the same shape as the earlier Flag-O resolution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Capability existence ≠ Capability authority ≠ Operational maturity
a_rows_sample.statement: Three distinct concepts are kept apart in the settled L1/L2/L3 model: capability existence, capability authority, and operational maturity; had L3 been read as maturity-only, the exercised-authority condition (E3) would have fallen out of the model entirely.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Four capabilities have NO OWNER: C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition. INFERRED: these four, not the six roles, are the substance of ADR-AIP-04.
b_rows_sample.statement: Headline finding: of a 20-capability inventory (C-1..C-20) derived from evidence of what the platform actually does, four capabilities (C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition) have no declared owner -- proposed as the real substance of ADR-AIP-04, in contrast to the six proposed roles.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EKS-01: the HANDOFF token's tokenRef acted as the de-facto knowledge channel and taught a lane the superseded path. A lane was taught the old path by its workflow record's tokenRef.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-5/F-5a: BC-7's HANDOFF tokenRef is performing de-facto knowledge distribution it does not own, evidenced by EKS-01 where a lane was taught a superseded path via its own workflow record's tokenRef -- the strongest evidence for a distinct C-10 (Knowledge Distribution) capability rather than 'Communication' in the ordinary sense.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Communication is two capabilities wearing one name. C-10 Knowledge Distribution -- a genuine, evidenced, unowned MECHANISM ... C-19 Communication Composition -- a STEWARDSHIP
b_rows_sample.statement: 'Communication' as commonly discussed is proposed to be two distinct capabilities: C-10 Knowledge Distribution (a genuine unowned mechanism, evidenced by EKS-01) and C-19 Communication Composition (a stewardship, failing the bounded-context test on language and reason-to-change); a single 'Communication Engineer' role would wrongly bind a mechanism gap and a reporting duty into one actor.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Distinguish, explicitly: ContextPublished, ContextSelected, ContextDelivered, ContextAvailable, ContextAcknowledged, ContextApplied, ContextVerified. Receipt is not proof of application or compliance.
b_rows_sample.statement: C-10's knowledge-distribution lifecycle is to be modelled as seven distinguished states (ContextPublished, ContextSelected, ContextDelivered, ContextAvailable, ContextAcknowledged, ContextApplied, ContextVerified); a receipt is never proof of application or compliance, only of a narrower claim.

type_signature.codomain: one of seven distinguished lifecycle states

b_rows_sample.anchor: that recurrence is itself evidence bearing on C-10 -- governed knowledge arriving outside the governed channel -- and the analysis may note it, but per AMD1 must not assume C-10 owns it.
b_rows_sample.statement: A pattern of substantive external input (a cited review, a 925-line brainstorming document, external research) repeatedly arriving outside the governed channel is recorded as evidence potentially bearing on C-10, but explicitly not assumed to be owned by C-10 without further decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-5: YES existence, control-plane function category. C-10: NOT YET ESTABLISHED, deferred category. C-14: CONTESTED, deferred. C-19: YES, stewardship/cross-cutting category. The forbidden collapse is absent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Independent verification confirms the existence/category split was applied without the forbidden collapse for all four capabilities: C-5 exists (control-plane function), C-10's existence is NOT YET ESTABLISHED (category deferred), C-14's existence is CONTESTED (category deferred), C-19 exists (stewardship/cross-cutting), each argued from positive properties rather than derived from the other axis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The four are not four candidate contexts. They are one CONTROL LOOP with four distinct capabilities in it. policy/knowledge DEFINED (BC-1) -> C-10 DELIVERS it to the gated session -> C-14 GATES the act -> C-19 EXPRESSES the outcome <- C-5 ATTESTS who acted
b_rows_sample.statement: Structural finding: C-5, C-10, C-14, C-19 are not four independent candidate bounded contexts but four capabilities within one control loop -- BC-1's policy/knowledge is delivered by C-10 to a gated session, C-14 gates the act, C-19 expresses the outcome, and C-5 attests who acted and how separately -- while still having four distinct reasons to change, so the relationship, not a merged boundary, is what explains them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-10 is NOT the whole path. Its smallest coherent boundary is APPLICABILITY + RECEIPT. ... What nothing owns is: (a) deciding WHICH governed knowledge is applicable to THIS assignment, and (b) evidencing that the executing session actually holds the CURRENT version.
b_rows_sample.statement: C-10's smallest coherent capability boundary is proposed to be applicability determination plus receipt (not the whole created->published->selected->retrieved->delivered->acknowledged->applied->verified path), since creation/publication is BC-1's, retrieval/bootstrap is BC-6's, and only applicability-determination and receipt-evidencing are genuinely unowned.

b_rows_sample.anchor: fails on 6 of 10 => a STEWARDSHIP / cross-cutting expression concern ... the only state that could make a Communication context real -- delivery-with-acknowledgement -- is C-10's receipt, not C-19's. building C-10 would REDUCE the case for a Communication context.
b_rows_sample.statement: C-19 fails a ten-part bounded-context test on six of ten criteria (own language, independent lifecycle, independent authority, authoritative state, distinct reason to change, audience/consent/channel concepts) and is classified a stewardship/cross-cutting expression concern; the one property that could give it authoritative state (delivery-with-acknowledgement) actually belongs to C-10, so realizing C-10 reduces rather than increases the case for a Communication bounded context.

b_rows_sample.anchor: two independent grounds: an ADOPTED invariant (INV-ATTR-2) that presupposes the capability, and the capability has been PERFORMED. C-10 satisfies neither limb.
b_rows_sample.statement: A two-limb existence test emerges from Amendment 1's C-5 analysis: a capability's existence is supported by (1) an ADOPTED invariant presupposing it, and/or (2) the capability having been PERFORMED at least once; C-5 satisfies both limbs (INV-ATTR-2 adopted; SB-1 clearance is a performed instance), while C-10 satisfies neither.

b_rows_sample.anchor: receipt <= application <= understanding <= compliance ... A receipt can only ever evidence ContextAcknowledged. ContextApplied and ContextVerified are different claims requiring different evidence, and no receipt can supply them.
b_rows_sample.statement: C-10's seven-state receipt model is elaborated with an explicit ceiling: a receipt can only ever evidence ContextAcknowledged, never ContextApplied or ContextVerified, and OQ-J is reformulated from a yes/no 'is the receipt authoritative' question into five separately-tested claims (delivery, possession, applicability, execution, compliance authority), of which a receipt can carry at most the first two.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Option C binds the receipt to an act the estate has never performed, that nobody owns, and that the analysis says a receipt cannot carry.
b_rows_sample.statement: Option C for C-10 receipt semantics is found unsatisfiable as worded, because it would require the receipt to reference an 'applicability decision' (ContextSelected) that never occurs and has no owner in the estate -- the same referent-gap defect noticed independently in several later documents.

b_rows_sample.anchor: establishes an applicability reference -- a pointer to decision A. does NOT establish the correctness of applicability -- whether A was right. A pointer to a judgement is not an assertion that the judgement was sound.
b_rows_sample.statement: C-10 Decision 1 (Option C) resolves OQ-J's authority defect by distinguishing an applicability REFERENCE (a pointer, which the receipt may carry) from applicability CORRECTNESS (whether the referenced judgement was sound, which the receipt does not establish) -- 'AUTHORITY IS CLAIM-SCOPED' is recorded as the invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The decision commits the receipt to reference an applicability decision that the estate never produces. ... This is no longer an authority problem -- it is an existence problem about the referent.
b_rows_sample.statement: A distinct 'referent gap' (as opposed to the already-solved authority gap) is identified: the decided receipt is required to reference an applicability decision (ContextSelected) that the estate never actually produces and nobody owns, so a conforming receipt is not presently populatable -- left as PO/ARB's to decide (optional/null reference, vs. a standing obligation to build ContextSelected).

b_rows_sample.anchor: No typed KnowledgeDeliveryReceipt structure is adopted -- and, verified: no such type exists anywhere in the estate
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit confirmation that no typed receipt data structure (e.g. KnowledgeDeliveryReceipt) exists anywhere in the estate's code or docs; schema design is deferred to Architecture and is not created by this semantic decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Recommended: YES -- C-10 exists as a capability, with realization NONE and its outer boundary OPEN. The load-bearing argument is D1 itself. ... A decision fixing the authoritative claim boundary of C-10's artifact presupposes a subject for that artifact.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance recommends C-10 existence = YES, arguing that D1's decided receipt-claim boundary presupposes a subject for that claim, supported by a distinct reason to change, a distinct outcome, and two genuinely unowned stages sharing one purpose (applicability + receipt) -- this recommendation is later overturned by the PO/ARB (S0120 D2) as conflating a decided semantic with a performed capability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Of five activities: one occurs and is owned elsewhere; four do not occur at all. Evidence of C-10 having occurred: none
b_rows_sample.statement: Applying the ten-question existence test to the estate's evidence: of C-10's five constituent activities (applicability, delivery, acknowledgement, claim-scoped receipt, invalidation/reconciliation), only one occurs and it is owned by other contexts (BC-6/BC-7), while four never occur at all and have no owner -- the counter-evidence supporting the later NOT YET ESTABLISHED verdict.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The platform cannot attest a specified session execution. identity binding must NOT be placed inside C-10's authoritative state, because C-10 cannot establish it. It is C-5-shaped
b_rows_sample.statement: The sharpest finding in the D3 prep: a C-10 receipt's binding to a specific session execution can never be stronger than what INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2 permit (self-declared, not attested), so identity binding cannot be placed inside C-10's authoritative state -- it is C-5-shaped, and C-5 owns no attestation record either.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Adopting the receipt as authoritative state would supply limb one of the estate's existence test. A decision framed as constitutive would decide existence by the back door -- which this act forbids. Framed as a boundary specification, it does not.
b_rows_sample.statement: A distinction between a 'constitutive' decision (which would establish existence as a side effect) and a 'boundary specification' decision (which defines a candidate scope without establishing existence) is drawn, warning that D3 must be framed as the latter to avoid silently satisfying the D2 existence test.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C -- SPLIT. Fits every decided constraint. It matches OQ-J's 2-of-5 result ... applicability / transport / execution are already owned or already excluded
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommendation: Option C (SPLIT) for D3 -- C-10 would own only the receipt/attestation lifecycle and state (receipt identity, lifecycle state, invalidation, completeness), explicitly excluding applicability determination, delivery transport, session execution, identity binding, dispute adjudication, execution authority, and compliance/application.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'c10-d5-establishment-criteria' POSSIBLY relates to 'capability-c10-knowledge-distribution' (batch B0004). Note: The adopted E1-E10 criteria and three-level assurance-establishment framework (L1 PROTOTYPE, L2 OPERATIONAL, L3 AUTHORITATIVE) for determining when C-10 may be considered established (S0127).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Both prior positions were partly right and stated the wrong conclusion. ... The correct classification is SOURCE ESTABLISHES / CORPUS ESTABLISHES x NOT ADOPTED -- a governance gap, not a mathematical one.
a_rows_sample.statement: All three capabilities (uncertainty, non-identifiability, missingness) are present as raw-corpus (Stratum 1) formal constructions but measured absent (0 grep occurrences) from the authorized canonical-architecture-v0.2 model; the corpus's own governance ruled the Abhava material 'Enrichment, NOT a row' and closed a related process point (P4), meaning the constructions exist but were deliberately not promoted -- reframing the gap as governance non-adoption rather than a mathematical inexpressibility.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The three exclusions were a discovery failure, not a mathematical limit. They are absent from the AUTHORIZED MODEL v0.2 ... so the finding is real, and it is a GOVERNANCE finding: the constructions exist and were never promoted.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a prior verdict ('THEORY CLOSED AGAINST THE STATED CRITERIA -- NOT COMPLETE IN EVERY RESPECT', with 'a theory that cannot say nobody ever asked is closed, not finished') by showing the corpus does say 'nobody ever asked' (the not-assessed Zero-lens dimension state, committed one day before this programme began) and does have formal, typed constructions for non-identifiability and uncertainty; reclassifies the three exclusions as a discovery failure rather than a mathematical limit, and as a governance finding since these constructions are measured absent (zero grep occurrences of unknown/absent/not assessed/uncertain/identifiab) from the authorized v0.2 model despite existing in the raw corpus.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do the three capability constructions ... enter the architecture, or do they stay research? ... an authority has already ruled the other way, and the ruling is still in force. ... Assessment -> verdict -> NEVER grants authority -- this verification cannot make that decision, and saying so is the rule working, not a hedge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses the programme's single genuinely normative, non-derivable question to a human authority (PO/ARB): whether (W,Omega)/identifiability, the Zero dimension-state taxonomy, and U(H) should enter the architecture or remain research, explicitly declining to answer it itself because a standing governance ruling (Abhava material ruled 'Enrichment, NOT a row', P4 CLOSED, DeepSeek NOT INCORPORATED) already went the other way and the operating discipline (Assessment -> verdict -> NEVER grants authority) forbids the verification from overriding it; offers four options (A adopt all three / B adopt only D_t / C adopt none, reclassify as unadopted not inexpressible / D commission a separate evidence pass) with a recommendation of D-then-B, explicitly distinguishing this from the TG-01/02/06/09 engineering repairs which are stated to have derivable answers requiring no human decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 132/132 is evidence that the field is always filled. It is not evidence that authority is bound. ... This is IMPLEMENTATION-ONLY, and specifically a tautology -- not a proof of Sigma perp Gamma.
b_rows_sample.statement: Re-measuring humanActRef across the whole estate (22 work items, 132 grants, 269 transitions) confirms 132/132 non-empty, stronger than the prior audit's 20/20, but the field is free-text (83 prose, 49 with a document path) with no schema or verification, establishing a discipline not a binding; the estate already contains a failure case (ASD-001 hand-composed append; two distinct authority acts sharing one grantId).
