a_rows_sample.anchor: Four capabilities have NO OWNER: C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition. INFERRED: these four, not the six roles, are the substance of ADR-AIP-04.
a_rows_sample.statement: Headline finding: of a 20-capability inventory (C-1..C-20) derived from evidence of what the platform actually does, four capabilities (C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition) have no declared owner -- proposed as the real substance of ADR-AIP-04, in contrast to the six proposed roles.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EKS-01: the HANDOFF token's tokenRef acted as the de-facto knowledge channel and taught a lane the superseded path. A lane was taught the old path by its workflow record's tokenRef.
a_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-5/F-5a: BC-7's HANDOFF tokenRef is performing de-facto knowledge distribution it does not own, evidenced by EKS-01 where a lane was taught a superseded path via its own workflow record's tokenRef -- the strongest evidence for a distinct C-10 (Knowledge Distribution) capability rather than 'Communication' in the ordinary sense.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Communication is two capabilities wearing one name. C-10 Knowledge Distribution -- a genuine, evidenced, unowned MECHANISM ... C-19 Communication Composition -- a STEWARDSHIP
a_rows_sample.statement: 'Communication' as commonly discussed is proposed to be two distinct capabilities: C-10 Knowledge Distribution (a genuine unowned mechanism, evidenced by EKS-01) and C-19 Communication Composition (a stewardship, failing the bounded-context test on language and reason-to-change); a single 'Communication Engineer' role would wrongly bind a mechanism gap and a reporting duty into one actor.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Distinguish, explicitly: ContextPublished, ContextSelected, ContextDelivered, ContextAvailable, ContextAcknowledged, ContextApplied, ContextVerified. Receipt is not proof of application or compliance.
a_rows_sample.statement: C-10's knowledge-distribution lifecycle is to be modelled as seven distinguished states (ContextPublished, ContextSelected, ContextDelivered, ContextAvailable, ContextAcknowledged, ContextApplied, ContextVerified); a receipt is never proof of application or compliance, only of a narrower claim.

type_signature.codomain: one of seven distinguished lifecycle states

a_rows_sample.anchor: that recurrence is itself evidence bearing on C-10 -- governed knowledge arriving outside the governed channel -- and the analysis may note it, but per AMD1 must not assume C-10 owns it.
a_rows_sample.statement: A pattern of substantive external input (a cited review, a 925-line brainstorming document, external research) repeatedly arriving outside the governed channel is recorded as evidence potentially bearing on C-10, but explicitly not assumed to be owned by C-10 without further decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C-5: YES existence, control-plane function category. C-10: NOT YET ESTABLISHED, deferred category. C-14: CONTESTED, deferred. C-19: YES, stewardship/cross-cutting category. The forbidden collapse is absent.
a_rows_sample.statement: Independent verification confirms the existence/category split was applied without the forbidden collapse for all four capabilities: C-5 exists (control-plane function), C-10's existence is NOT YET ESTABLISHED (category deferred), C-14's existence is CONTESTED (category deferred), C-19 exists (stewardship/cross-cutting), each argued from positive properties rather than derived from the other axis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The four are not four candidate contexts. They are one CONTROL LOOP with four distinct capabilities in it. policy/knowledge DEFINED (BC-1) -> C-10 DELIVERS it to the gated session -> C-14 GATES the act -> C-19 EXPRESSES the outcome <- C-5 ATTESTS who acted
a_rows_sample.statement: Structural finding: C-5, C-10, C-14, C-19 are not four independent candidate bounded contexts but four capabilities within one control loop -- BC-1's policy/knowledge is delivered by C-10 to a gated session, C-14 gates the act, C-19 expresses the outcome, and C-5 attests who acted and how separately -- while still having four distinct reasons to change, so the relationship, not a merged boundary, is what explains them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C-10 is NOT the whole path. Its smallest coherent boundary is APPLICABILITY + RECEIPT. ... What nothing owns is: (a) deciding WHICH governed knowledge is applicable to THIS assignment, and (b) evidencing that the executing session actually holds the CURRENT version.
a_rows_sample.statement: C-10's smallest coherent capability boundary is proposed to be applicability determination plus receipt (not the whole created->published->selected->retrieved->delivered->acknowledged->applied->verified path), since creation/publication is BC-1's, retrieval/bootstrap is BC-6's, and only applicability-determination and receipt-evidencing are genuinely unowned.

a_rows_sample.anchor: fails on 6 of 10 => a STEWARDSHIP / cross-cutting expression concern ... the only state that could make a Communication context real -- delivery-with-acknowledgement -- is C-10's receipt, not C-19's. building C-10 would REDUCE the case for a Communication context.
a_rows_sample.statement: C-19 fails a ten-part bounded-context test on six of ten criteria (own language, independent lifecycle, independent authority, authoritative state, distinct reason to change, audience/consent/channel concepts) and is classified a stewardship/cross-cutting expression concern; the one property that could give it authoritative state (delivery-with-acknowledgement) actually belongs to C-10, so realizing C-10 reduces rather than increases the case for a Communication bounded context.

a_rows_sample.anchor: two independent grounds: an ADOPTED invariant (INV-ATTR-2) that presupposes the capability, and the capability has been PERFORMED. C-10 satisfies neither limb.
a_rows_sample.statement: A two-limb existence test emerges from Amendment 1's C-5 analysis: a capability's existence is supported by (1) an ADOPTED invariant presupposing it, and/or (2) the capability having been PERFORMED at least once; C-5 satisfies both limbs (INV-ATTR-2 adopted; SB-1 clearance is a performed instance), while C-10 satisfies neither.

a_rows_sample.anchor: receipt <= application <= understanding <= compliance ... A receipt can only ever evidence ContextAcknowledged. ContextApplied and ContextVerified are different claims requiring different evidence, and no receipt can supply them.
a_rows_sample.statement: C-10's seven-state receipt model is elaborated with an explicit ceiling: a receipt can only ever evidence ContextAcknowledged, never ContextApplied or ContextVerified, and OQ-J is reformulated from a yes/no 'is the receipt authoritative' question into five separately-tested claims (delivery, possession, applicability, execution, compliance authority), of which a receipt can carry at most the first two.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Option C binds the receipt to an act the estate has never performed, that nobody owns, and that the analysis says a receipt cannot carry.
a_rows_sample.statement: Option C for C-10 receipt semantics is found unsatisfiable as worded, because it would require the receipt to reference an 'applicability decision' (ContextSelected) that never occurs and has no owner in the estate -- the same referent-gap defect noticed independently in several later documents.

a_rows_sample.anchor: establishes an applicability reference -- a pointer to decision A. does NOT establish the correctness of applicability -- whether A was right. A pointer to a judgement is not an assertion that the judgement was sound.
a_rows_sample.statement: C-10 Decision 1 (Option C) resolves OQ-J's authority defect by distinguishing an applicability REFERENCE (a pointer, which the receipt may carry) from applicability CORRECTNESS (whether the referenced judgement was sound, which the receipt does not establish) -- 'AUTHORITY IS CLAIM-SCOPED' is recorded as the invariant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The decision commits the receipt to reference an applicability decision that the estate never produces. ... This is no longer an authority problem -- it is an existence problem about the referent.
a_rows_sample.statement: A distinct 'referent gap' (as opposed to the already-solved authority gap) is identified: the decided receipt is required to reference an applicability decision (ContextSelected) that the estate never actually produces and nobody owns, so a conforming receipt is not presently populatable -- left as PO/ARB's to decide (optional/null reference, vs. a standing obligation to build ContextSelected).

a_rows_sample.anchor: No typed KnowledgeDeliveryReceipt structure is adopted -- and, verified: no such type exists anywhere in the estate
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit confirmation that no typed receipt data structure (e.g. KnowledgeDeliveryReceipt) exists anywhere in the estate's code or docs; schema design is deferred to Architecture and is not created by this semantic decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Recommended: YES -- C-10 exists as a capability, with realization NONE and its outer boundary OPEN. The load-bearing argument is D1 itself. ... A decision fixing the authoritative claim boundary of C-10's artifact presupposes a subject for that artifact.
a_rows_sample.statement: Governance recommends C-10 existence = YES, arguing that D1's decided receipt-claim boundary presupposes a subject for that claim, supported by a distinct reason to change, a distinct outcome, and two genuinely unowned stages sharing one purpose (applicability + receipt) -- this recommendation is later overturned by the PO/ARB (S0120 D2) as conflating a decided semantic with a performed capability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Of five activities: one occurs and is owned elsewhere; four do not occur at all. Evidence of C-10 having occurred: none
a_rows_sample.statement: Applying the ten-question existence test to the estate's evidence: of C-10's five constituent activities (applicability, delivery, acknowledgement, claim-scoped receipt, invalidation/reconciliation), only one occurs and it is owned by other contexts (BC-6/BC-7), while four never occur at all and have no owner -- the counter-evidence supporting the later NOT YET ESTABLISHED verdict.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The platform cannot attest a specified session execution. identity binding must NOT be placed inside C-10's authoritative state, because C-10 cannot establish it. It is C-5-shaped
a_rows_sample.statement: The sharpest finding in the D3 prep: a C-10 receipt's binding to a specific session execution can never be stronger than what INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2 permit (self-declared, not attested), so identity binding cannot be placed inside C-10's authoritative state -- it is C-5-shaped, and C-5 owns no attestation record either.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Adopting the receipt as authoritative state would supply limb one of the estate's existence test. A decision framed as constitutive would decide existence by the back door -- which this act forbids. Framed as a boundary specification, it does not.
a_rows_sample.statement: A distinction between a 'constitutive' decision (which would establish existence as a side effect) and a 'boundary specification' decision (which defines a candidate scope without establishing existence) is drawn, warning that D3 must be framed as the latter to avoid silently satisfying the D2 existence test.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C -- SPLIT. Fits every decided constraint. It matches OQ-J's 2-of-5 result ... applicability / transport / execution are already owned or already excluded
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommendation: Option C (SPLIT) for D3 -- C-10 would own only the receipt/attestation lifecycle and state (receipt identity, lifecycle state, invalidation, completeness), explicitly excluding applicability determination, delivery transport, session execution, identity binding, dispute adjudication, execution authority, and compliance/application.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The platform cannot attest a specified session execution. identity binding must NOT be placed inside C-10's authoritative state, because C-10 cannot establish it. It is C-5-shaped
b_rows_sample.statement: The sharpest finding in the D3 prep: a C-10 receipt's binding to a specific session execution can never be stronger than what INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2 permit (self-declared, not attested), so identity binding cannot be placed inside C-10's authoritative state -- it is C-5-shaped, and C-5 owns no attestation record either.

b_rows_sample.anchor: M4 must be classified NOT ATTESTED -- never MISSING. ... Calling it MISSING asserts "no receipt", which the evidence does not support. Calling it present asserts a binding the platform cannot make.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extension of the NOT-ATTESTED-never-PASS discipline to condition classification: a receipt that exists but cannot be bound to its executing session (M4) must be classified NOT ATTESTED, since calling it MISSING or VALID would each assert something the platform cannot establish.

b_rows_sample.anchor: two residues no selection resolves ... knowledge versions K ... all three new propositions are silent on it ... S is unattestable. INV-ATTR-1 -- no gate reads identity ... E2 must mark the session-execution reference RECORDED, NOT ATTESTED.
b_rows_sample.statement: Two residues survive any D1 selection unresolved: whether 'knowledge versions K' remains a required receipt property (silently dropped by all three new propositions), and that the session-execution reference S must be marked RECORDED-NOT-ATTESTED per INV-ATTR-1/D4.3's M4 finding, both flagged for E2 (receipt completeness) to settle.

b_rows_sample.anchor: recording session identity != attesting session identity ... recording an applicability reference != attesting correctness of applicability
b_rows_sample.statement: D3 formalises two non-equivalences carrying the decision: recording session identity is not attesting session identity, and recording an applicability reference is not attesting the correctness of applicability -- the platform cannot attest 'a specified session execution' (INV-ATTR-1/2), so identity binding is placed outside C-10's boundary entirely.

b_rows_sample.anchor: One prohibition, three surfaces: an unresolved status may never be laundered into a resolved one.
b_rows_sample.statement: A single cross-cutting prohibition is observed recurring in three independent places in the estate's governance (independence classification, C-5 separation dimensions, D4.1 compensating controls, later a fourth at D4.3 M4): an unresolved epistemic status must never be laundered into a resolved one -- recorded as an observation bearing on, but distinct from, the canonical unifying-invariant candidate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: THE REVIEWER MUST BE A FRESH INDEPENDENT ARCHITECTURE PROCESS ... Satisfied on the measurement in §2.2: this is a process with no registered role in the chain.
b_rows_sample.statement: Demonstrates the independence-verification method in practice: enumerate every process occurrence across all transitions and grants in the aggregate plus a whole-repository grep, and treat zero occurrences as the only admissible basis for eligibility.

b_rows_sample.anchor: independence is not transferable: an assignment whose recorded evidence names a8ce5a39 cannot be discharged by 8a525719 without the record asserting something false about who did the work.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names a second-order independence failure distinct from personal ineligibility: a genuinely independent process cannot discharge a review under a workflow lane whose registered execution context names a different process, since INV-ATTR-1 means the engine itself would never detect the substitution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I will not adopt another process's identity in order to become operable.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a refusal principle: a process must not adopt a different, already-registered process's self-declared identity merely to satisfy a commission's addressee field and become operable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: you may self-bind identity; you may never self-choose role, scope, work item, or authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the governing invariant for the candidate-declaration mechanism: a process may discover and declare its own runtime identity, but may never self-select the role, scope, work item, or authority it is to hold -- those must come from the authoritative commission (AST-018 next-actor), with a MISMATCH between the prompt's claimed role and the commission's role forcing STOP (GO-08).

b_rows_sample.anchor: F-3 is disclosed as aggravating, not exculpatory: producing this record adds a further participating act by 77b85fa3 on this work item. If the PO/ARB's ruling turns on 'has this process already acted here,' this record is itself part of the evidence against it.
b_rows_sample.statement: A candidate for an independence-sensitive review role discloses that the very act of writing its own declaration record is itself a further participating act that could count against its own independence, explicitly refusing to treat its own record-production as exculpatory -- an instance of radical self-disclosure over self-serving interpretation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not decide for yourself that read-only orientation is or is not participation if the governing policy is ambiguous. Report the factual evidence. The candidate therefore returned UNDETERMINED and stopped, rather than self-certifying under reading B.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes a governance behavioral principle: when a governing policy is deliberately left as a placeholder and genuinely ambiguous, the correct response for a self-assessing process is to report factual evidence and return UNDETERMINED rather than adjudicate the ambiguity in its own favor, escalating the open question to the PO/ARB with named legitimate dispositions instead of a recommendation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: role != process identity, identity != eligibility, eligibility != appointment, appointment != activation, activation != authorization ... A process identity is DISCOVERED FROM THE RUNTIME -- never invented by the human, copied from another session, inferred from prompt text, or chosen from a human-entered UUID.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a six-link non-collapse chain of governance-identity concepts (role != process identity != eligibility != appointment != activation != authorization), each a genuinely separate step, and the rule that process identity is always discovered from the runtime, never supplied, copied, inferred, or human-chosen.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Basis: PROVENANCE ATTRIBUTION -- not self-declaration. The producer never declared this identity in any governed artifact. It is attributed here by a third party from runtime evidence. ... Every prior identity in this estate was declared by the process itself. This one is attributed by a third party from evidence the producer never confirmed. That is a new act type here.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces provenance-attributed identity as a genuinely new act type in this estate's governance model, distinct from the previously universal rule (INV-ATTR-1/2, G-2) that process identity is always self-declared and never attestable by others: here Governance attributes a producer identity to a third-party process from transcript timestamp/content evidence the producer itself never confirmed, bounded explicitly as barring-only (never enabling), evidentially grounded in operator-side transcripts outside the governed repository store, and remaining falsifiable/supersedable if contradicting evidence appears.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A previous candidate on the parent work item read the material first and declared afterwards. Its own reading then became prior participation ... Do not repeat that. Establish your identity FIRST. Check the bars FIRST. Read ONLY the authoritative state ... Declare. Then STOP.
b_rows_sample.statement: Institutionalizes a corrective procedural step ('declare before you orient') directly caused by the S0375 episode where a candidate's own pre-declaration reading became disqualifying prior participation with no policy able to resolve it; the fix reorders the candidate protocol (identity first, bars first, then only the minimal authoritative state, then declare and stop) without deciding the underlying open independence-policy question, which remains open.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The appointment names a ROLE, not a process. It deliberately contains no session identifier, and none was invented. Appointee identity: NOT DECLARED -- it comes from the runtime of the fresh session the PO/ARB starts.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reconfirms, in a concrete appointment act, that a governed appointment names only a role and never invents or pre-selects a process identity -- the appointee's identity is discovered later from the runtime of whichever fresh session the human actually starts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: process context continuity != workflow session identity continuity ... A Claude restart can produce a different CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID while retaining essentially the same working conversation and context. ... This is the temporal extension of INV-ATTR-1/2, not a new subject.
b_rows_sample.statement: States observation O-5: process context continuity is not the same as workflow session identity continuity -- a Claude restart can yield a new CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID while the same working context persists, so process identity is not only self-declared and unattestable (INV-ATTR-1/2) but also temporally unstable across restarts, and this instability is itself a temporal extension of INV-ATTR-1/2 rather than a separate subject.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Direction A -- false independence (the dangerous one; the one that actually materialised). ... Nothing malicious is required. A restart is enough. ... Direction B -- lost continuity (the tolerable one). ... The rule below deliberately errs toward Direction B. A wrongly-barred process needs one governed act to be re-established. A wrongly-admitted one cannot be repaired at all.
b_rows_sample.statement: Analyzes the O-5 instability as producing two asymmetric failure directions: (A) false independence -- a restarted process presenting a clean UUID could be wrongly admitted as independent while carrying the complete prior context of the very work it should be excluded from, destroying the independence guarantee retrospectively with a record that looks clean; (B) lost continuity -- a legitimately continuing process cannot prove it is the registered lane holder and must be re-established, a merely tolerable cost. States the governing principle that any remedy must err toward B, since a wrongly-barred process is one governed act away from repair while a wrongly-admitted one can never be repaired because its check was never actually independent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Independence must be declared and assessed on PRIOR PARTICIPATION, not on identity difference. A different UUID is necessary but not sufficient evidence of independence. ... A restarted process is a new candidate until Governance explicitly establishes its participation.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the corollary that carries the load: independence must be assessed on disclosed prior participation, never merely on identity difference, since a different UUID is necessary but not sufficient evidence of true independence; the resulting safe rule is that a restarted process is treated as a new candidate until Governance explicitly re-establishes its participation, explicitly rejecting as dangerous the alternative of treating UUIDs as durable, permanent identities.

b_rows_sample.anchor: That process authored ASD-001, scoped REPAIR-001, recorded the CONTINUATION (seq 5) and the grant G-REPAIR-001, and wrote the candidate-declaration prompt. Appointing it would collapse the separation between Governance analysis and Implementation ... The mechanism would not have caught this. AST-018 appoint might well have accepted e40f3fd0.
b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms O-5's abstract danger with a concrete live instance: the governance-recording process that scoped and authorized REPAIR-001 reappeared under a new runtime identifier (e40f3fd0) after a restart, which appears on no identity bar list, so the mechanical appointment check (AST-018 appoint) would have accepted it as independent -- the bar had to be applied manually by the PO/ARB on participation grounds since the mechanism itself would not have caught it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This process added itself to the implementer bar the moment it recorded §2-§6. Governance-recording is not a lane, but it is participation.
b_rows_sample.statement: States that a process recording a governance decision, though holding no formal workflow lane, is itself a participation act that self-bars that process from later filling an independence-sensitive role on the same matter -- governance-recording capacity is explicitly not exempt from participation-based exclusion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K = S + iA where S = semantic state, A = authority state ... What something says and whether the organization is authorized to treat it as true are different dimensions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes representing a knowledge artifact's semantic-state and authority-state as the real and imaginary components of a complex number, so the two dimensions are never collapsed into a single scalar.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ΔK = ΔS + iΔA ... They disagree semantically. from: They agree semantically, but their authority states conflict. Those are completely different governance problems.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the complex-number model with a difference operator separating semantic conflict from authority conflict as two distinct governance problems, noting compatibility with the existing R-CONFLICT concept.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not make 'complex number = knowledge' ... KnowledgeOS is fundamentally about: meaning, evidence, provenance, authority, lifecycle, invariants, relationships, decisions, governance. A complex number cannot represent all of that.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly warns against equating knowledge itself with a complex number; mathematics is proposed as a domain-supporting analytical mechanism layered above the domain model, never the domain model itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K = [S, E, A, P, T]^T ... complex numbers become a special two-dimensional projection: z = S+iA or z = E+iP.
a_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes the two-dimensional complex-number model into a five-dimensional vector (semantic validity, evidence strength, authority, provenance integrity, temporal validity), with any complex-number model recast as a special two-axis projection of the fuller vector.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EKS PKS AIP → Current architecture → Domain discovery → Invariants → Knowledge concepts → Mathematical properties → Mathematical representation. Not: Complex numbers → invent KnowledgeOS model.
a_rows_sample.statement: States a DDD-priority ordering rule: mathematical representation must be derived last, after current-architecture evidence, domain discovery, invariants, and knowledge concepts are established — never chosen first and used to invent the domain model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would record this as a research hypothesis, not an architecture decision ... Can the semantic state and authority state of real EKS/PKS artifacts be represented without losing domain meaning? If yes, investigate further. If no, discard the model.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes the first concrete falsifiable experiment for the complex-number model: test K=S+iA against real EKS/PKS artifacts and discard the model if domain meaning is lost.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CAPPI's numeric epistemic stack (mu/tau/w -> Bayesian fusion -> quality score) has ZERO current-architecture support. None of EKS/PKS/AIP uses a continuous calibrated confidence signal, a Bayesian fusion step, or a scalar quality score.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports the single strongest case in the investigation of an elegant external principle unsupported by current evidence: continuous calibrated confidence, per-instance uncertainty, and a reliability weight (mu/tau/w) are absent from all three baselines, whose discrete verdict vocabularies and honest UNKNOWN answers are philosophically the inverse of a probabilistic quality score.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ALT-09 · Complex-number epistemic model
a_rows_sample.statement: K(t) = M(t) + iA(t) — knowledge as a complex quantity over time (20260821-2325, root era) — was a modeling-tool exploration never carried into kernel or Step eras; the notation K_t was later re-coined with a different meaning; no v0.2 correspondence, and the same-notation collision was recorded in the GN-28 delta pass.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero = Neutral starting condition ... It begins as: UNKNOWN
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero as neutral knowledge state: Zero != Nothing, it is a neutral starting condition. A new knowledge object begins without authority, evidence, validation or interpretation -- it begins as UNKNOWN.

b_rows_sample.anchor: UNKNOWN != False. UNKNOWN != Missing. UNKNOWN = Known unresolved state
b_rows_sample.statement: UNKNOWN is proposed as a first-class state, distinct from False and from Missing: UNKNOWN = a known, unresolved state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: UNKNOWN != False. UNKNOWN != Missing. UNKNOWN = Known unresolved state
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero lens: UNKNOWN restated as a first-class known-unresolved state, distinct from False and Missing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS should not force: Unknown -> False / Unknown -> Guess / Unknown -> Empty. Instead: Unknown -> Known Unknown
b_rows_sample.statement: Combining Zero ('unknown is a valid state') with ECS ('failure does not destroy truth, failure pauses advancement'): Unknown should be preserved and later resolved, never forced into False/Guess/Empty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Different observations may represent different projections of the same underlying object.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets the elephant-and-blind-men story (cited by the source) not as 'everyone is equally right' but as 'different observations may represent different projections of the same underlying object', formalized as perspectives A/B/C/D undergoing structural comparison to yield a common invariant = ZERO.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge is perspective dependent, but structure may be perspective invariant.
b_rows_sample.statement: Abstracts the source's citation of Subhash Kak's six-darsanas-as-cube-walls metaphor into the principle 'knowledge is perspective dependent, but structure may be perspective invariant', with the research question 'what survives when we rotate the perspective?' answered by ZERO = invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z_M(K) = invariant across plausible worlds ... The technology disappears. The invariant remains.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces modal Zero Z_M(K) = invariant across plausible worlds, alongside a claimed prior representation Zero Z_R(K)=invariant across representations and temporal Zero Z_T(K)=invariant across time; illustrated by four possible event-bus technology choices (Kafka/RabbitMQ/sync API/another event bus) all preserving the invariant requirement 'evidence publication must remain replayable' -- the technology disappears, the invariant remains.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z = ⋂_i Structure(I_i) ... What structure remains invariant across competing models, representations, times, and perspectives? That may be one of our strongest candidates for robust knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the Zero lens as Z=intersection_i Structure(I_i) over interpretations generated from multiple world models W1..Wn (not necessarily literal set intersection in implementation), asking what structure remains invariant across competing models, representations, times and perspectives, proposed as one of the strongest candidates for robust knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: O_i = π_i(R) ... O1 ≠ O2 doesn't necessarily mean R1 ≠ R2. It may simply mean π1 ≠ π2. This gives us a very useful projection lens.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the elephant analogy as a projection: observation Oi=pi_i(R) for underlying reality/object R and observer perspective pi_i, concluding that differing observations O1!=O2 need not imply differing underlying realities R1!=R2 -- it may simply reflect differing perspectives pi1!=pi2 -- named the 'projection lens'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z = Invariant(O1,...,On) ... Zero is not "nothing." It is the minimum invariant structure that survives changes in representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Given observations O1..On, defines Z=Invariant(O1,...,On) and explicitly corrects a possible misreading: Zero is not 'nothing', it is the minimum invariant structure that survives changes in representation -- called one of the strongest concepts in the entire exploration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dhātu = transformation structure ... Zero = invariant structure ... what changed? / what remained?
b_rows_sample.statement: States a Dhatu/Zero duality: given O1 --T1--> O2 --T2--> O3, Dhatu asks what transformation generated the new state (Dhatu = transformation structure) while Zero asks what remained (Zero = invariant structure).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge itself should not be reduced to its representations.
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens result on Williamson: after removing beliefs, documents, language, databases, probabilities, possible worlds, embeddings, topics, LLMs, what survives is minimal: 'A participant is related to a proposition/content in a world/context/time such that the proposition is true and the participant is in a factive state of knowing.' Knowledge itself should not be reduced to its representations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Participants make commitments. 2. Commitments have inferential consequences. 3. Some commitments are supported/entitled...
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens extraction on Brandom (removing language/English/sentences/speech/Frege/Wittgenstein/philosophy) yields ten survivor claims: participants make commitments; commitments have inferential consequences; some commitments are supported/entitled; commitments can conflict; participants assess one another's commitments; new actions alter the state; implicit relations can become explicit; concepts are characterized partly by inferential roles; objectivity can emerge within social assessment; a claim is not merely a string but a position in a normative/inferential structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown is not simply an error state. It is a legitimate epistemic condition.
b_rows_sample.statement: ASP answer-set semantics give TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN query results and ground at least three distinct kinds of 'unknown': unknown because alternatives remain (P and ¬P both possible), unknown because the agent is unaware (neither represented), and unknown because a default was blocked (an exception/missing condition prevented an otherwise-applicable default). The earlier flat UNKNOWN category should become an Epistemic Status taxonomy: true/false/unresolved-alternatives/not-represented-unaware/defeasibly-inferable-but-blocked/etc; the exact taxonomy remains a research question but the distinction itself is now strongly grounded.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Absence must not silently become an epistemic state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Danger flagged in the Projection model: 'If Projection P2 doesn't contain X, therefore X is false' would be wrong, since absence from a projection could mean not relevant, not visible, not assessed, outside scope, unavailable, superseded, or genuinely no longer justified — these are different meanings. This connects to the ZERO lens: absence must not silently become an epistemic state, giving another reason to preserve ZERO discipline within the Projection idea.

b_rows_sample.anchor: U(e) ∈ {alternative, unrepresented, blocked-default, outside-scope, computationally-unresolved}
b_rows_sample.statement: Unknownness U(e) is proposed not as a Boolean but a classification (alternative / unrepresented / blocked-default / outside-scope / computationally-unresolved), with the exact taxonomy left empirical and countable for future statistical analysis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. There is an underlying world/domain. 2. A participant has beliefs/knowledge about it. 3. Only part of that knowledge may be explicitly represented...
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens extraction on Brachman & Levesque (removing FOL/Prolog/frames/description logic/SAT/default logic/Bayesian networks/STRIPS/GOLOG) yields twelve survivor claims: an underlying world/domain exists; a participant has beliefs/knowledge about it; only part is explicitly represented; representation is a mapping between domains; reasoning derives implicit content from explicit content; meaning depends on interpretation/context; different representation languages have different expressive power; reasoning capability is resource-limited; knowledge changes and can be revised; uncertainty/vagueness require richer representations; the same knowledge may have different representations; action depends on knowledge — described as extraordinarily close to the current model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: what survives across *both* phases is: **a knower/participant · something known · a ground · and a record that the two were connected.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens applied across both phases: after stripping optional attributes, what survives universally is a knower/participant, something known, a ground, and a record that the two were connected — every phase and nearly every model retains those four; nothing else survives universally. The corpus distinguishes 'nothing exists' from 'we do not know' (0258: 'Knowledge is not only about what exists'; formal law §9: unknown≠absent≠false). Whether UNKNOWN is the absence of Knowledge or a state of an identified object is NOT resolved by the corpus: formal law (⟨Z-1⟩) says UNKNOWN/ABSENT/FALSE/REJECTED are states of an identified epistemic object, while kernel document 125708 §17 pushes the other way ('UNKNOWN must not be a single epistemic state', eight readings) — no new state proposed here.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AF-004 · Zero's chronology inverts CF-005's apparent ordering
b_rows_sample.statement: The repository's 'third sense' of Zero (Z-KOS-001 meta-principle) and the absence-lens sense are BOTH dated 2026-08-22; the goal-gap function sense is the LATEST (2026-08-27 era) — inverting an apparent ordering implied by CF-005.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CF-005 · Zero naming collision — a third sense
b_rows_sample.statement: Repository Zero (Z-KOS-001) is a foundational meta-principle explicitly refused as kernel article and implementation object ('Zero is the name for that prevention', 'Zero != Component = Property of the boundaries'), whereas v0.2 Zero is the computable goal-gap function Zero(K, EC); same term, incompatible senses, extending the CON-01 lineage with an implementation-side third sense; no repository counterpart of the goal-gap function exists, and the eta-totality/G-residual question (T-9) stays open.

a_rows_sample.anchor: How can we construct an interpretation when we do not already know the meaning of the language or the beliefs of the speaker? ... Meaning, Belief, Truth must be reconstructed together.
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames Davidson's radical-interpretation problem as structurally identical to a core KnowledgeOS problem: constructing semantic knowledge from observation without presupposing the interpretation being established; yields Observation!=Interpretation, Evidence!=Meaning, Meaning!=Belief, with the key insight that Meaning/Belief/Truth must be reconstructed TOGETHER, not derived linearly.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A finite generative theory -> many particular determinations. ... the KnowledgeOS kernel is a transformation mechanism rather than merely a knowledge database.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports Davidson's interpreter as constructing a finite generative theory from which interpretations of infinitely many utterances follow, offered as strong structural support (independent of Rescorla) for the hypothesis that the KnowledgeOS kernel is a generative transformation mechanism (script-K -> {K_1,...,K_n}) rather than a stored answer database.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Truth(c,t) iff Nexus listens on port 8081 at t. ... P(c)=0.95 does not tell us what would make c true. TruthConditions != Probability.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces truth conditions as a semantic layer distinct from probability: a claim's truth condition specifies what would make it true, which a probability/confidence value does not supply, reinforcing Pi_t!=K_t and proposing TruthConditions->EpistemicProbability rather than Probability->Meaning.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Meaning(k_i) not-equiv Meaning(k_i) independently. More plausibly: Meaning(k_i) = f(k_i, K_t, Context). ... Atomicity != Context independence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies Davidsonian holism to the atomic-claim model: an atomic claim's meaning is not semantically isolated but a function of the whole knowledge state and context (Meaning(k_i)=f(k_i,K_t,Context)), illustrated by 'Nexus server runs RHEL 9.8' vs 'Nexus container runs on RHEL 9.8' -- yielding the principle Atomicity != Context-independence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KS_t = (K_t, R_t) where R contains relations such as entails, contradicts, presupposes, supports, depends on, contextualizes, excludes, is compatible with. ... Knowledge quality depends partly on relational structure, not merely atomic claim count.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes reconceiving Knowledge Space as a relational structure KS_t=(K_t,R_t) rather than a bare storage set, with R_t carrying entailment/contradiction/presupposition/support/dependency/contextualization/exclusion/compatibility relations among claims -- explicitly a research candidate, not the KnowledgeOS definition, connected to the corpus's existing DDD/evidence-graph work.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Buddhi_candidate = Discriminate(Interpretations | Evidence, Context, Coherence, Truth).
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines the candidate Buddhi/Discriminate operator using Davidsonian interpretation constraints (coherence, truth conditions, evidence, background beliefs, behavioral compatibility) into Buddhi_candidate=Discriminate(Interpretations | Evidence,Context,Coherence,Truth), explicitly [INF] not an established Gita-KnowledgeOS identity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: BestInterpretation = argmax Intelligibility, subject to Truth+Evidence+Coherence+Context. ... otherwise KnowledgeOS could optimize for what everybody agrees with rather than what is epistemically defensible.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a naive principle-of-charity formulation (BestInterpretation=argmax Agreement) to BestInterpretation=argmax Intelligibility subject to Truth+Evidence+Coherence+Context, explicitly to prevent KnowledgeOS from optimizing for consensus rather than epistemic defensibility.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Maintain competing interpretations/models until evidence discriminates. ... premature collapse is dangerous.
a_rows_sample.statement: Combines Davidson's requirement to compare multiple candidate interpretations with a parallel rival-hypotheses principle into a generalized rule: maintain competing interpretations/models simultaneously until evidence actually discriminates between them, warning that the corpus already shows a tendency toward proliferating candidate models without ever selecting one, but that premature collapse is equally dangerous.

a_rows_sample.anchor: significantly different theories may still fit the evidence equally well [after all evidence is available]. ... Evidence sufficient for adequacy does not imply unique representation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports Davidson's indeterminacy-of-interpretation result (multiple significantly different theories can fit all available evidence equally well) as grounds for a KnowledgeOS distinction between epistemic uncertainty (we don't know which is correct) and representational indeterminacy (several representations are equally adequate) -- explicitly not the same phenomenon, and both compatible with Evidence-sufficient-for-adequacy not implying a unique representation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Fahrenheit and Celsius differ numerically while preserving the relevant structure. ... RepresentationEquality(A,B) should be defined independently from SemanticEquivalence(A,B).
a_rows_sample.statement: Uses Davidson's temperature-scale example (Fahrenheit and Celsius numerically differ while preserving the same relational/semantic pattern) as a second, independent argument for separating RepresentationEquality(A,B) from SemanticEquivalence(A,B), extending the corpus's existing SNF(x)=SNF(y) does not imply x=y non-collapse with a positive converse case (different representations, same meaning).

a_rows_sample.anchor: What is invariant across valid KnowledgeOS representations? Possibilities include: truth conditions, entailment relations, causal relations, identity, temporal relations, evidential dependencies, inquiry adequacy. But we must test each.
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses, drawing on Davidson's claim that meaning may be what remains invariant across alternative acceptable truth theories, the research question of what is invariant across valid KnowledgeOS representations, listing seven untested candidate invariants (truth conditions, entailment, causal relations, identity, temporal relations, evidential dependencies, inquiry adequacy), framed as potentially more important than finding one canonical representation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Different representations != different worlds. ... Ontology is constrained by truth, evidence, language, and relations [but there is no neutral common coordinate system].
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports Davidson's rejection of radically incommensurable conceptual schemes (different representations != different worlds; different ontologies must be compared via shared constraints/evidence) while equally explicitly rejecting the opposite overreading that Davidson licenses one neutral universal KnowledgeOS ontology -- Davidson denies a neutral common coordinate system entirely, so ontology remains constrained rather than unified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SemanticFrame = (Agent, Time, Context, Language, Purpose). ... a claim cannot always be interpreted without knowing whose claim, under what conditions, for what purpose.
a_rows_sample.statement: Strengthens the 'Knower owns the frame' principle into a candidate SemanticFrame=(Agent,Time,Context,Language,Purpose), grounded in Davidson's finding that interpreting an utterance requires accounting for speaker, time, circumstances, beliefs, intentions and actions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Communication != shared representation. Communication = Successful alignment of interpretation. ... Inquiry + Semantic Contract. Q=(T,P,C,R,Gamma,Sigma).
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Inquiry tuple with a semantic-interpretation-constraints field, Q=(T,P,C,R,Gamma,Sigma), motivated by Davidson's Communication-and-Convention argument that successful communication does not require speaker and hearer to share identical languages or prior interpretation theories (Communication != shared representation; Communication = successful alignment of interpretation) -- aimed at preventing KnowledgeOS from answering the wrong interpretation of a client's question.

a_rows_sample.anchor: reduction and definition are sometimes too much to expect; the relation between theory and evidence may be looser. ... Theory -> constraints -> empirical consequences -> increasing determination.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts an anti-premature-definition principle from Davidson (definitional reduction can be too much to expect of a theory; theory-evidence fit may be looser than strict definition), matching and reinforcing the corpus's own discipline against prematurely fixing 'Knowledge := X.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel Minimality Experiment ... {Observe, Interpret, Represent, Relate, Discriminate, Hypothesize, Infer, DetectGap, Challenge, Validate, Revise, Determine, Select} ... remove one operator at a time.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a concrete, executable 'KnowledgeOS Kernel Minimality Experiment': a 13-operator candidate set to be tested against a checklist of required capabilities by removing one operator at a time, with explicit survival logic (if removing Interpret makes semantic knowledge impossible, Interpret survives as primitive; if removing Hypothesize merely causes another operator to absorb its function, Hypothesize may not be primitive; if Zero can be represented as a predicate over K_t rather than an operation, it is not a kernel primitive) -- explicitly proposing Zero(K_t,I_Q,EC) be treated as a state predicate rather than assumed a primitive kernel operation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Freedman tells us: don't trust an unsupported inference. Davidson tells us: don't even assume the interpretation of the evidence is already known. ... How does an epistemic system construct, constrain, validate, and revise the interpretation through which evidence becomes knowledge?
a_rows_sample.statement: States the file's most important conclusion: combining an unread-in-this-batch 'Freedman' source's inference-scrutiny principle with Davidson's interpretation-scrutiny principle reframes the central KnowledgeOS question from 'how do we infer knowledge from evidence' to 'how does an epistemic system construct, constrain, validate, and revise the interpretation through which evidence becomes knowledge' -- named one of the central unanswered questions of the theory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What is the smallest set of genuinely irreducible epistemic capabilities required for KnowledgeOS to support the required knowledge lifecycle? ... This is a MINIMALITY / ABLATION experiment. It is NOT a naming exercise.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the primary research question as a formal ablation experiment over candidate operator set C0 (13 operators), explicitly distinguishing it from naming exercises, aesthetic simplification, universal-necessity claims, or retrofitting existing architecture, and requiring provenance tagging ([CORPUS]/[EXT]/[INF]/[PROP]/[EXP]/[NEG]/[OPEN]) with no silent promotion to canon.

b_rows_sample.anchor: if the proposed implementation merely changes Discriminate into DiscriminateIncludingGapDetection, then DetectGap has NOT actually been eliminated. That is semantic smuggling.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines 'semantic smuggling' as the critical failure mode of the whole experiment: claiming an operator is reducible by silently renaming its function into a remaining operator (e.g. Remove DetectGap, redefine Validate to also detect gaps) rather than genuinely composing it from independent semantics -- requires an explicit SMUGGLING=TRUE/FALSE flag with justification for every proposed reduction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A. Cardinality minimality ... B. Semantic minimality ... C. Compositional minimality ... D. Architectural minimality ... E. Cognitive universality. Do NOT assume these are equivalent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes five non-equivalent senses of kernel 'minimality' (cardinality; semantic -- no operator removable without losing an irreducible capability; compositional -- every retained operator contributes something non-reproducible by composition of others; architectural -- no separate responsibility introduced when naturally derivable from another; cognitive universality -- required by every epistemic system), designating semantic+compositional minimality as the primary experimental target and cardinality as only secondary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C1 acquire an observation ... C24 support learning from new observations. These are INITIAL capabilities. ... Do not optimize the capability list merely to make the operator set smaller.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a 24-item capability space (C1-C24, spanning observation acquisition, meaning construction, representation, relation, discrimination, hypothesis formation, inference, gap detection, challenge, validation, revision, inquiry-adequacy determination, action selection, context/temporal/uncertainty/assumption representation, provenance and alternative preservation, non-identifiability support, observation-vs-interpretation distinction, representation-independent semantic equivalence, smallest-adequate-answer production, and learning from new observations) that must be derived independently of the candidate operator names, not by restating them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: oi : S_i -> S_j where S_i and S_j are abstract epistemic states/artifacts. Do not assume all operators act directly on K_t.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes candidate operators as typed transformations over explicitly distinct carrier types (Observation, Evidence, SemanticRepresentation, Hypothesis, Model, Claim, AlternativeSet, RequirementSet, EpistemicState, DecisionProposal), explicitly rejecting the assumption that every operator acts directly on K_t, and requires every proposed composite reduction o_removed=f(o_remaining) to be documented across nine dimensions (input/output type, preconditions, postconditions, semantic/epistemic effect, information loss, introduced assumptions, and whether removed semantics were secretly embedded elsewhere).

b_rows_sample.anchor: SCENARIO 7 — Missing evidence ... Expected possibility: cannot determine. ... SCENARIO 12 — Smallest adequate answer.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a 16-scenario canonical test suite grounded in concrete Nexus-infrastructure examples (basic/numeric/network observation; conflicting evidence; ambiguous semantics like 'the server is available'; temporal revision without conflating historical and current-state equality; missing evidence legitimately yielding 'cannot determine'; competing partially-supported hypotheses; model criticism; context-dependent semantic interpretation; inquiry-relative adequacy; smallest adequate answer; cost-constrained action selection; non-identifiability; provenance conflict; representation equivalence).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Build a SMALL RESEARCH SIMULATOR. ... Do NOT claim this is the canonical KnowledgeOS state model. Label it: [PROP] experimental state representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires building a small, explicitly non-production research simulator over an explicitly [PROP]-labelled experimental epistemic state K_t=(claims,representations,relations,evidence,provenance,assumptions,alternatives,uncertainty,context,history), with every helper function classified (domain operator / data-structure operation / infrastructure utility / test harness / serialization) so that only genuine domain operators count toward kernel size.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Leave-one-out is not sufficient. Some operators may be individually removable but jointly necessary. ... pairwise ablation; ... selected triple ablations.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires pairwise and higher-order ablation beyond simple leave-one-out, explicitly anticipating that some operators may be individually removable yet jointly necessary (synergy, substitution, hidden dependency, or operator bundles) -- illustrated by Interpret+Represent potentially being coupled without necessarily being one operator, requiring a typed factorization test rather than an assumption.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PROPERTY P2 — Non-identifiability: If evidence cannot distinguish H1 and H2, the system must not fabricate a unique determination. ... PROPERTY P7 — No information creation: Processing existing evidence cannot create unsupported empirical information.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies ten falsifiable properties (P1-P10) for randomized property-based simulation testing: revision-representability under contradicting evidence, non-fabrication under non-identifiability, provenance preservation, temporal consistency (no erasure of historical truth), semantic distinction preserved when evidence does not resolve it, adequacy != mere answer-existence, no information creation from pure processing, alternative preservation absent evidence-based elimination, context-sensitivity of relevance, and challenge-required-before-validated.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT interpret a 99% scenario success rate as proof of correctness. ... Statistics support robustness assessment; they do not prove minimality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Prescribes disciplined statistical treatment: separate deterministic logical failures from stochastic/implementation/model-specification/conceptual failures, report failure rates and robustness across seeds and sensitivity to definitional choices rather than a single aggregate score, and explicitly distinguishes the statistical robustness question (p_hat_failure) from the logical necessity question (exists x: Reach(S,x) != Reach(S union {o},x)) -- statistics inform robustness, they do not establish minimality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: But do NOT equate: information quantity = knowledge. ... Do NOT equate: Pi_t = K_t. ... fit != validation, regression != causality, estimation != identification.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires the experiment to run information-theoretic checks (data-processing inequality, sufficient representation) without equating information quantity with knowledge, probabilistic checks (Pi_t=L(X|F_t) without Pi_t=K_t) across six specified uncertainty scenarios, and a causal/model-criticism check enforcing fit!=validation, regression!=causality, estimation!=identification as three explicitly distinct failure classes a model must not conflate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero = predicate ... Ideal State = state/target construct ... Inquiry = domain input ... Governance = external constraint ... Authorization = governance mechanism ... Select = decision/action mechanism. But these are hypotheses. Test them.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a DDD pass over every candidate operator asking whether it is a genuine domain capability owning a distinct invariant/responsibility, or instead a policy, state predicate, or orchestration concern -- explicitly naming Zero, Ideal State, Inquiry, Governance, Authorization, and Select as operators whose kernel membership must be tested rather than assumed, offering (only as hypotheses) demotions of each to a non-operator role.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not conclude: 'Operator X is necessary because the current KnowledgeOS architecture already has X.' That would be circular.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly forbids architectural circularity as a justification for kernel membership (existing class != domain primitive; existing service != kernel operator; existing workflow != epistemic necessity), requiring the experiment to reason from domain capabilities and epistemic requirements rather than from current implementation structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: F1 — Representation failure ... F19 — Implementation artifact ... F20 — Simulator artifact. Do not call F19/F20 kernel failures. ... Never manufacture a positive result.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a twenty-category failure taxonomy (F1-F20) for classifying ablation failures, explicitly excluding implementation and simulator artifacts (F19/F20) from counting as genuine kernel failures, and mandates that negative results ('removing X did not break anything', 'no meaningful conclusion can currently be drawn') be treated as first-class, valid, and never suppressed in favor of manufactured positive findings.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Search for multiple Pareto candidates. ... Do not collapse these into one arbitrary weighted score.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires searching for multiple Pareto-optimal candidate kernels (not one single smallest kernel) evaluated along nine uncollapsed axes (cardinality, semantic coverage, compositionality, coupling, interpretability, falsifiability, domain cohesion, implementation independence, evidence strength), with any weighted composite score requiring an explicit sensitivity analysis over weight choices.

b_rows_sample.anchor: find S subset-of O such that C_required subset-of Reach(S) and forall o in S: C_required not-subset-of Reach(S \ {o}). ... Reach(S) ... must be defined carefully.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes semantic minimality as a set-system reachability problem: find a minimal operator subset S such that all required capabilities are reachable by valid typed compositions of S, and no operator in S can be removed without breaking that containment -- explicitly cautioning that the Reach(S) composition function must be defined by explicit, non-arbitrary rules rather than declared to include whatever the researcher wishes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Empirically necessary ... Formally necessary ... DDD-necessary ... These can disagree. ... That is a very interesting result -- not a contradiction.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three independent necessity tests (empirical: the simulator cannot run without it; formal: no valid composition of remaining operators supplies it; DDD: the responsibility is a genuinely distinct domain concept) that can legitimately disagree without contradiction, illustrated by Select potentially being computationally derivable from Determine while DDD analysis still separates epistemic determination from action selection as distinct responsibilities.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 01-research-question.md ... 03-capability-model.md ... 04-operator-contracts.md ... 05-operator-capability-matrix.md ... 06-composition-rules.md ... FINAL-kernel-reduction-report.md
b_rows_sample.statement: Prescribes a fixed 18-file experimental output directory (docs/knowledgeos/research/kernel-reduction/), explicitly forbidding modification of canonical architecture documents and requiring the simulator code to be isolated in an experimental directory -- this file naming scheme directly matches several files this same batch reads (01-research-question.md, 03-capability-model.md, 04-operator-contracts.md, 05-operator-capability-matrix.md, 06-composition-rules.md), identifying this prompt as their likely originating mandate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would consider the experiment successful even if Claude concludes: 'The 13 operators cannot yet be meaningfully minimized because the semantic granularity of the candidate operators is unstable.' ... What is the correct mathematical type and semantic granularity of an epistemic primitive?
b_rows_sample.statement: Names as potentially the single most valuable possible experimental outcome a finding that the 13 candidate operators cannot yet be meaningfully minimized because their semantic granularity is itself unstable -- reframing the open research problem from 'which operator to delete' to 'what is the correct mathematical type and semantic granularity of an epistemic primitive', and explicitly allows the kernel to turn out structurally different from a flat operator set (e.g. K=(S,T,O) or K=(P,R,delta), or some operators turning out to be predicates like Zero rather than transformations).

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'kernel-reduction-ablation-experiment-protocol' POSSIBLY relates to 'davidson-radical-interpretation-holism-and-kernel-minimality-experiment' (batch B0056). Note: A fully worked-out, copy-paste-ready Claude Code CLI research prompt operationalizing the kernel-minimality-experiment idea (raised earlier the same day, see the Davidson file's closing section) into a rigorous ablation/ DDD/statistical protocol. States the primary research question over the candidate 13-operator set C0={Observe,Interpret,Represent,Relate,Discriminate,Hypothesize,Infer,DetectGap,Challenge,Validate,Revise,Determine,Select}: for each operator, does removal necessarily destroy a required capability, or can the capability be reconstructed by composition without SEMANTIC SMUGGLING (renaming a removed operator's function into a remaining one, e.g. redefining Validate to secretly also detect all gaps rather than genuinely composing it from DetectGap-free primitives) -- an explicit, formally flagged (SMUGGLING=TRUE/FALSE) failure mode. Preserves twenty numbered prior KnowledgeOS research constraints (K_t!=K_{t+1}; historical identity!=current-state equality; Kernel/K_t/KnowledgeSpace distinct; Zero as a state-predicate candidate Zero(K_t,I_Q,EC) rather than assumed a primitive operation; Ideal State as inquiry/purpose/context-dependent; Inquiry=(Target,Purpose,Context,Requirements,Constraints,...); Extraction!=Determination; Observation!=Interpretation; Information!=Evidence!=Justification!=Truth!=Knowledge; probability as epistemic metadata not knowledge; representation-equality!=semantic-equality; Knowledge Space as relational not a bag; assumptions must be explicit; 'cannot determine' as a legitimate outcome; non-identifiability must be represented). Distinguishes five distinct senses of 'minimal' that must not be assumed equivalent: cardinality minimality, semantic minimality (no operator removable without losing an irreducible capability), compositional minimality (every retained operator contributes something non-reproducible by the others), architectural minimality (no separate responsibility introduced when one is naturally derivable from another), and cognitive universality (required by every epistemic system) -- the experiment's primary target is semantic+compositional minimality, cardinality only secondary. Defines an independently-derived 24-item capability space (C1-C24: acquire observation, preserve/construct meaning, construct representation, relate representations, discriminate alternatives, formulate hypotheses, perform inference, detect epistemic insufficiency, challenge a claim/model, validate, revise state, determine inquiry-adequacy, select next action, represent context/temporal-conditions/uncertainty/assumptions, preserve provenance/alternative-hypotheses, support non-identifiability, distinguish observation from interpretation, support semantic equivalence without representation identity, produce a smallest adequate answer, support learning from new observations) that must NOT be derived merely by restating operator names, feeding an operator-times-capability matrix (cell codes 0/1/D/S/R/?) and per-operator abstract contracts (input/output/preconditions/postconditions/state/information/semantic/epistemic effects/dependencies/possible composition/non-reducible responsibility). Formalizes an abstract typed operator algebra (oi: S_i -> S_j over carriers such as Observation/Evidence/SemanticRepresentation/Hypothesis/Model/Claim/AlternativeSet/RequirementSet/EpistemicState/DecisionProposal, not all acting directly on K_t) and requires every proposed reduction o_removed=f(o_remaining) to be documented across nine dimensions including whether the removed operator's semantics were secretly embedded elsewhere. Mandates a 16-scenario canonical test suite (basic/numeric/network observation; conflicting evidence; ambiguous semantics; temporal revision; missing evidence -> 'cannot determine'; competing hypotheses; model criticism; semantic interpretation context-sensitivity; inquiry-relative adequacy; smallest adequate answer; action selection under cost; non-identifiability; provenance conflict; representation equivalence) and a small (non-production) executable research simulator over an explicitly [PROP]-labelled experimental state K_t=(claims,representations,relations,evidence,provenance,assumptions,alternatives,uncertainty,context,history). Requires leave-one-out AND pairwise/higher-order ablation (individually-removable-but-jointly-necessary operators are a distinct, expected finding), randomized property-based simulation testing ten explicit properties (P1 revision-representability, P2 non-identifiability-non-fabrication, P3 provenance preservation, P4 temporal consistency/no historical erasure, P5 semantic distinction under unresolved evidence, P6 adequacy != mere answer-existence, P7 no information creation from pure processing, P8 alternative preservation absent elimination-by-evidence, P9 context-sensitivity of relevance, P10 challenge-required-before-validated), and statistical treatment that explicitly refuses false precision (no single percentage-better claim; reports failure categories, robustness across seeds, sensitivity analyses; separates the statistical robustness question p_hat_failure from the logical necessity question exists-x: Reach(S,x) != Reach(S union {o}, x)). Requires an information-theoretic check (data-processing inequality, sufficient representation) without equating information quantity with knowledge, a probabilistic check (Pi_t=L(X|F_t) without Pi_t=K_t), and a causal/model-criticism check (fit != validation, regression != causality, estimation != identification) as distinct failure classes. Requires a full DDD pass asking of every operator whether it is a genuine domain capability, owns an invariant, is a policy/predicate/orchestration-concern rather than a kernel primitive -- explicitly naming Zero/IdealState/Inquiry/Governance/Authorization/Select/Determine as operators whose kernel membership must be TESTED not assumed, with candidate demotions (Zero=predicate; IdealState=state/target construct; Inquiry=domain input; Governance=external constraint; Authorization=governance mechanism; Select=decision/action mechanism) offered only as hypotheses. Explicitly forbids architectural circularity ('X is necessary because current KnowledgeOS architecture already has X' is invalid reasoning) and mandates twenty explicit failure-mode categories (F1-F20, with F19/F20 explicitly excluded as mere implementation/simulator artifacts, never counted as kernel failures) and mandatory negative-result reporting (never manufacture a positive result; 'no meaningful conclusion can currently be drawn' is a valid outcome). Requires the researcher to search for Pareto-optimal ALTERNATIVE kernels (not just one smallest one) evaluated along nine uncollapsed axes (cardinality, semantic coverage, compositionality, coupling, interpretability, falsifiability, domain cohesion, implementation independence, evidence strength) and formalizes minimality as a set-system reachability problem (find minimal S subset-of O such that C_required subset-of Reach(S) and no o in S is removable without breaking that containment) while cautioning Reach(S) must be explicitly and non-arbitrarily defined. Prescribes a fixed 18-file output directory structure under docs/knowledgeos/research/kernel-reduction/ (01-research-question.md through 17-open-questions.md plus a FINAL report) -- directly matching several files this same batch reads (01-research-question.md, 03-capability-model.md, 04-operator-contracts.md, 05-operator-capability-matrix.md, 06-composition-rules.md), confirming this prompt is their originating mandate. Distinguishes three independent necessity tests that can legitimately disagree without contradiction -- empirical necessity (simulator cannot run the scenarios without it), formal necessity (no valid composition of remaining operators supplies it), and DDD-necessity (the responsibility is a genuinely distinct domain concept even if software composition is technically possible) -- illustrated by Select potentially being computationally derivable from Determine while DDD analysis still treats epistemic determination and action selection as separate responsibilities. Explicitly allows the experiment to discover the kernel is not simply a flat operator set but something structurally different (e.g. K=(S,T,O) a state space plus transformations, or K=(P,R,delta) primitives/composition-relations/transition-mechanism, or some 'operators' turning out to be predicates like Zero rather than transformations) -- naming as the single most valuable possible outcome the finding that the 13 operators cannot yet be meaningfully minimized because their semantic granularity is itself unstable, reframing the open research problem from 'which operator to delete' to 'what is the correct mathematical type and semantic granularity of an epistemic primitive.'
