a_rows_sample.statement: Elaborates the earlier Zero/Lord/Sarathi/Transition division with explicit role definitions: Zero detects gaps/conflicts/boundaries; Lord expands the possibility space; Sarathi navigates/guides; Transition actually changes state. The earlier Sarathi formalization is given a full function signature: Sarathi(K_t, Z_t, L_t, I_t, Q_t, C_t) -> a_t, where a_t is the next epistemic action -- described as remarkably close to what is now called action selection/guidance, though the modern formal model deliberately avoids promoting the old lens vocabulary into architectural objects. Confirms the earlier KnowledgeOS-as-Epistemic-Sarathi formulation (rather than an answer engine) and its See != Guide != Decide principle, noting it later became compatible with the modern formal chain Evidence != Determination != Proposal != Decision != Authorization != Action.

type_signature.domain: K_t, Z_t, L_t, I_t, Q_t, C_t

a_rows_sample.anchor: Z(I_t)\rightarrow \{\text{Undefined Criterion, Unassessed Risk, Hidden Assumption}\} ... I_{t+1}=Revision(I_t,U_t). ... \boxed{\text{The Sārathi may challenge the Ideal State, but the Knower owns the revision.}}
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the 'Before We Continue' principle with explicit notation: when current understanding is insufficient, the system can challenge the objective itself. Z(I_t) -> {Undefined Criterion, Unassessed Risk, Hidden Assumption} detects deficiencies in the Ideal State I_t; L(I_t) -> {Possible New Goal Dimensions} expands it; followed by I_{t+1} = Revision(I_t, U_t). The governing rule: the Sarathi may challenge the Ideal State, but the Knower owns the revision -- explicitly named as one of the strongest bridges between the old Step-series theory and the concurrent Gita Chapters 1-4 interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Early conceptual model ↓ KnowledgeState / lenses / journey ↓ Sārathi + Zero + Lord separation ↓ "Before we continue" / objective revision ↓ formal Questions ↓ 25-series formalization ↓ Step 049 kernel reduction ↓ Step 050 adversarial audit ↓ falsification ↓ v0.2 canonical synthesis ↓ Final Architecture ↓ mathematical re-audit
a_rows_sample.statement: Sketches a twelve-stage historical evolution pipeline: early conceptual model -> KnowledgeState/lenses/journey -> Sarathi+Zero+Lord separation -> 'before we continue'/objective revision -> formal Questions -> the 25-series formalization -> Step 049 kernel reduction -> Step 050 adversarial audit -> falsification -> v0.2 canonical synthesis -> Final Architecture -> the current mathematical re-audit (GN-46, S1326). Characterizes v0.2 as a compression and purification of a much larger body of theory, explaining why current Edition-2 production is finding exactly the gaps it is finding. Recommends, rather than reconstructing artificial Step numbers beyond 156, building a four-way crosswalk: Step-era theory <-> v0.2 formal model <-> mathematical research <-> Gita Chapters 1-4, which would show which ideas were already discovered, formally retained, compressed, left open, rediscovered philosophically, and are now testable mathematically -- framed as a much stronger intellectual history of KnowledgeOS than simply claiming the Gita inspired the architecture. Poses an unresolved open research question: what mathematical object is actually produced by epistemic discernment -- a single action a_t in A, a three-valued classification D(K_t,G,Policy) -> {Permitted, Forbidden, Undetermined} over candidate actions, or a map D: A -> {epistemically justified classes}? Explicitly states this is not yet known.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t \neq A Single Assertion ... K_t \neq A Set of Assertions ... K_t = A Structured Collection of Assertions + Their Relationships + Their Epistemic Status + Their History ... K_t = (A_t, R_t, E_t, H_t, Z_t, L_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Knowledge State K_t as a 6-component structure: Assertions A_t, Relationships R_t, Evidence E_t, History H_t (all previous Knowledge States), Zero findings Z_t, and Lord candidates L_t; forms a Knowledge Graph G_t=(A_t,R_t) with Assertions as nodes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identical, Equivalent, Consistent, Contradictory, Causal, Temporal, Normative Conflict, Logical Contradiction ... R_j = (A_i, A_k, Type, Strength, Evidence)
b_rows_sample.statement: Types the Relationship edges of the knowledge graph with eight relation kinds spanning both the earlier Compare vocabulary (Identical/Equivalent/Consistent/Contradictory) and the newer conflict taxonomy (Causal, Temporal, Normative Conflict, Logical Contradiction), each carrying Strength and supporting Evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: State_t = (K_t, I_t, Q_t, C_t) ... I_t = (D_I, V_I, R_I, C_I) ... Compare(K_t, I_t) -> G_t
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces the complete System State as (KnowledgeState,IdealState,Question/Intent,Context), formalizes the Ideal State I_t=(IdealDimensions,IdealValues,IdealRelationships,Constraints), and defines Compare(K_t,I_t)->G_t as the set of gaps between current knowledge and the ideal.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero Detection: Normative conflict between A_2 and A_3 ... Z_1 = (Normative Conflict, {A_2, A_3}, 'Family duty vs. war duty') ... Resolution... Zero Resolved: Z_1 is resolved.
b_rows_sample.statement: Traces the full Arjuna example through five knowledge states K_0..K_4, showing a Zero-detected NormativeConflict finding created when the opposing-side assertion is added and resolved once the moral-conflict assertion clarifies the relation between the grandfather and opponent assertions as Compatible rather than contradictory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A Knowledge State should probably not be defined as 'everything KnowledgeOS has.' It should be defined as the epistemically structured state relevant to a particular observer, purpose, context and time... K_t = K(X,P,N,C,tau)
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects modelling K_t as an absolute, single global object; since the Observation model already parameterizes on Purpose/Observer/Context/Time, the Knowledge State must be similarly parameterized: K_t=K(X,Purpose,Knower,Context,tau), since two Knowers (Arjuna vs Dhrtarastra) observing the same reality do not share an identical Knowledge State.

type_signature.domain: Reality x Purpose x Knower x Context x Time

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t \supset Z_t but Z_t=Zero(K_t) which means the state contains the output of an operation that operates on the state itself... I would therefore define: K_t = CurrentKnowledgeState and separately H_{0:t}=KnowledgeHistory
b_rows_sample.statement: Flags a definitional circularity in the S0783 Knowledge State: embedding Z_t=Zero(K_t) and H_t={K_0,...,K_t} as components of K_t itself makes K_t contain the output of an operation applied to K_t, and makes each historical K_i recursively contain its own history; proposes separating CurrentKnowledgeState K_t from KnowledgeHistory H_{0:t} and computing Zero(K_t)/Lord(K_t) as derived views rather than stored fields.

b_rows_sample.anchor: An assertion does not simply exist. It applies somewhere... Scope = (Context, Time, Subject, Boundary, ...) This is essential for avoiding false contradictions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces Scope as a missing concept an assertion needs (e.g. Nexus.Version=3.69 applies to production but not test; a policy applies to one organization but not another), motivated as necessary to avoid false apparent contradictions between assertions that actually hold in different scopes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge State \neq Conflict Free State ... Coherence = all assertions are mutually interpretable under their dimensions, scopes, contexts and temporal constraints ... A Knowledge State may contain unknowns, conflicts, competing interpretations, unresolved questions, normative tensions and still be coherent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Redefines Coherence away from 'no contradictions' toward 'all assertions are mutually interpretable under their dimensions, scopes, contexts and temporal constraints', explicitly allowing a coherent Knowledge State to contain unknowns, unresolved normative tensions and competing interpretations without being incoherent -- Knowledge State != Conflict-Free State.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Question 13: What is the formal structure of the Knowledge State? ... Is Knowledge State a set, graph, typed graph, labelled graph, relational structure, lattice, or some composite algebraic structure?
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses Question 13 as the prerequisite to formalizing distance: K_t must be given an exact formal structure (set/graph/typed-graph/relational-structure/lattice/composite) before any distance/measurement function over it can be mathematically meaningful.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge State is the formal, typed, structured representation ... K_t = (A_t, R_t, E_t, H_t, Z_t, L_t, T_t, G_t, C_t, M_t) ... Knowledge State = A Structured Typed Graph with Epistemic Metadata
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a ten-component Knowledge State (Assertions, Relationships, Evidence, History, ZeroFindings, LordCandidates, Temporal structure, Knowledge Graph, Context, Metadata/provenance) formalized as a typed, directed, labelled graph, with immutability of History (new states appended, never overwritten) as a core invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K contains things that are not knowledge ... Zero findings: No. Zero findings are observations about the Knowledge State. Lord candidates: Definitely no. History: Probably not part of the instantaneous Knowledge State. Knowledge Graph: probably a representation of the Knowledge State, not another independent component inside it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the ten-component K_t as a category error: Zero findings and Lord candidates are derived observations/hypotheses about the state, not the state itself; History is a temporal model over states, not a field within one state; the typed graph is a representation/projection of the state, not an ontologically independent component. Proposes a smaller canonical K_t=(Propositions,Assertions,Relationships,Evidence,EpistemicState,Context,Temporal,Provenance) with Z_t=Zero(K_t,I_t,Q_t,C_t), L_t=Lord(K_t,I_t,Q_t,C_t), and H_t=History(K_0,...,K_t) all computed externally.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'Contained in' is not the right mathematical relation. Entity not-subset Proposition ... use Participates In / Referenced By / Forms instead.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the typed-universe diagram's 'contained in' arrows (Entity/Dimension/Value -> Propositions) which are not subset relations: an entity participates in a proposition, a dimension is referenced by it; recommends participates-in/referenced-by/forms relations instead, consistent with the earlier containment-vs-set-inclusion correction from Question 7.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SystemState_t = (K_t, U_t, X_t, I_t, Q_t, C_t, N_t, Z_t, L_t, H_t) ... K_t = Knowledge State only
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the complete runtime SystemState as wrapping the (now smaller) Knowledge State K_t together with Understanding U_t, Domain X_t, Ideal I_t, Intent/Question Q_t, Context C_t, Knower N_t, and the derived Z_t/L_t/H_t, cleanly separating what KnowledgeOS knows from what it also tracks about the Knower and the epistemic journey.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Question 14 — What is the Ontology of Knowledge? Is a Proposition a value object? Is an Assertion an entity or value object? Is Evidence itself knowledge? Is a Relationship a proposition? Is an Epistemic State part of an assertion or external? Is a Gap part of knowledge or a finding about knowledge? Is Zero part of the domain model or an operation over it? Is the Knowledge Graph the ontology or merely one representation?
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses Question 14 (Ontology of Knowledge) listing eight unresolved ontological-status questions (Proposition as value object? Assertion entity or value object? Evidence itself knowledge? Relationship a proposition? EpistemicState internal or external to Assertion? Gap knowledge or finding? Zero domain-model or operation? Graph ontology or representation?) to be resolved before implementation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: There is no component of K holding the set of recognised dimensions. ... D_t is the smallest missing component. With it, 'not assessed' is D in D_t AND not exists a in A: a.P.D=D -- decidable in O(n). Without it, the statement has no truth-maker.
b_rows_sample.statement: An executed probe (MISSINGNESS-NOT-ASSESSED in THEORY-CONSTRUCTION-TEST.md) shows a never-assessed dimension and an assessed-with-no-result dimension both render identically in K=(A,R) as 'no assertion mentioning that dimension', proving them provably indistinguishable; introducing D_t (the set of currently recognised dimensions) as a component of K makes 'not assessed' decidable in O(n) and is identified as the smallest missing component to close the missingness gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A construction score is not a proof of adequacy. A scoring exercise establishes RELATIVE rank among the candidates enumerated; it establishes nothing about whether any candidate is sufficient, and it cannot detect a capability that NO candidate was scored on.
b_rows_sample.statement: The claim that K=Set(Assertion) x R is correct because it scored highest (15/19) against six candidates is challenged on methodological grounds: a comparative score establishes only relative rank among enumerated candidates, never absolute sufficiency, and cannot detect capabilities no candidate was scored on -- exactly the three (uncertainty, non-identifiability, missingness) later shown to be missed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K is a representation whose referent is undeclared. That is why adequacy could only be argued by SCORING AGAINST CAPABILITIES, never by FIDELITY TO A REFERENT.
b_rows_sample.statement: Testing five possible classifications of what K 'is' (ontology, mathematical state, representation, abstraction, domain-specific projection), only 'representation' is defensible, but its referent (the W it represents) is never named in the theory, so adequacy can currently only be judged by capability-scoring rather than fidelity to a declared referent; once Omega:W->O exists, adequacy becomes answerable, but not before.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Three of eleven have no body: dedup (does not exist), Sigma's strength rule, delta's commit case.
b_rows_sample.statement: A table of eleven operations over K (member, add, merge, supersede, contradicts, dedup, Sigma, Gamma, delta, History, Lineage) with signatures, preconditions, postconditions, determinism and failure modes shows three have no defined body: dedup does not exist as an operation, Sigma's strength rule is absent, and delta's body is undefined for the commit case.

b_rows_sample.anchor: id before withdrawal : 86a0330e2b65 / id after withdrawal : a9d84e7a43d8 / SAME? False / R edge (...) now dangles: True ... The theory's identity rule and its mutability rule cannot both hold.
b_rows_sample.statement: Executing kaudit.py shows that because id is declared derived as H(P,e,c,t,Pi) while e.state is declared mutable, withdrawing one evidence item re-keys the assertion's id and breaks every R edge pointing at the old id, violating StructuralValid's own no-dangling clause -- an internal contradiction between the identity rule and the mutability rule in the same field table, worsened by the audit's own addition of a mutable state field to e.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Because Pi is inside id, the same fact from two sources is two assertions. ... K grows without bound under re-observation ... R is not maintained by merge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Executing kaudit.py shows two assertions of the identical proposition from two different sources get distinct ids (because Pi/provenance is inside id), so merge-as-union cannot deduplicate: corroboration becomes indistinguishable from duplication, K grows unboundedly under repeated observation of the same fact, merge's idempotence holds only for byte-identical assertions, and cross-state relations between semantic twins are never created by merge, silently dropping information.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'K_t=(A_t,R_t,E_t,H_t,Z_t,L_t)'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemic State != Epistemic Quality != Epistemic Value != Practical Value. This is potentially a major missing dimension in KnowledgeOS. ... Why is one epistemic state better, more valuable, or more worth pursuing than another?
a_rows_sample.statement: Reads the Epistemic Value anthology's central Meno-problem framing (why is knowledge more valuable than mere true belief) as motivating a four-way separation Epistemic State != Epistemic Quality != Epistemic Value != Practical Value, identified as a candidate missing dimension beyond the existing Evidence->Assessment->Determination->Knowledge->Decision->Action pipeline; also extends the corpus's existing Truth!=Justification!=Knowledge chain by adding Value as a fourth distinct term.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Content != Understanding Structure ... suppose two systems contain the same true propositions ... B contains relationships and explanatory structure. ... Know What / Know That / Know How / Know Why / Understand System ... These must not automatically be collapsed into one KnowledgeOS object.
a_rows_sample.statement: Uses a two-state Nexus example (State A: bare fact 'GitLab Runner = 70GB/day'; State B: the same fact plus relational/explanatory structure among CI/CD, caching, network, egress) to argue Knowledge Content != Understanding Structure, and proposes a five-level hierarchy Know What / Know That / Know How / Know Why / Understand System that must not automatically be collapsed into one KnowledgeOS object.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Attention != Value != Truth. ... Epistemic Agency should not automatically optimize practical utility. ... practical relevance does not by itself establish the epistemic value of knowledge. ... Epistemic Value != Practical Utility.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts from the anthology's curiosity/attention and pragmatic-encroachment chapters the candidate distinctions Attention != Value != Truth and Epistemic Value != Practical Utility, warning that the existing Epistemic Agency dimension-selection formula must not silently optimize practical utility as if it were epistemic value, and connecting this to the already-established EU != EpistemicQuality caution in the Expected Utility work.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the swamping problem ... If truth already gives a belief its epistemic value, why does adding reliability, justification, or another property give it additional value? ... some components may be derivationally or normatively parasitic on others. That resembles our anti-double-counting principle
a_rows_sample.statement: Draws an explicit structural analogy between the philosophical 'swamping problem' (does adding reliability/justification to an already-true belief add genuine additional value, or is it parasitic on truth) and the corpus's own kernel-minimality question (which capabilities are genuinely irreducible), warning against summing K=Truth+Evidence+Reliability+Justification+... without checking for derivational/normative parasitism, consistent with the existing anti-double-counting discipline.

a_rows_sample.anchor: we should not build KnowledgeOS around a single scalar Knowledge Quality ... V_epi(K) = (V_truth, V_just, V_reliability, V_understanding, V_explanatory, V_inquiry, ...) ... fits our previous rejection of scalar cancellation in Zero Algebra.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a candidate vector-valued epistemic-value assessment V_epi(K)=(V_truth,V_just,V_reliability,V_understanding,V_explanatory,V_inquiry,...) with dimensions left open, explicitly rejecting a single scalar Knowledge Quality, consistent with the corpus's prior rejection of scalar cancellation in Zero Algebra; also states False Model does not imply Zero Epistemic Value, and Useful Model does not imply Truth, extending the existing Model!=Truth, Fit!=Validity, Understanding!=Knowledge chain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KR-EPISTEMIC-VALUE-LENS-2026-09 ... EV1 ... Is epistemic value distinct from epistemic correctness? ... EV10 ... Does epistemic value depend on context/purpose without making truth itself context-relative? ... Epistemic Success, Explanatory/Understanding Success, Practical/Action Success ... They can correlate. They can also diverge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes KR-EPISTEMIC-VALUE-LENS-2026-09 with ten research questions EV1-EV10 (epistemic value vs correctness, knowledge vs understanding, explanatory structure representability, reliability-independent-of-truth value, non-scalar value, value-vs-inquiry-selection, value-vs-action-utility, process-attributable success, false/idealized models retaining value, context-dependent value without relativizing truth), concluding with the strongest preliminary hypothesis that KnowledgeOS eventually needs three distinguishable notions of success (Epistemic, Explanatory/Understanding, Practical/Action) that can correlate or diverge; explicitly [EXT]->[PROP]->[EXP]->[NEG] only, no promotion into Theory v1.2.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemic Outcome != Epistemic Process ... Value(State) and Value(Process) ... Same conclusion. Different epistemic achievement. ... Epistemic Success = Outcome Quality + Process Attribution. But that equation is not established. It is a research hypothesis.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the omission of Value(State) vs Value(Process) (Goldman/Olsson reliabilism): two findings with the identical conclusion ('GitLab Runner caused the egress') can differ in epistemic achievement depending on whether the process involved independent validated multi-hypothesis investigation or a single misleading log, giving Epistemic Outcome != Epistemic Process and the unestablished candidate hypothesis Epistemic Success = Outcome Quality + Process Attribution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: context of discovery ... context of the final product ... Value(E | Discovery) != Value(E | FinalState). ... A clue that is enormously valuable while searching can become redundant after determination.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Kusch's context-of-discovery vs context-of-final-product distinction, proposing that evidence value can depend on the stage of inquiry, Value(E|Discovery) != Value(E|FinalState), so KnowledgeOS should not treat evidence as having a timeless scalar value -- directly relevant to Fact-Finding and Zoom-In.

a_rows_sample.anchor: knowledge as a collective good ... K_t^collective ... Is KnowledgeOS fundamentally an individual epistemic system, or a distributed/collective epistemic system?
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Kusch's social/collective account of knowledge (informant, inquirer, social institution of testimony) as motivating the open question whether KnowledgeOS is fundamentally an individual epistemic system or a distributed/collective one, proposing a candidate K_t^collective spanning agents, sources, testimony, validation, and shared state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the concept of knowledge economically packages multiple valuable properties. He compares it to a Swiss Army knife ... Is KnowledgeOS a semantic compression/packaging mechanism? ... connects directly to our representation reduction research.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Weiner's 'Swiss Army knife' analogy (knowledge is valuable because it economically packages multiple valuable properties rather than adding a mysterious extra value) as motivating the research hypothesis that KnowledgeOS's Knowledge State representation might function as a semantic compression/packaging mechanism (KnowledgeState=Package(Truth,Evidence,Standing,Provenance,Context,...)), connecting to the existing representation-reduction research and the Adequacy != Minimality != Q-equivalence distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: value pluralism ... the values need not themselves all be epistemic -- they can be pragmatic, moral, aesthetic, etc. ... context-relativity of value does not imply context-relativity of truth.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Baehr's value-pluralism reframing (ask the full range of ways an epistemic state can be valuable, rather than whether knowledge scalarly exceeds true belief) to reject a premature additive V_epi(K)=V_truth+V_justification+V_understanding, proposing instead Value(K,Q,C,P)->V_possible with values potentially epistemic, pragmatic, moral, or aesthetic, while explicitly preserving that context-relativity of value does not imply context-relativity of truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: epistemic judgments contain a special kind of 'should', a binding/reason-giving character, rather than merely a calculation of which belief best achieves some goal. ... Epistemic Norm != Utility Function ... Epistemic 'Should' != Practical 'Should'.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Grimm's argument that epistemic normativity is not reducible to teleological goal-promotion, giving Epistemic Norm != Utility Function and Epistemic 'Should' != Practical 'Should', requiring KR-EXPECTED-UTILITY to remain downstream of epistemic assessment rather than silently defining epistemic rationality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Which goods are actually capable of motivating belief? ... Reason to Believe != Reason to Investigate != Reason to Act.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Jones's evidentialist/pragmatist question of which goods can motivate belief (as opposed to motivating action to acquire a belief), giving the three-way separation Reason to Believe != Reason to Investigate != Reason to Act, directly relevant to Epistemic Agency and Action Fact-Finding.

a_rows_sample.anchor: an ugly/complex analysis of a valuable concept does not show that the concept itself lacks value ... Complex formalization not-implies Bad epistemic architecture ... Elegant minimal formalization not-implies Correct epistemic theory ... semantic minimality != syntactic minimality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts DePaul's 'ugly analysis' lesson (a complicated analysis of a valuable concept does not undermine the concept's value) as a methodological warning for kernel minimality: Complex formalization does not imply Bad epistemic architecture, and Elegant minimal formalization does not imply Correct epistemic theory, reinforcing semantic minimality != syntactic minimality -- the kernel must not be chosen merely because it is mathematically prettier.

a_rows_sample.anchor: understanding can be a relation to a comprehensive, coherent body of commitments ... Knowledge Element versus Understanding Structure. The latter is not just a larger set of Knowledge Elements. It is a relational organization.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Kvanvig/Elgin's account of understanding as relational organization (not merely a larger set of propositions) to propose Knowledge Element vs Understanding Structure as a candidate distinction relevant to the Knowledge Graph research; and extracts Elgin's felicitous-falsehoods thesis (idealizations can support scientific understanding while remaining literally false, provided the theory stays answerable to evidence) to give Understanding != Factive Knowledge and False component does not imply the entire explanatory structure is worthless.

a_rows_sample.anchor: understanding involves not merely possessing information, but an ability to use it -- reason with it, apply it, generate hypotheses from it, and assess its limits. ... EpistemicCapability(K_t): What can the system actually do with what it knows?
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Elgin's ability-to-use dimension of understanding to propose EpistemicCapability(K_t) as distinct from KnowledgeState(K_t), asking what the system can actually do with what it knows, potentially important for the 60-capability catalogue work; also extracts Riggs's control/attribution anti-luck account giving Outcome != Epistemic Achievement (a correct answer by luck differs in epistemic status from a correct answer through controlled process) and a candidate 'degrees of understanding' UnderstandingProfile(Q) rather than a scalar.

a_rows_sample.anchor: value can be relational rather than intrinsic ... Value(K_t | Q,C,P,S) is a much more promising research object. ... seven research primitives ... EV-1 Epistemic Outcome ... EV-7 Social/Collective Epistemic Value ... this is a research map, not Theory v1.3.
a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the second-pass reading into seven candidate research primitives (EV-1 Epistemic Outcome, EV-2 Epistemic Process, EV-3 Epistemic Achievement, EV-4 Understanding Structure, EV-5 Epistemic Norm, EV-6 Value Relation, EV-7 Social/Collective Epistemic Value) and a revised value-as-relation formula Value(K_t|Q,C,P,S), presenting a research-map architecture (Epistemic State->Truth/Justification/Reliability->Determination->Knowledge/Understanding/Model->Epistemic Value->Inquiry/Social/Practical Value->Agency->Action) explicitly not Theory v1.3.

a_rows_sample.anchor: THE SEVEN EPISTEMIC RESEARCH PRIMITIVES ... EV-1: Epistemic Outcome ... EV-7: Collective Infrastructure ... KR-EPISTEMIC-ACHIEVEMENT-LENS-2026-09 ... EA1-EA14
a_rows_sample.statement: Maps the seven EV-1..EV-7 primitives to concrete KnowledgeOS system-mechanics interpretations and registers KR-EPISTEMIC-ACHIEVEMENT-LENS-2026-09 (status [EXT][PROP], prerequisite KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-01) with an expanded fourteen-question research ledger EA1-EA14 spanning process attribution, inquiry-stage value, collective infrastructure, packaging, value-as-relation, norm/utility decoupling, reason-type separation, and understanding representation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The book gives us distinctions and research questions; it does not give KnowledgeOS metrics, operators, or invariants. ... remove 'anti-luck score' ... The book gives us a philosophical problem ... It does not give us a KnowledgeOS scoring function.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the key governance principle for the whole Epistemic Value lens: the book gives distinctions and research questions, not KnowledgeOS metrics, operators, or invariants; on this basis removes EV-3's invented 'anti-luck score'/'ability control measure' since the source supports only the research question of process attribution, not a scoring function, and downgrades all seven primitives from implied artifacts to [EXT][PROP] research directions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EV-1 needs one correction ... F_t = Determination and K_t = Knowledge State. A determination can contribute to a state, but they are not the same object. ... F_t != K_t.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects EV-1's grouping of 'the static determination F_t, claim, or state K_t reached' (conflating two distinct objects) to F_t != K_t, redefining EV-1 as the epistemic result reached by an inquiry (a determination, assessment, commitment, or attributed epistemic state), strengthening rather than weakening the source's contribution to existing theory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: NextEpistemicAct(K_t,Q_t,Delta_t,R_t,Pi) ... a_t in {Clarify, Search, Observe, ConsultResource, AssessEvidence, Determine, Defer, Act}. ... EA1..EA7
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a four-layer Epistemic Agency Execution Loop (front-end interaction; gap detection & classification via K_t|=Q; epistemic agency selection via a*=argmax[ExpectedGapReduction/(Cost+Risk)]; determination & output) and seven hypotheses EA1-EA7: EA1 observation!=interpretation; EA2 intent as unconfirmed hypothesis; EA3 typed gap resolution over {Semantic,Epistemic,...}; EA4 epistemic action optimization a*=argmax[E[DeltaRed]/Cost]; EA5 resource-bounded actions A_t=Filter(A,Resources_t); EA6 Lord/Sarathi duality (generate vs select); EA7 Determine(Evidence) before Act.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t |= Q ... This notation is dangerous. ... Adeq(K_t,Q,C,EC,S,R) ... or Determine(K_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R) ... should not become a new KnowledgeOS primitive. Use the existing vocabulary.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the dangerous overloading of logical entailment notation K_t|=Q (which normally means semantic entailment, much stronger than intended) to the existing Adequacy/Determination vocabulary Adeq(K_t,Q,C,EC,S,R) or Determine(K_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R), so as not to introduce a redundant new primitive, consistent with the established Determination!=Knowledge and Adequacy!=Determination!=Knowledge distinctions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Delta_t in {Semantic, Epistemic, Resource, Policy} ... I would not call these the four gap types yet ... ClassifyGap: Delta_Q -> G where G is itself still research-open.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects freezing the four-way gap taxonomy {Semantic,Epistemic,Resource,Policy} as exhaustive; recommends Delta_Q(K_t) as a typed collection of unsatisfied requirements with a ClassifyGap:Delta_Q->G mapping where G remains research-open, illustrated by four metro-scenario gap readings (inquiry gap, knowledge gap, resource gap, decision/policy gap).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Gap -> Opportunity -> Decision -> Authorization -> Execution ... Proposal != Decision != Authorization != Action. That distinction should remain intact.
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates four conflated concerns in the original design (what is missing, what can be done, what should be done, what is allowed) into an explicit chain Delta_t -> A_t^possible -> A_t^feasible -> a_t* -> Authorization(a_t*) -> Execute(a_t*), preserving the existing Proposal!=Decision!=Authorization!=Action distinction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: a_t^* = argmax_{a in A_t^feasible} EU(a|K_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t) ... KnowledgeOS should not assume that epistemic information gain is always the objective.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects EA4's argmax[E[DeltaRed]/Cost] formula as an insufficient decision rule (pure info-gain/cost could select an unsafe action, and sometimes not acting is optimal), generalizing to a_t*=argmax EU(a|K_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t) without freezing the exact utility formula, and abstracting the capability as NextEpistemicAct:(K_t,Q_t,Delta_t,R_t,C_t,EC_t)->A_t to be determined experimentally.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Resource_t(r) = (Avail,Quality,Cost,Risk,Latency,Authority,...) ... Feasible(a|R_t,C_t,EC_t) becomes meaningful.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects EA5's simple Filter(A,Resources_t) model to a richer per-resource state Resource_t(r)=(Availability,Quality,Cost,Risk,Latency,Authority,...), making Feasible(a|R_t,C_t,EC_t) meaningful and connecting to the existing evidence-channel work.

b_rows_sample.anchor: unless your actual observation included a specified probability model, that inequality is not established. Likewise "maintaining eye contact" was not part of the original factual description. ... Never move directly O -> P(H) without specifying the inference model.
b_rows_sample.statement: Flags that the worked human trace contains invented (unobserved) details treated as facts (e.g. an unstated probability inequality, 'maintaining eye contact', 'language barrier'), violating the very Observation!=Interpretation discipline KnowledgeOS is meant to enforce; recommends explicitly labeling O(observed)/I(interpretation)/H(hypothesis)/P(probability output) and never moving directly from O to P(H) without a specified inference model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q_0 -> Clarification -> Q_1 -> Clarification -> Q_2 ... until WellFormed(Q_n,C) and only then Gap(Q_n,K_t). ... Inquiry Formation ... distinct from Inquiry Resolution.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the pipeline with a multi-cycle Inquiry Formation stage (Q0->Clarification->Q1->...->WellFormed(Q_n,C)) preceding gap analysis, explicitly distinguished from Inquiry Resolution; illustrated by the metro example needing a follow-up clarifying question ('Where are you going?') before the direction question is answerable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Determine(Evidence) BEFORE Act. ... I would not make this universal. ... Required epistemic determination precedes authorized operational action, when the action contract requires determination.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects EA7 (universal Determine-before-Act) by distinguishing three action classes (epistemic actions like search/inspect/ask which may precede determination; operational actions requiring determination+authorization; safety/emergency actions taken under uncertainty), giving the conditional rule 'required epistemic determination precedes authorized operational action, when the action contract requires determination', preserving Epistemic Decision != Operational Decision != Authorization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: a metaphor can expose a structure without proving that the metaphor names an architectural component. ... [PROP] Lord/Sarathi is an interpretive naming lens for the two functions; not a canonical architectural name.
b_rows_sample.statement: Demotes EA6's Lord/Sarathi naming to CandidateGenerator(K_t,Delta_t,R_t)->A_t and ActionSelector(K_t,Delta_t,A_t,C_t,EC_t)->a_t, tagging Lord/Sarathi as merely [PROP] interpretive naming, invoking the prior Gita governance lesson that a metaphor can expose a structure without naming an architectural component.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Does epistemic action selection expose a capability that cannot be semantically derived from the existing theory under the frozen contract? ... A new primitive is admissible only if it changes the semantic contract, exposes a required capability absent from the current model, or defeats an existing irreducibility result.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the kernel question from 'should Epistemic Agency become a kernel operator' to 'does epistemic action selection expose a capability that cannot be semantically derived from the existing theory under the frozen contract', restating the standing rule that a new primitive is admissible only if it changes the semantic contract, exposes a required absent capability, or defeats an existing irreducibility result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation equivalence not-implies Intent equivalence ... Good action selection not-implies Correct knowledge ... Resource availability not-implies Resource reliability.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a controlled factorial benchmark (fixed K_t,Q,Delta while varying resources R_t across cases A-D, then epistemic standards/risk/inquiry across cases E-G, expecting A*_A!=A*_B!=A*_C!=A*_D when resources materially differ) plus two adversarial experiments: a 'wrong assumption' test with four worlds sharing an identical observation but different underlying intent, giving Observation equivalence does not imply Intent equivalence; and a 'wrong resource' test where good action selection leads to a wrong search result, giving Good action selection does not imply Correct knowledge and Resource availability does not imply Resource reliability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EU(a) = E[U_gap(a)] - C_resource(a) - Omega_risk(a) + U_task(a) ... the additive form is not theoretically established. ... EU = F(U_gap,C,Omega,U_task) as the general specification, and treat the additive version as [PROP] EU_additive.
b_rows_sample.statement: The draft's additive four-term utility decomposition EU(a)=E[U_gap(a)]-C_resource(a)-Omega_risk(a)+U_task(a) is corrected to a general (unestablished-form) specification EU=F(U_gap,C,Omega,U_task), with the additive version relegated to [PROP] EU_additive pending experimental validation, since e.g. risk may interact with epistemic benefit rather than subtract independently.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ||Delta_Q(K_t)||_G ... This is currently underdefined ... These don't naturally form a vector space. ... U_gap(a) = V(Delta_t,Delta_{t+1}^a; Q,C,EC,S) where V is a candidate gap-value/reduction function.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects assuming a generic norm ||Delta||_G over the gap space, since typed gaps (missing value, missing dimension, contradiction, insufficient evidence, unobservable quantity, underdetermination, model insufficiency, semantic ambiguity) do not naturally form a vector space; replaces it with a general candidate gap-value/reduction function U_gap(a)=V(Delta_t,Delta_{t+1}^a;Q,C,EC,S), with an actual metric d(Delta_t,Delta_{t+1}) introduced only if experiments establish a numerical structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reduction != Validation != Determination != Knowledge ... U_gap must not silently become KnowledgeGain. I recommend the term Expected Gap Resolution Value rather than Expected Epistemic Value
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues raw gap-cardinality reduction (|Delta_{t+1}|<|Delta_t|) does not imply epistemic improvement, via a worked example (3 hypotheses reduced to 1 surviving hypothesis that is false), extending Reduction!=Validation!=Determination!=Knowledge; recommends renaming 'Expected Epistemic Value' to 'Expected Gap Resolution Value' to prevent gap reduction being silently equated with knowledge gain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: rho(a) * E[DeltaRed] ... This risks double counting ... E[U(a)] = sum_o P(o|a,K_t,M) U(a,o) where reliability belongs in the observation/evidence model
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the draft's reliability multiplier rho(a)*E[DeltaRed] as risking double-counting reliability (since it may already shape the observation distribution P(O|a,K)); recommends the cleaner E[U(a)]=sum_o P(o|a,K_t,M)U(a,o), moving resource reliability into the observation/evidence model P(O|a,R_t,...) instead.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Constraint != Preference. ... PrivacyViolation(a)=1 may mean a not-in A^feasible rather than EU(a)-1000. ... A^safe = {a: P(harm|a) <= epsilon} and only then a* = argmax_{a in A^safe} EU(a).
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the draft's treatment of safety/risk as a soft utility penalty (Omega_risk subtracted, beta(R_t) scaling) to a hard feasibility constraint where appropriate: Constraint != Preference, e.g. a privacy violation should remove an action from A^feasible rather than merely penalize its utility, giving A^safe={a: P(harm|a)<=epsilon} filtered before a*=argmax_{a in A^safe}EU(a); likewise the draft's 'high-precision mode' weight adjustment is reframed as a hard safety constraint rather than a mere utility-weight change.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EU(a1) approx EU(a2) does not mean a1 equiv_sem a2. So I would call it: candidate deterministic tie-break policy not: selection invariant.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the draft's tie-breaking rule (favor lower latency when utilities are approximately equal) from a 'selection invariant' to a 'candidate deterministic tie-break policy', noting approximately-equal expected utility does not imply semantic equivalence of the two actions, and that the tie-break policy should itself be configurable under the active decision regime.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Stop or NoFurtherInvestigation ... Suppose Adeq(K_t,Q,...) = True. Continuing to investigate can have negative utility. ... This prevents KnowledgeOS from becoming an agent that always searches.
b_rows_sample.statement: Adds a Stop/NoFurtherInvestigation candidate action to the action set A^possible, so that once Adeq(K_t,Q,...)=True continuing investigation can legitimately have negative utility and EU(Stop) can win, preventing KnowledgeOS from becoming an agent that always searches.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Agreement(Selection,Validation) not-implies Truth. ... ActionDecisionRecord_t containing at minimum: Inquiry, Current Knowledge State, Typed Gap, Candidate Actions, Resource States, Feasibility Results, Utility Model, Utility Parameters, Risk Policy, Selected Action, Rejected Alternatives, Decision Reason, Authorization.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a counterfactual-action-quality experiment (estimate P(Adeq(K_{t+1}^a,Q)=1 | K_t,Q,R_t) for every candidate action and compare to the selected action, using a candidate Regret(a)=U(a*)-U(a) or outcome proxies) and an adversarial reliability test giving Agreement(Selection,Validation) does not imply Truth; requires an ActionDecisionRecord_t (inquiry, state, typed gap, candidates, resource states, feasibility, utility model/parameters, risk policy, selected action, rejected alternatives, decision reason, authorization) for inspectability.

a_notations: Epistemic State != Epistemic Quality != Epistemic Value != Practical Value
a_aliases: Epistemic Value (ed. Haddock, Millar, Pritchard) as a KnowledgeOS research lens
b_aliases: From Knowledge State to Next Epistemic Act

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 3 separate times across the corpus

b_rows_sample.anchor: Established (4) -- the EKS/PKS/AIP synthesis rows
b_rows_sample.statement: Register census, Established rows: INV-001 Evidence != Authority; INV-002 Observation != Decision; INV-003 Assessment != Authority; INV-004 Projection != Source -- all registered at UM-24 settle, validation state Established, lineage HPA synthesis INV-001..004, validated cross-system tier-1/2.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Family 3 -- AUTHORITY (Who/What may authorize?)
b_rows_sample.statement: Family 3 (AUTHORITY) table: INV-003 Assessment != Authority (ESTABLISHED, forbids Assessment->Authority; an instance of Relation-001); Authority-as-Recorded-Reference (C-1, STRONG landscape row -- EKS grant 126/126 humanActRef, PKS Charter G-17, AIP grant G-2/R5b -- 'the record references a human act; it never manufactures authority'; forbids Record->Authority; whether this landscape row is SAME or RELATED to the register's authority rows across systems is UNKNOWN, U-02).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Landscape integration -- which EKS/PKS/AIP responsibilities already exist, and where their boundaries lie
b_rows_sample.statement: Nine landscape findings (C-1..C-10 evidence) mapped onto the register, with F2/F3/F4 carry-forwards honored (implemented mechanism != domain ownership; evidence is current-state-scoped not universal; consumption != ownership != KnowledgeOS): state-as-fold/append-only log (C-2, SAME as Revisability-001's enforcement, mechanism layer); forward-only supersession (C-5, SAME as Revisability-001, asymmetric ownership PKS-governance/EKS-mechanism/AIP-declared-only); closed-verdict vocabulary (C-3, SAME as the Validation Layer, a published-language boundary); assessment-conferring-no-authority (C-4, SAME as INV-003 Established); epistemic-class discipline (C-8, SAME as Pramana-001's source-role separation, PKS-owned, asymmetric F3); regenerable non-authoritative projection (C-7, SAME as INV-004 Established); honest-UNKNOWN (C-10, SAME as H-ZERO-001, 'discipline, not mechanism'); authority-as-recorded-reference (C-1, SAME as the Authority family's core, X-02 SAME-vs-RELATED across systems UNKNOWN/U-02); the F4 relationship question (AIP is DISTINCT -- a consumer/runtime, not the owner, not the KnowledgeOS layer itself).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Family 2.3 Authority family and 2.4 Transformation family
b_rows_sample.statement: INV-003 STRONG (C-4, ESTABLISHED) -> KERNEL(established), SURVIVES (law 3). Transformation family: INV-002 STRONG (ESTABLISHED) -> KERNEL(established), SURVIVES (law 4); INV-004 STRONG (C-7, ESTABLISHED) -> KERNEL(established), SURVIVES (law 5); INV-KOS-001 STRONG (SS31 score-collapse) -> KERNEL, SURVIVES (law 2, the general anti-collapse law whose named instances are INV-001..004 + Expression!=Meaning + Observation!=Inference); H-KOS-NonInterference-001 MODERATE (ruled OVERLAPPING with INV-KOS-001) -> KERNEL, SURVIVES/CONSOLIDATE into law 2; INV-KOS-Revisability-001 STRONG (C-2/C-5) -> KERNEL, SURVIVES (law 11, folding in the Temporal family); INV-KOS-Decision-001 STRONG (the decision-collapse target) -> KERNEL, SURVIVES (law 4).

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'INV-003'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Canonical concept glossary — the 14 examined, plus 3 the corpus forces in
a_rows_sample.statement: A 17-row glossary assigns each term (KnowledgeOS, PKS, Engineering Knowledge, Engineering Capability, Engineering Method, Engineering Governance, Engineering Runtime, Runtime Adapter, Engineering Evidence, Engineering Ontology, Documentation Ontology L-A, Platform Ontology L-B, Product Ontology L-C, Knowledge Graph, Engineering Kernel, Knowledge Space, Design Policy DP-n, Execution Asset AST-nnn) one meaning, owner, protected invariant, place, and verdict (KEEP/REJECTED-MERGED/SPLIT/CANDIDATE). Success criterion: every major engineering term gets one meaning, one owner, one place.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Engineering Evidence | not one thing ... SPLIT stands: Evidence Protocol (platform) ∕ Evidence Records (product)
a_rows_sample.statement: 'Engineering Evidence' is not one thing; it splits into Evidence Protocol (platform-level, ES-006.1/.4, owner Decision Authority) and Evidence Records (product-level, owner 'the producing track', append-only).

a_rows_sample.anchor: D-6 · Engineering Evidence — SPLITS. It is not one domain ... The boundary runs THROUGH the concept, not around it
a_rows_sample.statement: D-6, Engineering Evidence, splits into two domains: D-6a Evidence Protocol (ES-006.4 harvest question, ES-006.1 ladder, Observation Protocol with a clock, saturation gate; owner KnowledgeOS, reusable, a hospital project inherits it entirely) and D-6b Product Evidence (106 reports, session logs, CAP-001 §9 rows; owner the producing product, never reusable). The split is not inference but canon's own stated ownership ('the producing track; consumed by DA') — a single owner cannot be both the producing track and the platform. D-6a has 0 traversals: a bounded context that has never executed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Does the folder structure follow the model? THE SAME MISFIT, NOW DERIVED FROM MEANING RATHER THAN FROM A GREP ... it also exposes D-6b (product records inside engineering/), which no vocabulary search could find
a_rows_sample.statement: Assessing folder-to-model fit last (as commissioned): D-1 Governance follows the model; D-2 Method does not (sits in docs/architecture/design/, a PRODUCT path, the model's largest misfit); D-3 Runtime is split (mount correct, model product-side); D-5 Capability split; D-6a follows; D-6b is inverted (product records inside the platform tree, engineering/verification/); D-7 split across two roots. The domain-model reasoning (asking who owns the knowledge) reaches further than a vocabulary grep: it also exposes D-6b's misplacement, which no vocabulary search could find since records contain no methodology terms at all — demonstrating that the model had to precede the index.

a_rows_sample.anchor: O-1..O-24 (repository facts — no interpretation)
a_rows_sample.statement: 24 repository observations are recorded, each traced to a source artifact and kept strictly separate from interpretation. Key ones: O-1/O-2/O-3/O-4 (a 'Platform != product' table already classifies KnowledgeOS as potential product, Supporting Subdomain, and states the product binds the platform, never forks it); O-9 (an observed promotion model, itself a candidate for promotion); O-12 (Operational Evidence's owner recorded as 'the producing track; consumed by DA', lifecycle append-only, never edited); O-13 (a standing STOP forbidding a context map until operational evidence and an ARB ruling exist); O-16..O-18 (the Product Discovery Charter's five gated stages, PROPOSED status, one retrospective data point/zero market data points); O-20 (cross-product-research resolves to PENDING, no root); O-21 (CAP-001's Domain/Application/Shared contain zero repository knowledge); O-24 (CAP-001's evidence record holds four rows, zero tool executions, zero decisions changed).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate Strategic Responsibilities ... The one responsibility the litmus splits is Evidence & Learning — and canon already splits it the same way
a_rows_sample.statement: Six candidate responsibility clusters tested against the litmus ('would this exist if PublicDigit vanished?'): Governance, Decisions, Execution, Verification are all platform-side; Evidence & Learning splits (the mechanism yes, the evidence no — a hospital project would inherit the protocol and none of the observations); Knowledge (research-frozen theory) is platform-side but research-frozen. PKS content, CAP-001's register configs, and R-nn/PMR-nn register contents would not survive PublicDigit's disappearance and are product-specific.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Lifecycle — what produces what ... Two of nine links are observed inside the platform. The chain is a destination, not a pipeline
a_rows_sample.statement: Of nine proposed lifecycle links (Platform Domains->Platform Ontology, Platform Ontology->Documentation Ontology, Documentation Ontology->Knowledge Graph, Documentation Ontology->Indexes, Knowledge Graph->PKS, PKS->Runtime Context, Runtime->Software, Software->Evidence, Evidence->Platform), only two are observed (Documentation Ontology->Knowledge Graph and ->Indexes); one (Knowledge Graph->PKS) is falsified since PKS artifacts are authored/accepted, not derived; Evidence->Platform is empty with 0 traversals. The chain is a destination, not an observed pipeline.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SP-5 · Operational Learning — NOT MISSING. DISPERSED, NAMED, AND NEVER ONCE EXERCISED ... What is missing is not a domain. It is a single traversal
a_rows_sample.statement: The commission's claim that Operational Learning is a missing strategic product is refined: the machinery is not missing, it is already governed in six places (Operational Evidence as a candidate aggregate root; the ES-006.4 harvest question; the ES-006.1 promotion ladder; the observed promotion model of Reference Model section 7.2; the Observation Protocol; Pattern Cards + Pattern Evidence Register). What is missing is not a domain but a single traversal — EAD-1: 'no evidence has flowed from PublicDigit to PKS, the arrow has never been traversed'. Naming SP-5 as a new strategic domain would not make evidence flow, it would give a non-functioning mechanism a better title.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Several fields distinguish: Observation, Evidence, Claim, Inference, Belief, Decision ... especially: Truth Maintenance Systems, Belief Revision, Argumentation Systems
a_rows_sample.statement: Epistemic-systems research (Truth Maintenance Systems, Belief Revision, Argumentation Systems) separates Observation (data received), Evidence (supporting material), Claim (proposition), Inference (derived proposition), Belief (accepted proposition), and Decision (authorized commitment) as six distinct roles that should not be conflated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: causal inference can be strengthened by linking statistical analysis to qualitative knowledge, and that qualitative evidence can help refute old ideas, develop new ones and test them.
a_rows_sample.statement: Qualitative evidence must be legitimate evidence, not automatically dominated by quantitative data (attributed to the book's Chapter 20); Evidence taxonomy expanded from numeric-only to quantitative/qualitative/documentary/observational/experimental/experiential/expert/computational, each with provenance and authority.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KNOWLEDGEOS ... OBSERVATIONS/SOURCES -> EVIDENCE -> QUALITATIVE/QUANTITATIVE -> INFERENCE -> ASSUMPTIONS/RIVAL EXPLANATIONS/MECHANISMS -> VALIDATION/TESTING -> IDENTIFICATION STATUS -> CLAIM -> SUPPORTED/INCONCLUSIVE
a_rows_sample.statement: Synthesized whole-book epistemic architecture diagram chaining Observations/Sources -> Evidence -> {Qualitative, Quantitative} -> Inference -> {Assumptions, Rival Explanations, Mechanisms} -> Validation/Testing -> Identification Status -> Claim -> {Supported, Inconclusive}, described as 'a very strong conceptual model.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Qualitative evidence is legitimate evidence when appropriately sourced and contextualized.
a_rows_sample.statement: Invariant 8: Qualitative evidence is legitimate evidence when appropriately sourced and contextualized.

a_rows_sample.anchor: combine multiple independent classifiers or evidence-producing mechanisms ... Do not blindly average evidence. Evidence sources have different authority, independence, provenance, freshness, correlation.
a_rows_sample.statement: KOS-14 Ensemble Evidence / Evidence Fusion: combine multiple independent evidence-producing sources (data fusion, majority voting, Bayesian fusion, stacked generalisation, mixture of experts, bagging, boosting, random forests, model averaging) but explicitly warns against blindly averaging evidence, proposing EvidenceIndependence/EvidenceAuthority/EvidenceCorrelation/EvidenceWeight as needed model fields.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DemonicCycle(K_t) = Attachment(K_t) > 0 ∧ Confidence(K_t) > Evidence(K_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a formal failure condition for epistemic 'demonic cycle': Attachment(K_t)>0 AND Confidence(K_t)>Evidence(K_t), i.e. miscalibration where stated confidence exceeds the evidence that supports it, mapped to the Gita's cycle of greed/pride/dissatisfaction (16.13-15).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Quality(Evidence) ∈ {Sattva, Rajas, Tamas} ... Quality(Assessment) ∈ {Sattva, Rajas, Tamas} ... Quality(Discipline) ∈ {Sattva, Rajas, Tamas} ... Quality(KnowledgeSharing) ∈ {Sattva, Rajas, Tamas}
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies a uniform three-valued quality classification (Sattva=high-quality/unbiased/selfless, Rajas=emotionally-charged/self-serving/status-driven, Tamas=low-quality/biased/harmful) across four distinct KnowledgeOS dimensions: evidence, assessment, discipline, and knowledge-sharing — each treated as an instance of the same generic Quality(X) function.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t^decayed = K_0 · e^{-λt}

b_rows_sample.anchor: C1. step-001 (140653) -- Operational Independence ... Ind_rho(e_i,e_j,G,C) -> {Independent,Dependent,Unknown} ... section15 the statistical correction: OperationallyIndependent does-not-imply StatisticallyIndependent
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-001 (file 140653) formalizes Operational Independence: Ind_rho(e_i,e_j,G,C) -> {Independent, Dependent, Unknown}, where G is a provenance/dependency graph, C is context, rho is an independence policy; a deterministic rule (a chain relation between two evidence items forces Dependent, 'no LLM required'); a common-ancestor relation implies independence is normally Unknown, not Confirmed; different sources do not imply independence; a six-component independence evidence vector I(e_i,e_j)=(i_S,i_A,i_P,i_M,i_T,i_C) (source/acquisition/provenance/method/temporal independence plus common-ancestor status) each valued in {Confirmed,Rejected,Unknown}, explicitly refusing a scalar IndependenceScore because it 'would obscure why'; states the law 'Independence must be established, not assumed'; and adds a critical statistical correction: operationally-established independence does not imply statistical independence, so Bayesian multiplication's requirement P(E1,E2|H)=P(E1|H)P(E2|H) is a separate, stronger condition -- 'exactly why Evidence Architecture and Statistical Inference Policy must remain separate.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: C2. step-002 (140919) -- Evidence Identity / Equivalence Calculus ... Identity != Semantic Equivalence != Same Observation != Independence. Five relations section5 ... section4 critical invariant: Semantic equivalence must NOT imply deduplication.
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-002 (file 140919) opens with Identity != Semantic Equivalence != Same Observation != Independence and formalizes five relations between evidence items: same-evidence-object (=_I), same-proposition (=_P), same-underlying-observation (=_O), dependency (prec, e2 produced using e1), and operational independence under policy rho (perp_rho); states the critical invariant that semantic equivalence must NOT imply deduplication; works seven cases including 'different values, same observation' yielding a DERIVATION_CONFLICT status distinguishing independent-observation-count from derived-interpretation-count; builds a multi-relational lineage graph G_E=(V,L_1..L_n) with typed edge sets (DerivedFrom, ExtractedFrom, TransformedFrom, SummarizedFrom, CopiedFrom, ObservedFrom, ReviewedFrom); states CommonCause != SameObservation and CommonCause != AutomaticDependence; argues the corpus's eight relationship labels (IDENTICAL, SAME_OBSERVATION, DERIVED, SEMANTICALLY_EQUIVALENT, COMMON_SOURCE, INDEPENDENT, CONTRADICTORY, UNKNOWN) should not collapse into a single enum since they coexist; and distinguishes a fact about provenance from an inference about provenance, warning KnowledgeOS should never silently promote the second into the first.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C3. step-003 (141118) -- Evidence Assessment Algebra ... EA=(S+,S-,U,Q,V,D,X,Pi) ... Notice what is not here: Truth. ... section4 Aggregation must occur after normalization ... section12 not every useful assessment is monotonic
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-003 (file 141118) defines the Evidence Assessment tuple EA=(S+,S-,U,Q,V,D,X,Pi) -- Supporting, Opposing, Uncertainty, Quality, Validity/temporal, Dependency, Context/applicability, Provenance -- explicitly noting Truth is absent from the tuple; refuses S=S+-S- as an aggregate since '0.9 minus 0.8 does not mean 0.1' (there is substantial evidence on both sides); requires aggregation to occur only after a normalization step N_rho handling identity/provenance/semantic/relevance/temporal/dependency/polarity resolution; distinguishes Quality!=Relevance, Reliability!=Validity, ProvenanceQuality!=SourceAuthority; introduces an aggregation equivalence class [e]_~O (same underlying observation aggregated once unless policy states otherwise); and corrects a naive monotonicity claim: not every useful assessment is monotonic -- SupportAggregation may be monotonic with respect to additional supporting evidence while a CompleteAssessment need not be, seeding closure-04a's signed monotonicity and step-004's axiom 6. Establishes the chain Evidence->Assessment->Conclusion->Decision (never Evidence->Decision directly) and four bounded contexts (Evidence/Assessment/Knowledge/Decision Context).

b_rows_sample.anchor: C4. step-004 (142250) -- The Evidence Aggregation Axioms ... Axioms 1-16 ... section19 kernel invariants A1-A4 ... vs policy properties A5-A8. section20 the Evidence Constitution E-K1...E-K10 ... section21 nine-framework comparison table ... There is probably no single universal KnowledgeOS evidence algebra.
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-004 (file 142250) states 16 evidence-aggregation axioms: (1) Determinism (LLM variability != epistemic randomness), (2) permutation invariance, (3) duplicate invariance ('This should be a kernel invariant'), (4) derived-evidence non-inflation, (5) irrelevance invariance, (6) supporting monotonicity with three qualifiers (admissible, independent, supporting evidence) and an explicit disclaimer that it scopes only the S+/S- components, never the final conclusion, (7) contradiction preservation, (8) conflict sensitivity, (9) dependency sensitivity, (10) unknown dependency stays unknown, (11) corroboration (value deliberately left as policy territory), (12) temporal sensitivity (Stale != Delete), (13) context sensitivity ('Evidence has no universal relevance'), (14) provenance preservation, (15) no evidence creation (empty evidence set yields NoEvidence, not 0.5 or Confirmed), (16) no certainty creation (StrongEvidence does not imply Truth). Separates four kernel invariants A1-A4 (identity preservation, provenance preservation, contradiction preservation, no automatic independence) from four policy properties A5-A8 (corroboration rule, saturation, decision threshold, probability interpretation), and states a ten-item Evidence Constitution E-K1..E-K10 covering identity, no-duplicate-inflation, provenance preservation, dependency awareness, unknown-is-not-independent, contradiction preservation, context dependence, Stale!=Deleted, no-truth-by-aggregation, and no-decision-by-aggregation. Compares nine aggregation frameworks (Maximum/Mean/Weighted-sum/Saturating/Bayesian/Dempster-Shafer/Possibility/Argumentation/Graph-based) and concludes there is probably no single universal KnowledgeOS evidence algebra, proposing a fixed kernel plus pluggable assessment calculi C_admissible = {rho | Agg_rho satisfies A_kernel}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C5. step-005 (142333) -- What Is the Mathematical Object Being Aggregated ... section21 KERNEL/POLICY partition (verbatim sets): KERNEL = {Evidence, Proposition, Provenance, Lineage, Dependency, Context, TemporalValidity, Polarity, AssessmentBasis}; POLICY = {Aggregation, Inference, Thresholds, ProbabilityModels, BeliefModels, DecisionRules}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-005 (file 142333) states Evidence != Support != Belief != Probability != Truth, and argues the contribution function c_rho(e,P,C) must deliberately not be typed into [0,1], since '0.8 has no epistemic meaning until its semantics are specified' -- a direct answer to an earlier morning file's problem 4 (094259). Distinguishes seven semantic domains (Reliability, Relevance, Evidential support, Probability, Belief, Plausibility, Information gain) and argues the kernel must not choose one calculus over another. States the single most citable boundary statement in the batch: the KERNEL/POLICY partition, KERNEL = {Evidence, Proposition, Provenance, Lineage, Dependency, Context, TemporalValidity, Polarity, AssessmentBasis} versus POLICY = {Aggregation, Inference, Thresholds, ProbabilityModels, BeliefModels, DecisionRules} -- 'the kernel stores the dimensions, the policy determines how they combine.' Also distinguishes Assessment != Acceptance and EvidenceValue != EvidenceStrength, closing with the verdict 'substantially resolved'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C6. step-006 (142514) -- Information Gain and Value of Evidence ... Evidence Strength != Information Gain != Decision Value ... section13 q*=argmax U_rho(q|K_t,I_t,P) -- potentially one of the most important equations in the whole KnowledgeOS theory. ... section24 safeguard: refuses Moksha = Delta=0
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-006 (file 142514) distinguishes Evidence Strength != Information Gain != Decision Value; defines information gain IG(e;P)=H(P)-H(P|e) but then explicitly refuses IG=EntropyReduction as a universal law, instead defining a discrepancy-reduction measure IG_D(e), an expected discrepancy reduction EDR(e) made more fundamental than entropy reduction ('KnowledgeOS is trying to move K_t toward I_t, not H(K_t) to 0'), and a value-of-evidence function VOE_rho and utility U_rho(e)=Benefit-Cost with explicitly policy-dependent weights; states q*=argmax_q U_rho(q|K_t,I_t,P) as potentially one of the most important equations in the whole theory; formalizes the guidance triad Zero(K_t,I_t)->Delta_t, Lord(Delta_t)->Q, Sarathi(Q,constraints)->a_t; and provides an explicit safeguard against an earlier morning file's (085756) Moksha-as-maximal-information claim, refusing Moksha=Delta=0 and stating Delta=0 always means only relative to the specified ideal state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C7. step-007 (142709) -- Knowledge State Transition Algebra ... K_t=(A_t,E_t,R_t,C_t,H_t,Gamma_t) ... section11 eight transition operations O_K ... with a PARTIAL map delta:K x O_K -harpoon-> K ... section33 invariants K1-K8
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-007 (file 142709) defines the Knowledge State tuple K_t=(A_t,E_t,R_t,C_t,H_t,Gamma_t) (Assertions, Evidence, Relations, Conflicts, History, validity conditions), states K_t != H_t and Superseded != Deleted, and mediates Evidence-does-not-imply-Knowledge via an epistemic event rather than evidence directly. Defines eight transition operations O_K = {Introduce, Corroborate, Qualify, Contradict, Supersede, Resolve, Retract, Invalidate} as a PARTIAL function delta:K x O_K -> K (partial because, e.g., Resolve(C) is invalid if C is not an active conflict); states TemporalChange != LogicalContradiction, Retract(A) != Delete(A), Invalidation != Retraction; rejects a single linear lifecycle in favor of a multidimensional epistemic-state vector Sigma_A=(Acquisition,Support,Uncertainty,Validity); models event sourcing K_t=Fold(delta,H_t,K_0) and K_t=F(K_0,H_t,rho,omega) with rho=policy version and omega=ontology/model version; states Knowledge-time != Source-time != Validity-time; takes a paraconsistent stance allowing P and not-P representable without trivializing the whole state; and closes with eight invariants K1-K8 (Evidence does not imply Accepted Knowledge; Superseded/Retracted != Deleted; P and not-P coexist without collapse; three distinct time coordinates; reconstructibility; policy versioning; semantic versioning; state-transition function). Leaves deliberately unresolved: 'when exactly is a conclusion allowed to modify the Knowledge State?' -- handed to step-008.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D2. step-025a-1 (181325) ... Honesty flag, verbatim: I attempted to execute the first prototype ... the execution environment did not successfully complete the run. So I will not claim experimental results that I have not actually obtained. ... section6 [UNRESOLVED] EVIDENCE FLAG
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-025a-1 (file 181325) opens with an honesty flag: an attempted first prototype execution did not successfully complete, so the author explicitly declines to claim unobtained experimental results. Defines nine fundamental types (WorldState W_t != K_t; Observation O; Evidence E, explicitly Observation != Evidence; Assertion A; Assessment Q(A,E,C); KnowledgeState K_t=(A_t,Q_t,E_t,C_t,P_t); Goal G, Goal != Action; Knowledge Requirement R; Epistemic Contract C_G) and a minimal state K_t=(E_t,A_t,Q_t,C_t,P_t,V_t) with G and C_G kept outside it, marked PROVISIONAL. Raises an explicit [UNRESOLVED] question -- whether evidence is actually part of K_t or merely externally referenced -- refusing to resolve it by intuition and instead proposing to test which representation is required for historical reconstruction, retraction, provenance, and conflict resolution. Runs eight attack scenarios including the discovery that more knowledge can increase |K_{t+1}| while decreasing Readiness(K_{t+1}), and that Authorization=False implies Execute=Forbidden as part of state-transition semantics, not merely policy overlay.

b_rows_sample.statement: Step-025a-5 (file 182235) property-tests the ten invariants I1-I10 (originating in step-025a-4) plus four newly promoted invariants I11-I14 (I11 No hindsight: a decision's basis is the knowledge state at decision time, not the current one; I12 World/knowledge independence; I13 Revision must not imply falsehood -- invalidating the only supporting evidence yields Unknown, not False; I14 Conflict resolution must preserve history) against generated adversarial sequences, all fourteen passing with qualifications; identifies exactly two genuine unresolved threats -- CircularDependencies (a derivation cycle A1 supports A2 and A2 supports A1, with AcyclicDerivationGraph proposed but not established) and EvidenceIdentity (not reducible to a text hash) -- plus four further threats (scale/propagation cost, stale rules requiring RuleVersion, changing ontology entering epistemic lineage, and source authority requiring temporal semantics with Truth != Authority); proposes the emergent structure K=(V,E,R,T,P,D,M) (epistemic objects, evidence/support relations, assessments/rules, temporal semantics, provenance, dependency/derivation, model/ontology/rule versions), characterizing KnowledgeOS as an increasingly revealed 'governed temporal epistemic graph' -- marked a strong emerging architectural result; and includes an explicit integrity disclaimer that no automated property-based software test was actually executed, only a conceptual/adversarial falsification pass.

b_rows_sample.statement: Step-025b (file 182411) runs a full end-to-end adversarial simulation (a Nexus migration scenario) covering the whole epistemic-to-operational loop rather than just the kernel, defining an epistemic contract EC_G with nine named requirements and stating Goal != EpistemicContract and Input != Evidence; demonstrates, inside the simulated loop rather than merely arguing it, that after a restore test KnowledgeGain > 0 while MigrationReadiness simultaneously decreases, establishing KnowledgeGain != ProgressTowardGoal empirically within the scenario; formalizes Delta = Zero(K_t, I, EC_G) decomposed into Epistemic/Operational/Governance gaps; states Lord does not necessarily change the world (it may select an epistemic action first); defines the pipeline Recommendation -> Decision -> Authorization -> Execution; runs five injected attacks (LLM hallucination, conflicting sources, stale source, changed requirement, execution failure becoming new evidence); defines six epistemic stopping conditions S1-S6 and an epistemic budget B_epi = {Time, Cost, Risk, HumanAttention, Compute}; distinguishes the epistemic loop from the operational loop; and closes by generating the entire subsequent research agenda (unresolved items U1-U6 feeding directly into steps 025c, 025c-3, 025d, 025f, 025g).

b_rows_sample.anchor: TV-F-020 -- The dependency relation prec has inconsistent orientation at its birth site ... step-002 section5 defines e1 prec e2 as "e2 was produced using e1" (parent prec child). Step-002 section6 Case B ... then writes e2 prec e1 -- child prec parent -- with the author's own caveat "depending on how we orient the provenance relation."
b_rows_sample.statement: TV-F-020 finds, by direct comparison of the definition site and first-use site within the same source file, that step-002's dependency relation e1 prec e2 (defined in section 5 as 'e2 was produced using e1', parent-to-child) is used with the opposite orientation (e2 prec e1, child-to-parent) in section 6's Case B, with the author's own caveat acknowledging the orientation is undecided ('depending on how we orient the provenance relation'). Classifies this as UNDER-SPECIFIED, not a mathematical error, since both orientations give isomorphic theory, but notes every formal statement using prec downstream (step-004's E-K4, step-003's dependency sensitivity) silently assumes the section-5 orientation, and a candidate kernel document (K0's P5 frame) adopted that orientation only as a PROPOSED RECONSTRUCTION -- the source itself never settles it. Severity MINOR; requires only a one-line governance/notation disposition, no mathematical content change; confirms no rim theorem depends on the arrow-direction convention.

b_rows_sample.anchor: TV-F-021 -- Two overlapping, unreconciled transition-operation alphabets in Steps 007/009 ... step-007 section11 ... O_K = 8 ops ... Step-009 section22 ... R_K = 9 ops ... Neither file cites or maps to the other's alphabet ... this finding pins the origin of the transition-alphabet divergence to 007->009, before any later fork.
b_rows_sample.statement: TV-F-021 finds two partially overlapping, mutually silent transition-operation alphabets defined over the same carrier K within a single day: step-007's 8-operation O_K = {Introduce, Corroborate, Qualify, Contradict, Supersede, Resolve, Retract, Invalidate} (with delta: K x O_K -> K) and step-009's 9-operation R_K = {Contextualize, Corroborate, Downgrade, Retract, Supersede, Accept, Reject, Defer, Resolve} (with Revise: K x R_K -> K), sharing exactly four operations (Corroborate, Retract, Supersede, Resolve) while diverging on the rest, with neither file citing or mapping to the other and step-009 never stating whether R_K extends, replaces, or coexists with O_K. Logical omniscience: The system believes all logical consequences ... computationally intractable and cognitively unrealistic. ... four-valued situations: True only, False only, Both, Neither. ... Beliefs are not closed under implication. ... {Bp,B(p\supset q),
eg Bq} ... {Bp,B

a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces the B (explicit belief) operator using four-valued situations (true-only/false-only/both/neither) to avoid logical omniscience -- beliefs are not closed under implication or consequence, exemplified by satisfiable sets {Bp,B(p⊃q),¬Bq} and inconsistent-without-explosion {Bp,B¬p,¬Bq}; a first-order variant interprets existential quantification constructively, making existential generalization fail (not |= B(P(a)∨P(b))⊃B∃xP(x)); complexity results range from co-NP-complete (propositional) to undecidable (first-order with existential generalization).
