a_rows_sample.anchor: semantic information → knowledge → reality ... semantic information as well-formed, meaningful, truthful data ... knowledge is relevant semantic information that is properly accounted for. ... SYSTEM/DOMAIN -> LEVEL OF ABSTRACTION -> {observables,behaviour,relations} -> DATA -[meaning]-> INFORMATION -[truth]-> SEMANTIC INFORMATION -[relevance]-> KNOWLEDGE -[account]-> WELL-FOUNDED KNOWLEDGE.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports Floridi's central chain semantic-information->knowledge->reality, defining semantic information as well-formed/meaningful/truthful data and knowledge as relevant semantic information properly accounted for, formalized as a full pipeline from System/Domain through Level of Abstraction (observables/behaviour/relations) to Data, Information (via meaning), Semantic Information (via truth), Knowledge (via relevance), and Well-Founded Knowledge (via account); concludes Knowledge Space should be modeled as a structured space of informational descriptions at different abstraction levels, not a collection of knowledge objects.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Words and sentences should almost certainly NOT be Kernel primitives of Knowledge itself. They belong to a representation / expression layer.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the idea that 'knowledge can be expressed in words' implies words/sentences are Kernel primitives: Floridi treats informational content as not identical with its particular encoding (books/databases/websites/words/sentences all carry information without being it), so the chain Word->Sentence->Proposition->Semantic Content is not Word=Knowledge; words and sentences belong to a representation/expression layer, one of the file's first recorded architectural conclusions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A Level of Abstraction is a finite non-empty set of observables. ... A Knowledge Space boundary should normally be a boundary of abstraction, purpose, scope and observability. ... The object did not change. The Knowledge Space changed because the Level of Abstraction changed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adopts Floridi's Level of Abstraction (LoA, a finite non-empty set of observables -- an observable being an interpreted typed variable representing a system feature, where 'system' can be physical/conceptual/mathematical/moral) as the answer to 'should a topic have a boundary?': yes, but as a boundary of abstraction/purpose/scope/observability, not an ontological one; illustrated by 'Car' described completely differently across four LoAs (brand/model/year; engine/transmission/fuel; combustion/thermodynamics/materials; molecular structure/quantum phenomena) where the object is unchanged but the Knowledge Space differs by LoA -- called the single most valuable idea in the book for KnowledgeOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A Knowledge Space is potentially unbounded in extension, but every usable knowledge representation is bounded by a selected Level of Abstraction, purpose, context and scope.
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines the project's 'knowledge can be infinite if you go deeper and deeper' intuition into: Knowledge Space is potentially unbounded in extension, but every usable knowledge representation is bounded by a selected LoA, purpose, context and scope, citing Floridi's Gradient of Abstraction allowing movement across LoA views.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the behaviour of the system at that LoA ... SCOPE BOUNDARY, SEMANTIC BOUNDARY, VALIDITY/BEHAVIOURAL BOUNDARY ... If you observe chess only by files, you cannot reconstruct the full game. If you observe it only by ranks, you also cannot. But when the two views are combined, the underlying game becomes recoverable. ... A topic does NOT necessarily need one boundary. ... KnowledgeOS should probably support overlapping knowledge spaces rather than forcing a single tree of topics.
a_rows_sample.statement: Uses Floridi's 'behaviour' (allowed observable-value combinations at a LoA, defined by a predicate) to distinguish Scope/Semantic/Validity-Behavioural boundaries (illustrated by an Election topic where not every voter/candidate/ballot relationship is valid); uses the chess files/ranks example (neither view alone reconstructs the game, combined they do) to argue a topic need not have one boundary but can be a projection into a knowledge space, concluding KnowledgeOS should support overlapping knowledge spaces rather than a single topic tree -- a major architectural consequence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: data exists, data is well-formed, the well-formed data is meaningful, the meaning is truthful. ... "Purple elephants negotiate database treaties." ... false information is not semantic information in the strict sense, but pseudo-information/misinformation. ... Claim: syntactic_status, semantic_status, truth_status, relevance_status, evidential_status, account_status.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports Floridi's four-condition definition of semantic information (data exists, is well-formed, is meaningful, is truthful) and his claim that false information is pseudo-information/misinformation rather than semantic information proper; illustrated by 'purple elephants negotiate database treaties' being syntactically valid but questionable on meaningful/truthful/relevant/knowledge; proposes replacing a single truth=true/false flag with a Claim record carrying six independent status fields (syntactic, semantic, truth, relevance, evidential, account).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Network Theory of Account ... a piece of semantic information is an answer to a question, but that answer generates further questions. ... How come?/historical, What for?/teleological, How does it work?/functional ... QUESTION -> ANSWER -> raises questions -> ACCOUNT -> KNOWLEDGE. This is one of the strongest findings from this book.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adopts Floridi's Network Theory of Account: semantic information answers a question but the answer generates further questions, and relevant information becomes knowledge only when such questions are correctly answered through an appropriate network of informational relations; distinguishes three kinds of 'why' (historical/How-come, teleological/What-for, functional/How-does-it-work, illustrated by Floridi's Berlin and boiling-kettle examples), extending the question taxonomy to what/who/which/where/when/how/why{causal,functional,historical,teleological}/under-what-conditions, formalized as a Question->Answer->raises-questions->Account->Knowledge cycle -- called one of the book's strongest findings.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ANSWER QUALITY: correctness, specificity, completeness, relevance, scope, granularity, evidence, accountability. ... An answer may be correct at LoA-1 but insufficient at LoA-3. ... "The application is slow because the database is overloaded." ... This is exactly the knowledge depth mechanism you were intuitively describing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Replaces the informal 'concreteness of an answer' intuition with eight Answer Quality dimensions (correctness, specificity, completeness, relevance, scope, granularity, evidence, accountability), illustrated by a database-slowness answer chain that is correct at one LoA but requires successive deeper LoAs to fully explain -- identified as exactly the 'knowledge depth' mechanism the project had been intuitively describing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: relevant semantic information becomes knowledge iff it is correctly accounted for. ... truthful + relevant information can still be epistemically lucky. The missing piece is the account connecting the information appropriately to its supporting informational sources. ... remarkably close to what we have been developing in KnowledgeOS around evidence, provenance, verification, justification, observations, deterministic assurance, architectural decisions.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the file's crucial insight: knowledge is not just truth -- truthful and relevant information can still be 'epistemically lucky' without an account connecting it to its supporting informational sources; identifies this account requirement as remarkably close to the project's existing evidence, provenance, verification, justification, observations, deterministic assurance, and architectural-decision work.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CLAIM "Berlin is the capital of Germany" ├── expression (sentence) ├── meaning (proposition) ├── context ├── LoA ├── truth ├── relevance ├── evidence ├── account └── temporal validity ... much closer to KnowledgeOS.
a_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts a normal knowledge-graph triple (Berlin--capitalOf-->Germany) with a fully-specified KnowledgeOS CLAIM object for the same fact, carrying nine branches (expression/sentence, meaning/proposition, context, LoA, truth, relevance, evidence, account, temporal validity), presented as much closer to what KnowledgeOS should represent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the UTI challenge: Is a grand unified theory of information possible? He leans toward a non-reductionist position, where different information concepts may be logically interdependent but mutually irreducible. ... We should NOT attempt to put everything into the Kernel. ... The Kernel should define what must be true of a Knowledge Space, not contain the world's knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports Floridi's non-reductionist stance on the Unified Theory of Information challenge (information concepts may be interdependent but mutually irreducible), warning against a KnowledgeKernel containing all ontology/semantics/epistemology/logic/language/domain-knowledge/reasoning; proposes instead a minimal-invariants Kernel (semantics/epistemics/structure) surrounded by extensible spaces (domain space/methodology/governance) -- the Kernel defines what must be true of a Knowledge Space, not the world's knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Keep: A. Level of Abstraction -- Strong Kernel candidate. B. Observable -- Strong candidate. C. Behaviour/constraints -- Strong candidate. D. Semantic information -- Strong candidate. E. Truthfulness -- Kernel-level concern, not a single Boolean. F. Relevance -- Strong candidate, contextual. G. Question->Answer->Account -- Extremely strong candidate. H. Network of information flow -- Strong candidate. I. Structural objects + relations -- Strong candidate. ... Do NOT directly adopt: Reality = information; "Humans are the only known semantic engines"; Floridi's exact epistemological definition of knowledge (treat as research evidence, not constitutional definition).
a_rows_sample.statement: Runs a systematic Zero-Lens keep/reject pass over Floridi's own concepts: nine concepts rated strong-to-extremely-strong Kernel candidates (Level of Abstraction, Observable, Behaviour/constraints, Semantic information, Truthfulness, Relevance, Question->Answer->Account, Network of information flow, Structural objects+relations), versus three items explicitly not to adopt (the metaphysical claim Reality=information, 'humans are the only known semantic engines', and Floridi's exact epistemological knowledge-definition, kept only as research evidence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Representation boundary ... 2. Semantic boundary ... 3. Epistemic boundary ... 4. Abstraction boundary ... That is a much better definition of the Knowledge Space boundary.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes four Knowledge Space boundary types: Representation (which language/symbols -- word/sentence/document/diagram/code), Semantic (what an expression means -- concept/proposition/reference/predicate/relation), Epistemic (what is actually known -- truth/evidence/relevance/account/confidence/uncertainty), and Abstraction (which part/aspect of the system is modeled -- scope/LoA/purpose/context/observables/behaviour), stated as a much better definition than a single undifferentiated 'boundary'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1. ENTITY/SYSTEM 2. IDENTITY 3. RELATION 4. OBSERVABLE 5. LEVEL OF ABSTRACTION 6. CONTEXT 7. PURPOSE 8. PROPOSITION/CLAIM 9. QUESTION 10. ANSWER 11. EVIDENCE 12. TRUTH/CORRECTNESS 13. RELEVANCE 14. ACCOUNT 15. TEMPORALITY 16. PROVENANCE 17. CONSTRAINT/BEHAVIOUR ... WORD, SENTENCE, DOCUMENT, TOPIC, ARTICLE, BOOK, MANIFESTO, CONSTITUTION would not necessarily be Kernel primitives.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a 17-item candidate Kernel list (Entity/System, Identity, Relation, Observable, Level of Abstraction, Context, Purpose, Proposition/Claim, Question, Answer, Evidence, Truth/Correctness, Relevance, Account, Temporality, Provenance, Constraint/Behaviour) explicitly excluding Word, Sentence, Document, Topic, Article, Book, Manifesto, and Constitution as representational/organizational structures built on top of the Kernel -- a major architectural simplification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: information can be approached through different spaces: probability space, modal space, state space, inference space, and data space. ... Perhaps Knowledge Space is a structured family of interrelated spaces ... Levels of Abstraction provide the coordinate system/interface through which these spaces can be related. That is, in my view, the most valuable result of reading this book.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes the file's most valuable result: Knowledge Space is not one mathematical space but a structured family of interrelated spaces (Data Space: symbols/expressions/documents; Semantic Space: propositions/meanings/references; Epistemic Space: knowledge/evidence/beliefs; State Space: dynamics/change; Modal Space: possible states; Inference Space: reasoning paths), with Levels of Abstraction functioning as the coordinate system/interface relating them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Floridi does not give us the final KnowledgeOS Kernel. ... stop asking: "What things belong inside KnowledgeOS?" and start asking: "What structures and transformations are invariant when knowledge is represented, abstracted, questioned, verified, related, and accounted for?" ... Knowledge Space Model v0.2 ... test it against the next book—especially Williamson.
a_rows_sample.statement: Declines to freeze the Kernel after Floridi, reframing the guiding question from 'what things belong inside KnowledgeOS?' to 'what structures and transformations are invariant when knowledge is represented, abstracted, questioned, verified, related, and accounted for?', naming the current state 'Knowledge Space Model v0.2' and committing to test it next against Williamson, since Floridi's biggest unresolved assumption (identified explicitly) is what makes semantic information become knowledge -- relevance and account.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Dretske instead develops: information -> information-caused belief -> knowledge. He explicitly proposes an information-theoretic replacement for the traditional justified-true-belief account. ... a particularly subtle distinction between information causing a belief and information causally sustaining a belief. ... OBSERVATION -> INFORMATION ACQUISITION -> BELIEF FORMATION -> BELIEF SUSTENANCE -> KNOWLEDGE CLAIM.
a_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts Floridi's semantic-information->relevance->account->knowledge route with Dretske's information->information-caused-belief->knowledge route (an information-theoretic replacement for justified-true-belief), distinguishing information causing a belief from information causally sustaining it, proposing a five-stage pipeline Observation->Information Acquisition->Belief Formation->Belief Sustenance->Knowledge Claim instead of treating evidence as a static attachment to a claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Floridi and Dretske are converging on some things but disagreeing or emphasizing different layers on others. That is precisely what we need from the Zero Lens. ... I would not freeze the Kernel yet. The next useful step is to construct a Floridi × Dretske comparative matrix and derive only the invariants that survive both books.
a_rows_sample.statement: Notes Floridi and Dretske converge on some points and diverge/emphasize different layers on others, which is exactly the intended use of the Zero Lens; explicitly declines to freeze the Kernel, proposing a Floridi x Dretske comparative matrix to derive only the invariants surviving both books as the next research step.

a_rows_sample.anchor: When should a database answer "I don't know" to a query? ... question answering itself is epistemic behavior. ... ANSWERABILITY, INFORMATION SUFFICIENCY, KNOWLEDGE, COMPUTABILITY, CONFIDENCE, COMPLETENESS. Those are not the same quantity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Uses Fagin et al.'s database 'when should I-don't-know be returned?' question to argue question-answering is itself epistemic behavior (Question->Knowledge regime->{enough information? awareness? computation? evidence? shared knowledge?}->YES/NO/UNKNOWN), extending Floridi's Answer Quality dimensions by separating Answerability, Information Sufficiency, Knowledge, Computability, Confidence, and Completeness as non-identical quantities.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge is moving in an infinite Knowledge Space. ... Knowledge should serve the nature of the Knowledge Space itself. ... Knowledge is not merely accumulated inside the Knowledge Space; its structure, relations, boundaries, changes, and representations should remain coherent with the nature of the space being modelled.
a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates sixteen prior project intuitions about Knowledge Space (infinite, boundary-crossing, facts+arguments, dynamic, representation≠knowledge, LoA-dependent, tolerates uncertainty/contradiction/suspension, changes via expansion/revision/contraction, entrenchment-dependent importance, exceeds language, questions open paths, explanations reduce surprise) into one closing principle: knowledge's structure/relations/boundaries/changes/representations must remain coherent with the nature of the space being modeled, not merely accumulate inside it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the central entities are epistemic states, representing a person's cognitive/epistemic situation at a point in time, while treating them as rational idealizations rather than literal psychological objects. ... 1. Model of epistemic states 2. Epistemic attitudes 3. Epistemic inputs 4. Epistemic commitment function ... I would not put the commitment function in the Kernel. It is a regime-specific rule for transforming states.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the guiding question from 'what is Knowledge?' to 'what is the minimal representation of an epistemic state, and how does that state change?', adopting Gärdenfors' four-component belief system (model of epistemic states, epistemic attitudes, epistemic inputs, epistemic commitment function), explicitly excluding the commitment function from the Kernel as a regime-specific transformation rule -- the Kernel preserves the state and the input/history needed to reconstruct the transformation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: belief sets, possible worlds, ordinal plausibility, Bayesian probabilities, truth-maintenance systems, mental models ... KnowledgeOS should not store an epistemic state as "possible worlds." Possible worlds are one epistemic representation regime. ... Epistemic status is regime-relative. That should probably become an explicit KnowledgeOS principle.
b_rows_sample.statement: Surveys six alternative epistemic-state representation regimes Gärdenfors considers (belief sets, possible worlds, ordinal plausibility, Bayesian probabilities, truth-maintenance systems, mental models), concluding possible worlds are only one such regime among several, reinforcing the Kernel-preserves/regimes-reason architecture; derives the principle 'epistemic status is regime-relative' -- the same proposition can be accepted/rejected/indeterminate under one attitude model or assigned probability/plausibility under another.

b_rows_sample.anchor: some models can contain hidden variables that have no direct expression in the available language ... Language does not contain the whole knowledge state. ... Pāṇinian/Vāṇī: language is expression. Floridi: representation ≠ information. Dretske: information ≠ encoding. Gärdenfors: epistemic state ≠ language. This is now a very strong cross-lens invariant.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports Gärdenfors' hidden/latent epistemic-state variables (aspects of a second-order probabilistic epistemic state with no direct linguistic expression), formalizing 'language does not contain the whole knowledge state' and recording independent four-lens convergence (Vāṇī: language is expression; Floridi: representation≠information; Dretske: information≠encoding; Gärdenfors: epistemic state≠language) into the principle 'language is an external expression/communication layer over the epistemic substrate.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: EXPANSION REVISION CONTRACTION ... An expansion adds information consistent with the current state. A revision incorporates information that conflicts with the current state. A contraction removes a commitment. ... we should preserve: previous_state, input, change_type, change_policy, resulting_state, rationale.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes three fundamental epistemic change types (expansion: adds compatible information; revision: incorporates conflicting information; contraction: removes a commitment) as a state-transition graph, requiring KnowledgeOS preserve previous_state/input/change_type/change_policy/resulting_state/rationale rather than merely overwriting a current_state field -- much stronger than an undifferentiated knowledge(t1)->knowledge(t2) chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Supersession is not necessarily: "A is false now." It may mean: Under the current epistemic regime and new input, retaining A is no longer rational/acceptable.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes supersession using the revision policy: rather than 'A is false now', supersession means retaining A is no longer rational/acceptable under the current epistemic regime and new input, with some commitments retained and others retracted -- a better model for living knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: beliefs have different degrees of epistemic entrenchment. Some are more difficult to give up because they are more important for inquiry, explanation and decision making. And this is not the same thing as probability. ... "2 + 2 = 4" probability = 1, entrenchment = extremely high. "The UI button is blue" probability = 1, entrenchment = low.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces epistemic entrenchment -- degree of resistance to giving up a belief, driven by importance for inquiry/explanation/decision-making -- as distinct from probability, illustrated by two claims with identical probability=1 but radically different entrenchment ('2+2=4' extremely high vs 'the UI button is blue' low), called probably the most valuable new idea from the book.

b_rows_sample.anchor: entrenchment depends on the epistemic state. The same proposition can have a different entrenchment ordering in different belief systems ... scientific paradigm shifts ... Importance is not an intrinsic property of a proposition. ... importance(P) = 0.9 would be misleading unless it specifies for whom? for what inquiry? in which context? under which epistemic regime? at what time?
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses Gärdenfors' claim that entrenchment orderings differ across belief systems (illustrated by scientific paradigm shifts, where a once-central claim becomes peripheral) to correct any naive 'importance(P)=0.9' score: importance is not intrinsic to a proposition but must specify for whom, for what inquiry, in which context, under which regime, at what time; extends the Knowledge Space boundary model (previously Level-of-Abstraction-based) by adding an entrenchment-structure dimension alongside scope/LoA/inquiry/context/regime/participants, with Topic as a projection of this fuller state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Minimal Epistemic Disturbance ... make the smallest rational change necessary to accommodate the new input. ... give up as little information as possible and avoid unnecessary loss. ... Not a Kernel primitive, but a very strong regime.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the 'Minimal Epistemic Disturbance' principle from Gärdenfors' minimal-change revision criterion and informational-economy contraction: when revising, change no more commitments than necessary to accommodate new input, avoiding unnecessary information loss; proposed as a strong candidate revision regime rather than a Kernel primitive.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVIDENCE HISTORY: immutable. EPISTEMIC STATE: revisable. KNOWLEDGE PROJECTION: recomputable. ... Observation O1 remains true as historical observation. But Interpretation I1 can be withdrawn. And Epistemic state S1 can become S2 without rewriting O1.
b_rows_sample.statement: Resolves the apparent conflict between 'evidence is immutable' and 'knowledge is revised' by distinguishing three tiers: Evidence History (immutable), Epistemic State (revisable), Knowledge Projection (recomputable) -- an observation O1 remains true as a historical record even as an interpretation I1 built on it is withdrawn and the epistemic state moves from S1 to S2 without rewriting O1.

b_rows_sample.anchor: LEVEL A — PRESERVED HISTORY: observations, inputs, assertions, sources, events, evidence, provenance; immutable. LEVEL B — EPISTEMIC STATE: acceptance, rejection, suspension, probability, plausibility, entrenchment, belief; mutable/derived. LEVEL C — PRESENTED KNOWLEDGE: answers, summaries, topics, reports, recommendations, current understanding; derived projections. This is one of the strongest architectural conclusions we've reached.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a three-level architecture explicitly called one of the strongest architectural conclusions reached: Level A Preserved History (observations, inputs, assertions, sources, events, evidence, provenance -- immutable), Level B Epistemic State (acceptance, rejection, suspension, probability, plausibility, entrenchment, belief -- mutable/derived), Level C Presented Knowledge (answers, summaries, topics, reports, recommendations, current understanding -- derived projections).

b_rows_sample.anchor: an epistemic input can be represented simply as a function from epistemic states to epistemic states. He explicitly calls this ontologically simpler. ... Input Event + Transformation Policy -> State Transition. ... EpistemicTransition: before, input, rule/regime, conflict, retained commitments, retracted commitments, after.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses Gärdenfors' ontological-simplification move (an epistemic input need not be a giant separate entity; it can be represented as a function K->K' on epistemic states) -- compatible with the Merricks/Zero-Lens eliminativism method -- to propose Input Event + Transformation Policy -> State Transition rather than an EpistemicInput entity, and a candidate (not-yet-Kernel) EpistemicTransition record (before, input, rule/regime, conflict, retained commitments, retracted commitments, after).

b_rows_sample.anchor: an explanation should provide relevant information that makes the phenomenon less surprising relative to the recipient's epistemic state. ... explanations depend on the epistemic circumstances of both the requester and the explainer. ... Explanation Quality = f(new information, recipient epistemic state, question/context).
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines explanation quality relative to the recipient's epistemic state (not as an intrinsic explanans/explanandum relation): a good explanation makes the phenomenon less surprising given the recipient's prior knowledge, context, and available evidence, formalized as Explanation Quality = f(new information, recipient epistemic state, question/context) -- a better starting point than an LLM-style intrinsic answer-quality score.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P(failure | current knowledge) = 0.05 ... After: The certificate expired. ... P(failure | expanded/revised knowledge) = 0.70. The explanation reduced surprise. ... surprise_before - surprise_after ... cognitive relief from reduced surprise.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an Explanation Gain metric = surprise_before - surprise_after (Gärdenfors' 'cognitive relief'), illustrated by a service-failure example where a candidate explanation ('the certificate expired') raises P(failure|knowledge) from 0.05 to 0.70, called a promising statistical bridge for KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: current knowledge includes C and E -> temporarily remove C -> ask whether E becomes less expected -> C has causal relevance. His probabilistic criterion is that, in the contracted epistemic state, occurrence of C raises the probability of E. ... probabilistic influence alone does not automatically establish causation ... P(E|C) > P(E) is not automatically C causes E. ... preserve causal_hypothesis separately from statistical_association.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes causal belief via contraction: temporarily remove candidate cause C from the epistemic state and test whether effect E becomes less expected (probabilistic criterion: in the contracted state, C's occurrence raises P(E)); connects this to the project's Persons+Causes research, proposing KnowledgeOS distinguish observed sequence/correlation/causal belief/causal evidence/causal hypothesis/causal explanation; explicitly warns P(E|C)>P(E) does not automatically establish C causes E (spurious/direct/indirect causes need additional treatment), requiring causal_hypothesis be preserved separately from statistical_association.

b_rows_sample.anchor: belief revision techniques to logical databases and legal codes. A logical database can be treated as a model of an epistemic state, and updates correspond to expansion, revision and contraction. ... deleting a tuple is not enough: removing one fact can have implications for several derived facts. ... Never equate storage mutation with epistemic change. Deleting a record is not the same thing as retracting a proposition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports Gärdenfors' direct application of belief revision to logical databases and legal codes (database updates correspond to expansion/revision/contraction; deleting one tuple is insufficient since it has implications for derived facts), deriving the principle 'never equate storage mutation with epistemic change' -- deleting a record is not the same as retracting a proposition, which can have dependent consequences.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the epistemic layer needs: OBSERVE, ACCEPT, EXPAND, REVISE, CONTRACT, SUPERSEDE, QUESTION, REASSESS, DERIVE. And importantly: DELETE is not a semantic operation equivalent to: CONTRACT.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues the Kernel should not be CRUD-centric (CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE), proposing instead a nine-operation epistemic vocabulary (OBSERVE, ACCEPT, EXPAND, REVISE, CONTRACT, SUPERSEDE, QUESTION, REASSESS, DERIVE), explicitly distinguishing DELETE from CONTRACT as different operations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: a proposition can be characterized by the change it would induce if added to an epistemic state. ... P : K → K' ... Meaning can be understood through the effect of an expression/proposition on a belief system.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports Gärdenfors' definition of a proposition as the change it would induce if added to an epistemic state (P: K -> K'), viewing a proposition as a potential transformation rather than only semantic content; correspondingly reframes meaning as understood through the effect of an expression on a belief system, connecting language/semantics/questions/belief-revision without making language foundational, independently supporting the Vāṇī/Paninian insight.

b_rows_sample.anchor: his epistemological theory can formulate epistemic states and rationality criteria without using truth as the basic ingredient; truth is secondary within this conceptualistic framework. That does not refute McGinn. They are answering different questions. ... Ontology / truth theory ≠ Epistemic dynamics. So our Kernel should probably not attempt to derive epistemic dynamics from a single metaphysical truth theory.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reconciles Gärdenfors (epistemic dynamics formulated without truth as a basic ingredient) with McGinn (truth as a primitive, reality-implying logical property): the two are not in conflict since they answer different questions, giving the principle Ontology/truth theory != Epistemic dynamics; the Kernel should not attempt to derive epistemic dynamics from a single metaphysical truth theory, instead supporting a relation to truth/verification while keeping epistemic-state transitions their own concern.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. A state exists at a time. ... 14. State dynamics can support database/legal-code updates. This is much closer to a Kernel boundary than the ontology we had been building before.
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies the Zero Lens by removing all Gärdenfors-specific machinery (AGM, possible worlds, Bayesian probabilities, Spohn, Ramsey test, belief set, logical language), leaving a fourteen-statement residual (a state exists at a time; contains commitments/attitudes; inputs can enter and change the state; different kinds of change exist; change follows a rationality/commitment policy; some commitments are more entrenched than others; the policy avoids unnecessary information loss; the same input can have different effects in different states; meaning can be studied through state-changing effects; explanation depends on the recipient's existing state; causal belief can depend on hypothetical state changes; state dynamics can support logic and database/legal-code updates), judged much closer to a Kernel boundary than the prior ontology-building work.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PRESERVATION SUBSTRATE: Identity, Agent/epistemic participant, Context, Time, Epistemic input, Input provenance, Assertion/proposition reference, Epistemic attitude/assessment, State-transition event, Previous state reference, Resulting-state reference, Change type, Rationale/commitment reference, Conflict/incompatibility, Evidence/source, Entrenchment assessment. Notice what is not here: possible worlds, Bayesian probabilities, logic engine, truth engine, LLM, topic hierarchy, embedding.
b_rows_sample.statement: Revises the candidate Preservation Substrate to sixteen items (Identity, Agent/epistemic participant, Context, Time, Epistemic input, Input provenance, Assertion/proposition reference, Epistemic attitude/assessment, State-transition event, Previous state reference, Resulting-state reference, Change type, Rationale/commitment reference, Conflict/incompatibility, Evidence/source, Entrenchment assessment), explicitly excluding possible worlds, Bayesian probabilities, logic engine, truth engine, LLM, topic hierarchy, and embedding as belonging to external regimes.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 2 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance -> DependenceStructure -> CorrectUncertaintyPropagation ... This is a major result
a_rows_sample.statement: States provenance's mathematical role: it enables estimating dependency and hence correct uncertainty propagation, called a major result.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance -> Dependency -> Redundancy/Synergy -> ResourceAllocation. Now they become inputs to portfolio optimization
a_rows_sample.statement: States portfolio optimization needs dependency information, chaining provenance and dependency graphs into redundancy/synergy detection and resource allocation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CommonCause(E_1,E_2). The provenance graph becomes an epistemic dependency graph. This is critical for statistical aggregation
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a common-cause predicate extending provenance into an epistemic dependency graph for statistical aggregation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SalesEvidence -> SalesClaim -> Translation -> BillingClaim. Otherwise the target claim looks as though it originated directly from Billing
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires translation provenance preserving the full source-to-target lineage.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For E_A translated into E_B, we preserve Lineage(E_B) superset Lineage(E_A). This allows downstream users to inspect the original context
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes evidence lineage preservation across translation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a cross-context claim should have lineage SourceClaim -> MappingVersion -> TranslatedClaim -> Decision. This is essential for auditability
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes translation lineage as essential for auditability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge graph G_K ... Provenance/dependency graph G_P ... Identity graph G_I ... These graphs must interact but must not be collapsed into one undifferentiated graph
a_rows_sample.statement: States the three-graph architectural distinction: knowledge, provenance/dependency, and identity graphs must interact without collapsing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence E1 -> Claim A, Evidence E2 -> Claim B, Evidence E3 -> Claim C, all -> Decision Gate, with provenance and dependency edges
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents an assurance graph connecting evidence, claims, and the decision gate via provenance/dependency edges.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The reviewer proposes a "Provenance Domain" ... Verdict: PROVENANCE is not a missing domain — it is a DISPERSED, NAMED, PARTLY-GOVERNED concern
b_rows_sample.statement: A check-before-recording pass finds provenance already lives in the corpus as: one axis of AUTHORITY itself (provenance x standing, Engineering Progression Model, PM-1), the PROVENANCE non-progression kind, identity discipline (CAP-001), evidence grading practice ([FETCHED]/[CANONICAL]/[2nd-hand]), and append-only evidence/traceability blocks. Verdict: provenance is a dispersed, named, partly-governed concern (the SP-5 pattern recognized a third time), not a missing domain. Disposition: the provenance questions enrich the existing Tier-1 Knowledge Governance stream (PM-1); 'Provenance as a strategic domain' is recorded as a hypothesis routed to the docket, admissible only if a live stream produces evidence requiring it; the identity-chain observation (CAP-001 as foundation if provenance grows) is a watch item, not a promotion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: U-GR-2 | Provenance: enrichment of Knowledge Governance (current disposition) or eventually its own domain?
b_rows_sample.statement: U-GR-2: whether provenance remains an enrichment of Knowledge Governance or eventually becomes its own domain, waiting on operational evidence from the live streams, not literature.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PM-1 ENRICHED (2026-08-03, external input): PROVENANCE as a named first-class concern
b_rows_sample.statement: PM-1 (provenance x standing) is enriched: industry treats provenance as a governance control plane (identity -> version -> retrieval event -> evidence -> answer -> audit), paralleling P4 and resting on identity discipline (CAP-001). Provenance already lives dispersed in the corpus (authority axis, non-progression kind, evidence grading, traceability blocks); 'Provenance as its own domain' is a hypothesis at the docket, not a new backlog stream — this row owns the questions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: authority = provenance × standing ... [CANONICAL] W3C PROV: derivation is an immutable provenance fact
b_rows_sample.statement: The formula authority = provenance x standing is supported by W3C PROV (derivation is an immutable provenance fact) and data-catalog practice (lineage != 'certified' flag are two independent fields in every major catalog). No challenge. Confidence: HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SC-5 | authority = provenance × standing in ONE field (its own header asks two questions)
b_rows_sample.statement: SC-5: authority combines provenance and standing into one field, though its own header asks two separate questions; open, routed to PM-1.

b_rows_sample.anchor: THE CORRECTION IS ACCEPTED IN FULL — AND IT IS MY FOURTH INSTANCE OF LEVEL CONFUSION ... I-4 is NOT falsified. I misdiagnosed a LIFECYCLE gap as an ONTOLOGY falsification
b_rows_sample.statement: A prior claim that I-4 was falsified is retracted: a discharge summary is not authoritative because it was projected, but became authoritative through DERIVED -> REVIEWED -> ATTESTED -> RELEASED; governance created the authority, not the derivation. The corrected conclusion is not 'DP-2 is wrong' but 'DP-2 conflates DERIVATION with ATTESTATION'. Four prior level confusions listed: flat vs dimensional (taxonomy), artifact vs concept (existence), layer vs sibling (ontology), lifecycle vs structure (this one). A fifth was avoided by checking: the author was about to report 'there is no lifecycle', when in fact nine exist.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The precise gap — located mechanically ... THE GAP: STATUS HAS A GOVERNED STATE MACHINE. AUTHORITY DOES NOT
b_rows_sample.statement: statuses.yaml and authorities.yaml are declared orthogonal but are not equally equipped: statuses.yaml has 8 values, a progression field (order), a terminal marker (settled), a defined who-may-move role table, and lint-checkable transition guards; authorities.yaml has 5 values and none of these. Authority gates a status transition, but nothing governs how authority itself changes — no rule for who may move derived->authoritative, and no guard for it. This is exactly the I-4 problem: attestation is an authority transition (derived->authoritative); because authority transitions are ungoverned, the model cannot express 'attested', so it collapses derived into 'never authoritative'. A prior reviewer's diagnosis ('DP-2 conflates derivation and attestation') now has a mechanical cause.

b_rows_sample.anchor: LG-1 (WITHDRAWN 2026-08-02 — ILL-POSED) ... authority is TWO dimensions in one field — immutable PROVENANCE × act-changed STANDING
b_rows_sample.statement: LG-1 ('should authority have a governed state machine?') is withdrawn as ill-posed: the question dissolved under discovery that authority is two dimensions in one field — immutable PROVENANCE (generated, derived) times act-changed STANDING (authoritative, provisional, historical). Provenance cannot have a state machine; standing changes by governance acts. Superseded by PM-1/PM-2, recorded in the Engineering Progression Model section 4.

b_rows_sample.anchor: LG-2 | Restate DP-2 to separate DERIVATION from ATTESTATION?
b_rows_sample.statement: LG-2: should DP-2 be restated to separate DERIVATION from ATTESTATION — this is CV-1, now with a mechanical cause; routed to the ARB.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 2. CANDIDATE — supported by evidence, awaiting ruling or more evidence (K-1..K-15)
b_rows_sample.statement: Fifteen candidate concerns, each citing its supporting commission and what it waits on: K-1 dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model; K-2 the archetype set (strong: DOMAIN/PROCESS/CAPABILITY/KNOWLEDGE/ARTIFACT/RUNTIME ASSET/PROJECTION; weaker: CONTAINER; weakest: PURPOSE); K-3 the four partial orders (authority, production, realization, containment); K-4 11 invariant relationships vs 8 implementation choices; K-5 DP-n as capability anchor; K-6 Knowledge Space = declared boundary+owner+constitution; K-7 authority = provenance x standing, four progression kinds; K-8 the strategic domain set PD-1/2/3/5; K-9 viewpoints as presentation; K-10 decision-readiness as the platform's product; K-11 FREEZE/RETIRE as insufficiency evidence; K-12 PKS extends context-engineering with governance; K-13 the canon-track reference artifacts themselves; K-14 the mission is enacted via 8 artifacts; K-15 ownership splits (candidate-unowned=ladder working, operating-unowned=defect, sole instance Runtime Adapter).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Convergences — conclusions this track reached that the blind review reproduced (items 1-12)
b_rows_sample.statement: Twelve conclusions reproduced blind, now carrying double independent derivation: (1) KnowledgeOS is a hypothesis, gate shut, Vision unapproved; (2) 'PublicDigit is the laboratory' rejected against ADR-AIP-02, Product Primacy governs; (3) the EKP is a real governed context with named individual owner; (4) Engineering Governance is the strongest bounded context; (5) the reusable kernel list, near-identical; (6) designed-for-reuse != demonstrated-reusable (verbatim convergence); (7) individual EKP ownership is a succession risk, sharpened to 'separation of duties is real as process and unevidenced as people'; (8) three knowledge ontologies coexist unreconciled; (9) domain-free methodology sits in product paths, placement breached, plus a new instance (Platform_Capability_Pattern); (10) PMR-10's manual adoption failed, sharpened into a falsification of the Reference Architecture's protocol-suffices stance; (11) most of the 11 invariants reproduced with citations, with I-8 downgraded to invariant-in-waiting; (12) the split verdict itself (enacted internal mission vs unratified product vision).

b_rows_sample.anchor: TWO CONCESSIONS BEFORE THE MODEL ... INTENDED is WITHDRAWN as a fourth evidence grade ... Intent is not evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: A prior 'INTENDED' evidence grade is withdrawn: intent is not evidence, and applying the repository's own rule (determine whether a proposal is a new dimension, an overloaded existing dimension, or merely another value) shows INTENDED was an overloaded existing dimension, added inside a document about evidence discipline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The four concerns, separated as required ... A fifth concern the repository already separates ... TRUST/PROVENANCE = authorities.yaml
b_rows_sample.statement: Four concerns mapped to dimensions: EVIDENCE (D-V, new), GOVERNANCE (D-III, existing/executable via statuses.yaml), OPERATIONAL STATE (D-VI, new), INTENT (derived: f(GOVERNANCE-STATUS, OWNER), both fields already exist). A fifth concern the repository already separates, worth naming so it is not re-added later: TRUST/PROVENANCE = authorities.yaml (authoritative, derived, generated, historical, provisional), and statuses.yaml already declares status independent of authority — the repository was doing orthogonal dimensions before this commission asked for them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: LG-1 was solution design, conceded ... exactly what DDD forbids. I located an asymmetry and immediately proposed its repair
b_rows_sample.statement: LG-1 ('missing transitions -> need a state machine') is conceded as solution design: an inference from a missing implementation to a model, which DDD forbids — an asymmetry was located and its repair immediately proposed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The reviewer's "that chain is QUALIFICATION, not authority" — CONFIRMED by the repository ... DERIVED → REVIEWED → ATTESTED → RELEASED describes a document becoming more trustworthy
b_rows_sample.statement: A reviewer's claim that the DERIVED->REVIEWED->ATTESTED->RELEASED chain describes qualification, not authority, is confirmed: the repository already has vocabulary for it (ES-006.1's qualification stage, ES-003 Qualification), though 'Qualification' also carries a recorded UL collision (verification activity vs promotion-ladder stage), now with a third candidate sense (the standing-assignment chain).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The progression mechanisms — inventoried as evidence (P-1..P-10)
b_rows_sample.statement: Ten progression mechanisms inventoried as observations, not assumed lifecycles: P-1 document status (8 values, order+settled+roles+guards); P-2 Authority (5 values with rank, no order/roles/guards); P-3 ES-006.1 promotion ladder; P-4 Methodology maturity; P-5 ADR-M status; P-6 Capability lifecycle; P-7 EEP (plan->...->decide); P-8 Observation Protocol (ACTIVE->CONCLUDED); P-9 Identifier lifecycles (4 series); P-10 Evidence accumulation (n=0->n=1->n>=2). A prior canonical distinction (Reference Model section 6, GEP-F1: two lifecycles never conflated, governance-artifact vs governed-work) is found before theorizing; this discovery extends that refusal rather than founding it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The flagship finding — authority is not one dimension ... authorities.yaml's own header asks TWO questions in ONE field: "how much should I trust this and where did it come from?"
b_rows_sample.statement: authorities.yaml's five values answer two different questions: 'generated' and 'derived' answer provenance (where did it come from), and can never change (origin is an immutable historical fact); 'authoritative', 'provisional', and 'historical' answer standing (how much should I trust it), and can change by a governance act. This dissolves LG-1 ('should authority have a governed state machine?') rather than answering it: half of authority cannot have a state machine (provenance never changes) and the other half changes by governance acts recorded as act-logs, not workflows. Authority = an immutable PROVENANCE fact x a mutable STANDING judgment; attestation changes standing, nothing changes provenance. This also explains why the I-4 confusion was persistent: 'derived' (provenance) was wrongly read as entailing low standing, but a signed financial statement can be derived in provenance and authoritative in standing simultaneously.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PM-1 | Should authority's two questions — provenance and standing — be separated?
b_rows_sample.statement: PM-1: should authority's two questions, provenance and standing, be separated — this supersedes LG-1, which is withdrawn as ill-posed — authority: ARB + PD-3's owner.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PM-2 | Should standing-changes (attestation, supersession) get the role/guard treatment status-changes have?
b_rows_sample.statement: PM-2: should standing-changes get the role/guard treatment status-changes have — an act-governance question, not a state-machine question — authority: ARB.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Invariant relationships vs implementation choices ... I-1..I-11 ... 11 invariants · 8 choices
b_rows_sample.statement: Eleven invariants traced to governed statements: I-1 Knowledge is represented by an Artifact, an Artifact is never the Knowledge; I-2 a Capability protects exactly one invariant; I-3 a Knowledge Space has a declared boundary; I-4 (underspecified, not false — holds until attestation, reclassified as a lifecycle gap not an ontology falsification, per DP-2's conflation of derivation with attestation); I-5 one authoritative artifact per topic+context (lint-enforced); I-6 the Runtime never owns Knowledge; I-7 a PKS never contains reusable Method (stated and breached); I-8 governance precedes automation; I-9 governance-status orthogonal to authority; I-10 a constitutional principle is void-overriding; I-11 (restated 2026-08-02: Knowledge does not execute, capabilities execute, knowledge constrains and informs generation — the restatement survived cross-product projection where the original would have failed). Eight implementation choices (folder mapping, markdown as representation, YAML/Mermaid, the graph's declared scope, Claude Code as the n=1 runtime adapter, frontmatter, identifier formats, Mermaid+markdown projections) may change freely without breaking the model — that distinction is what makes this a platform rather than a repository layout.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'formal-provenance-lineage-audit-graph' POSSIBLY relates to 'provenance' (batch B0022). Note: Recurring label across S0928, S0929, S0931, S0932, S0933, S0934, S0936 for the formal provenance/dependency/lineage graph underlying uncertainty propagation, common-cause detection, translation lineage, backward error-propagation, and assurance graphs; closely related to, and possibly identical with, the already-registered provenance and claim-provenance-chain objects. Added here to satisfy the batch's own label-registration requirement; a future merge review should determine whether this collapses into those existing objects.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A Knowledge Projection is not merely what is stored. It is a representation plus assumptions plus a reasoning semantics that determines what can be concluded from it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gelfond & Kahl independently confirm that the KnowledgeOS Kernel should not itself be 'the reasoning engine': their architecture separates representation language + reasoning algorithms + agent architecture. A Knowledge Projection is not merely what is stored but representation + assumptions + reasoning semantics determining what can be concluded (Knowledge Space -> Domain Model/Representation -> Reasoning Regime -> Query -> Answer).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown is not simply an error state. It is a legitimate epistemic condition.
a_rows_sample.statement: ASP answer-set semantics give TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN query results and ground at least three distinct kinds of 'unknown': unknown because alternatives remain (P and ¬P both possible), unknown because the agent is unaware (neither represented), and unknown because a default was blocked (an exception/missing condition prevented an otherwise-applicable default). The earlier flat UNKNOWN category should become an Epistemic Status taxonomy: true/false/unresolved-alternatives/not-represented-unaware/defeasibly-inferable-but-blocked/etc; the exact taxonomy remains a research question but the distinction itself is now strongly grounded.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS should not have one universal "knowledge confidence" number.
a_rows_sample.statement: P-log's probabilistic extension shows probability quantifies a rational agent's degree of belief within an explicitly represented knowledge base/model (P(P|KB,R)), but 'Knowledge = P' is still wrong — probability belongs to an epistemic regime, not to knowledge itself; this confirms KnowledgeOS should not have one universal knowledge-confidence number, since different regimes expose different dimensions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P-log is **probabilistically nonmonotonic**: adding information can add possible worlds and substantially change the probabilistic model, including through Bayesian learning.
a_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge evolution (KB_t -> KB_t+1) can change the space of possibilities itself (Ω_t -> Ω_t+1) and therefore the probability of a statement (P_t(P) -> P_t+1(P)), not merely which statements are believed — validating the 'knowledge is continuously changing' and 'movement through infinite Knowledge Space' intuitions with a precise mechanism (Bayesian learning changing possible-world sets).

a_rows_sample.anchor: This reinforces our decision not to put Fagin's possible-world model into the Kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: ASP answer sets and P-log possible worlds are both representations used for reasoning, not the universal Knowledge Space itself — the architecture becomes INFINITE KNOWLEDGE SPACE -> PRESERVED SUBSTRATE -> {ASP regime, possible-world regime, Bayesian regime, revision regime, causal regime, other regimes}, reinforcing the earlier decision to keep Fagin's possible-world model out of the Kernel.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A knowledge projection must support retraction of derived conclusions without rewriting the historical inputs from which those conclusions were previously derived.
a_rows_sample.statement: Default reasoning (e.g. 'normally car is not broken') shows that a new observation can withdraw a previously derived default conclusion while the historical observations and the default rule itself remain unchanged — only the derived epistemic projection changes. This yields the principle that a knowledge projection must support retraction of derived conclusions without rewriting historical inputs, and implies three things KnowledgeOS must preserve separately: INPUT HISTORY (observations/sources/rules/assumptions), DERIVATION HISTORY (what was inferred, under which regime, from which inputs), and CURRENT PROJECTION (what is currently supported/derived) — proposed as a major Kernel principle.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t^A = Project(H_{\le t},D,R,A)
a_rows_sample.statement: A knowledge snapshot is reconstructible from history<=t, domain model D, reasoning regime R, and participant A: K_t^A = Project(H_{<=t}, D, R, A) — a stronger form of the earlier S_t^A equation. Distinguishes World state (W_t), Agent epistemic state (K_t^A), and Knowledge projection/view (V_t^A / P_t^A) as different things: the world can change without the agent knowing, and the agent's knowledge can change without the world changing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A gap is not merely: UNKNOWN. It can be: observation incompatible with current model
a_rows_sample.statement: A diagnostic agent stores observations + its own actions + history, detecting new observations incompatible with possible past trajectories and searching for explanations involving previously unobserved exogenous actions (e.g. expected bulb lit, observed not-lit, possible explanations: bulb broke/relay broke/surge occurred). A knowledge gap is therefore not merely UNKNOWN but can be 'observation incompatible with current model', giving rise to diagnostic hypotheses — proposing a richer set of epistemic situations (SUPPORTED, REFUTED, UNRESOLVED, INCOMPLETE, CONFLICTING, UNEXPECTED, DEFAULT-SUPPORTED, PROBABILISTIC, HYPOTHESIZED, OUT-OF-SCOPE) that must remain outputs of different analytical regimes rather than one universal enum.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ## Knowledge Expansion Tolerance
a_rows_sample.statement: Elaboration tolerance: a good knowledge representation should allow the domain to be expanded/modified without forcing large-scale restructuring of existing representation (e.g. a Spanish-language database incorporated via a translation relation without rewriting existing 'father' relations). Yields the Knowledge Expansion Tolerance principle: adding a new concept/relation/source/domain/language/rule/exception should not require redesigning unrelated knowledge; supports 'language should remain a projection/access layer, not the Kernel ontology.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Hierarchy is one projection of Knowledge Space, not Knowledge Space itself.
a_rows_sample.statement: Hierarchy/inheritance (vehicle->car->electric car) is a representation technique useful for inheritance, not necessarily the structure of the entire Knowledge Space — concepts like causality, evidence, institution, agent, time, question may cross hierarchy boundaries, so hierarchy is one projection of Knowledge Space, not Knowledge Space itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Absence of representation must never be interpreted without an explicit epistemic policy.
a_rows_sample.statement: ASP can represent both open-world (not known -> unknown) and closed-world (not known -> assume false) assumptions; absence of representation must never be interpreted without an explicit epistemic policy — proposed as a KnowledgeOS invariant. Relatedly, NULL != FALSE != UNKNOWN != NOT APPLICABLE must be preserved as distinct semantic values, unlike a typical database that collapses them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### K-INV-08 — Absence is not automatically false
a_rows_sample.statement: Eight further Kernel invariants: K-INV-08 Absence is not automatically false (meaning of absence depends on the declared epistemic policy); K-INV-09 Derived knowledge must retain its derivation context (a conclusion from default D is not equivalent to a directly observed fact); K-INV-10 Historical observations are not overwritten by revised beliefs (a later contradiction changes the projection, not the historical observation); K-INV-11 Assumptions must be distinguishable from observations; K-INV-12 Prediction must be distinguishable from observation; K-INV-13 Explanation must be distinguishable from fact; K-INV-14 Probabilities are regime-specific, not universal truth values; K-INV-15 A knowledge representation must expose its epistemic assumptions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS may preserve computationally representable epistemic states without claiming that those states exhaust the philosophical nature of knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gelfond & Kahl's computational model of an agent's represented beliefs does not contradict Williamson's non-reduction claim: it models computationally representable epistemic states, not a metaphysical analysis of knowledge itself. This distinction (computational representation vs philosophical exhaustiveness) should remain explicit in KnowledgeOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge, as modeled by KnowledgeOS, is a bounded, time-dependent epistemic state of a participant or collective...
a_rows_sample.statement: Refined working definitions: Knowledge is a bounded, time-dependent epistemic state of a participant or collective, oriented toward a part of the unbounded Knowledge Space, represented by commitments, observations, assumptions, rules, available alternatives, evidential support, inferential consequences, and applicable uncertainties under an explicitly declared epistemic regime — the representation is not identical to knowledge itself. Knowledge Space is the unbounded space of entities, states, events, concepts, relations, institutional structures, propositions, explanations and possible connections toward which finite participants orient observation/reasoning. The KnowledgeOS Kernel is the domain-independent preservation substrate making bounded knowledge projections reconstructible (identity, context, boundary, participant, time, inputs/observations, content references, commitments/assessments, provenance, relations, conflicts, transitions, history), leaving semantics/reasoning to explicit external epistemic regimes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ## **Epistemic Model Separation Principle**
a_rows_sample.statement: Epistemic Model Separation Principle: 'KnowledgeOS must separate the preserved epistemic substrate from the model and reasoning regime used to derive a knowledge projection from that substrate,' formalized as H_t --projection under regime R--> K_t^R, where different regimes may produce different projections from the same history H_t. Also reframes the earlier Commitment/Entitlement/Knowledge Kernel candidates into Core preservation (Content, Input, History, Participant, Context, Commitment/assessment, Relations, Transition, Provenance) vs Derived epistemic machinery (Entitlement, Belief, Knowledge, Default conclusion, Possible world, Probability, Explanation, Prediction), and gives Ω -> H_t -> P_R(H_t) -> K_t^R with K_t^{A,R1} != K_t^{B,R2} not implying different underlying realities.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS should probably model **four things separately**: 1. KNOWLEDGE SPACE... 2. PRESERVED KNOWLEDGE HISTORY... 3. EPISTEMIC MODEL... 4. KNOWLEDGE CLAIM
a_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeOS should model four non-interchangeable things separately: (1) KNOWLEDGE SPACE — the unbounded conceptual object; (2) PRESERVED KNOWLEDGE HISTORY — what KnowledgeOS actually stores; (3) EPISTEMIC MODEL — a participant/regime's current structured view; (4) KNOWLEDGE CLAIM — an attributed statement that a participant knows something. Also gives a full Kernel candidate list (Identity, Context/Boundary, Participant, Time, Content reference, Observation/Input, Commitment/Assessment, Provenance, Inferential relation, Epistemic transition, History, Regime reference) and an explicit outside-Kernel list (ASP, FOL, Bayesian networks, P-log, possible-world semantics, default-reasoning/planning/diagnostic/causal-inference algorithms, LLM, embeddings, vector search, Pāṇinian grammar, Dhātu extraction, topological analysis, specific domain ontology).

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would now consider this a major refinement of the KnowledgeOS model rather than just another lens.
a_rows_sample.statement: Closing self-assessment: Gelfond & Kahl provide 'the missing computational validation' of the research direction reached so far (declarative representation kept separate from reasoning algorithms; tolerates elaboration; represents incomplete/defeasible knowledge; models dynamic transitions/histories; diagnoses unexpected observations; adds probabilistic reasoning without collapsing forms into one mechanism), classified as a major refinement of the KnowledgeOS model, not merely another lens.

a_rows_sample.anchor: L(p)= 1 if p belongs to every A_i; 0 if ¬p belongs to every A_i; ? otherwise
a_rows_sample.statement: Logical entailment status L(p) derived directly from ASP answer-set semantics (1 if p in every answer set, 0 if ¬p in every answer set, unresolved otherwise) — a genuinely mathematical quantity stronger than an LLM confidence score. A related but explicitly-labeled-as-proposed (not from the source book) model-support ratio S_model(p)=|{A_i:p∈A_i}|/n is flagged as a modelling choice, not automatically a probability, distinct from P-log's genuinely probabilistic P_R(p|KB).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Store the substrate; compute the measure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Core architectural rule: 'Store the substrate; compute the measure' — a metric is an assessment of the preserved substrate, not a property permanently attached to the knowledge itself; the Kernel must not be contaminated with numbers like confidence=0.83, PageRank=0.67, entropy=1.42, stability=0.91 unless explicitly recorded as assessments produced by named regimes. Consistent with Gelfond & Kahl's representation/reasoning-algorithm separation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We should not search for one universal scalar called "amount of knowledge." We should define a knowledge element mathematically and then quantify different properties of that element under an explicitly declared epistemic regime.
b_rows_sample.statement: Central conclusion: a knowledge element is e=(p,a,c,τ,r,E,D,σ) where p=proposition/content, a=participant, c=context+boundary+LoA, τ=temporal scope, r=epistemic/reasoning regime, E=evidence/input references, D=derivation/inferential structure, σ=current epistemic status (itself possibly multidimensional, not scalar). A knowledge state K_t^{a,R,C} is the set of such elements for a given participant/regime/context up to time t, supporting K_t^A≠K_t^B without different underlying realities. Not yet a Kernel schema, but a mathematical research model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K(e)=(L,P,U,T,I,X,S,M,C,G)
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a ten-dimensional Knowledge Measurement Vector K(e)=(L,P,U,T,I,X,S,M,C,G) — logical support, probabilistic support, unknownness, provenance/traceability, inferential relevance, conflict, stability, margin, scope coverage, explanatory/information gain — kept as separate dimensions, never collapsed into one scalar. A scalar Score(e)=Σw_i q_i(e) is allowed only when a specific purpose determines the weights (e.g. audit weights provenance heavily, troubleshooting weights explanatory gain, research weights uncertainty, governance weights authority+provenance+conflict); Pareto-frontier analysis is preferred over a weighted scalar because weighting can hide dimensions like 'high evidence, high conflict, high importance, low stability'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: L(p)= 1 if p belongs to every A_i; 0 if ¬p belongs to every A_i; ? otherwise
b_rows_sample.statement: Logical entailment status L(p) derived directly from ASP answer-set semantics (1 if p in every answer set, 0 if ¬p in every answer set, unresolved otherwise) — a genuinely mathematical quantity stronger than an LLM confidence score. A related but explicitly-labeled-as-proposed (not from the source book) model-support ratio S_model(p)=|{A_i:p∈A_i}|/n is flagged as a modelling choice, not automatically a probability, distinct from P-log's genuinely probabilistic P_R(p|KB).

b_rows_sample.anchor: U(e) ∈ {alternative, unrepresented, blocked-default, outside-scope, computationally-unresolved}
b_rows_sample.statement: Unknownness U(e) is proposed not as a Boolean but a classification (alternative / unrepresented / blocked-default / outside-scope / computationally-unresolved), with the exact taxonomy left empirical and countable for future statistical analysis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Stability(p) = Pr[status(p) remains unchanged under relevant perturbation]. ... Margin(p) = |{K'∈N(K):p remains supported}| / |N(K)|
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes formal candidates for revision stability (Stability(p)=1-E[d_p(K,K')]/d_max, or Pr[status unchanged under relevant perturbation]) and epistemic margin (Margin(p)=|{K' in neighborhood N(K): p remains supported}|/|N(K)|), giving a mathematical form to the Williamson-derived knowledge-margin concept; notes margin requires defining what counts as a 'nearby' state, which is where topology/perturbation theory/statistics enter.

b_rows_sample.anchor: IG(E;H) = H(H)-H(H|E)
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes an information-theoretic explanatory-value/information-gain measure IG(E;H)=H(H)-H(H|E) over a hypothesis/explanation space H given evidence E, and AnswerGain(Q,A)=H(Hypotheses|Q)-H(Hypotheses|Q,A) as a candidate answer to 'how concrete is an answer to a question' — explicitly flagged as the document's own proposed statistical extension, not a claim from Gelfond & Kahl (who provide only the computational explanation framework).

b_rows_sample.anchor: We cannot quantify "how much of the infinite Knowledge Space we know." We can quantify: **coverage of a declared finite inquiry boundary.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Coverage(K,C)=|relevant elements represented/assessed|/|Ω_C| is only meaningful relative to a declared finite scope Ω_C; since the full Knowledge Space Ω is infinite, |K|/|Ω| is explicitly stated to be useless — coverage of a declared finite inquiry boundary is the defensible quantity, not coverage of the infinite space itself.

type_signature.domain: knowledge state K, declared scope C

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### External adequacy ... ### Predictive adequacy ... ### Refinement stability
b_rows_sample.statement: Since d(K,Ω) cannot be computed directly (Ω is not a finite reference set), proposes three orientation-toward-the-infinite-Knowledge-Space proxies: External adequacy (independent verification success), Predictive adequacy (Pr[prediction correct]), and Refinement stability (as scope C1⊂C2⊂C3 expands, does d(Projection(C1), Restriction(Projection(C2),C1))→0?) — called a candidate formalization of 'serve the nature of the Knowledge Space'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A. Representation measurements ... B. Epistemic measurements ... C. Task measurements
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three fundamentally different measurement families: Representation measurements (coverage, provenance, completeness, semantic consistency, traceability — how well is knowledge represented), Epistemic measurements (entailment, uncertainty, probability, conflict, stability, margin, entrenchment — how strong is the current epistemic position), Task measurements (answer resolution, prediction accuracy, explanation gain, diagnostic accuracy, planning success, decision utility — how useful is the knowledge) — described as much better than one 'knowledge score'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Store the substrate; compute the measure.
b_rows_sample.statement: Core architectural rule: 'Store the substrate; compute the measure' — a metric is an assessment of the preserved substrate, not a property permanently attached to the knowledge itself; the Kernel must not be contaminated with numbers like confidence=0.83, PageRank=0.67, entropy=1.42, stability=0.91 unless explicitly recorded as assessments produced by named regimes. Consistent with Gelfond & Kahl's representation/reasoning-algorithm separation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KS=(V,E,\tau,\Gamma,\Pi)
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes an overall model KS=(V,E,τ,Γ,Π) — typed knowledge-bearing entities V, typed relations E, temporal structure τ, preserved histories/provenance Γ, projection specifications Π — with Projection_{R,P,C,t}(KS)->K_t^{P,R,C} and a metric M_R(...)->R^n. Proposes a typed vertex vocabulary (Entity, Event, Observation, Proposition, Assertion, Commitment, Rule, Assumption, Evidence, Question, Explanation, InstitutionalStatus, KnowledgeAttribution) rather than one undifferentiated 'knowledge element', and a small universal relation vocabulary (represents, observed-from, asserted-by, supported-by, derived-from, implies, contradicts, qualifies, supersedes, questions, answers, explains, causes, counts-as, authorized-by, valid-at), noting not all relations are necessarily Kernel primitives.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A knowledge element is a context- and time-bounded epistemic unit consisting of a proposition or meaningful content attributed to a participant...
b_rows_sample.statement: Final working (not philosophically final) definitions: a knowledge element is a context/time-bounded epistemic unit (proposition/content attributed to a participant, with provenance, evidential basis, inferential/deontic relationships, assumptions, current epistemic assessment under a declared regime); a knowledge state is the evolving collection/relational configuration of such elements available at a point in time; the Knowledge Space is the unbounded space toward which finite states are oriented, which KnowledgeOS does not contain but preserves structures to reconstruct/compare finite projections of; the Kernel is the minimal preservation substrate for those projections and histories, with mathematical/statistical quantification belonging to external epistemic/analytical regimes. Recommends stopping the search for a single 'knowledge quantity' in favor of designing a Knowledge Measurement Vector + Knowledge State Distance + Projection Refinement test.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We must not combine coverage, evidence, confidence, stability and information gain simply because all happen to produce numbers.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extensive measurement requires associativity, ordering, monotonicity, and Archimedean conditions for f(a⊕b)=f(a)+f(b) to be legitimate — so a proposed EvidenceTotal=E1+E2+...+En is not automatically meaningful without first demonstrating the empirical operation supports additive measurement. Conjoint measurement gives conditions under which u(a,b)=u1(a)+u2(b) has meaning, so the multidimensional Knowledge Vector Q_K=(C,E,U,S,IG,...) may only be collapsed into Score(Q_K) if the empirical preference/ordering structure supports an additive conjoint representation — otherwise keep the vector.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Faith (Shraddha) is not blind belief. It is epistemic trust that varies by quality (Sattva, Rajas, Tamas). The quality of faith determines the quality of knowledge, action, and outcome.
a_rows_sample.statement: Thesis: faith/trust is not binary but has three qualities (Sattva/Rajas/Tamas) which determine the quality of downstream knowledge, action and outcome; framed as the 'missing quality assurance and trust verification layer' of KnowledgeOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Quality(Evidence) ∈ {Sattva, Rajas, Tamas} ... Quality(Assessment) ∈ {Sattva, Rajas, Tamas} ... Quality(Discipline) ∈ {Sattva, Rajas, Tamas} ... Quality(KnowledgeSharing) ∈ {Sattva, Rajas, Tamas}
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies a uniform three-valued quality classification (Sattva=high-quality/unbiased/selfless, Rajas=emotionally-charged/self-serving/status-driven, Tamas=low-quality/biased/harmful) across four distinct KnowledgeOS dimensions: evidence, assessment, discipline, and knowledge-sharing — each treated as an instance of the same generic Quality(X) function.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Classify(X) = Sattva if Integrity(X) > Passion(X) + Ignorance(X); Rajas if Passion(X) > Integrity(X) + Ignorance(X); Tamas if Ignorance(X) > Integrity(X) + Passion(X)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a comparative classification rule for the three-valued quality (pairwise-majority style: whichever of Integrity/Passion/Ignorance strictly dominates the sum of the other two) with no stated measurement procedure, units, or normalization for the three component quantities.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Trust(K_t) = Faith_Sattva(K_t) - Faith_Rajas(K_t) - Faith_Tamas(K_t) ... Trust(K_t) > 0 ⟺ System is Sattvic
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a scalar Trust(K_t) as the difference between a system's Sattvic faith component and the sum of its Rajasic and Tamasic components, with positive Trust equated to the system being classified 'Sattvic'.
