a_rows_sample.anchor: B(P,H) \rightarrow H^*
a_rows_sample.statement: From 2.41's one-pointed (resolute) vs many-branched (irresolute) buddhi: a proposition P entering the system can generate uncontrolled interpretation branching B_1->B_2->B_3->... (epistemic explosion / uncontrolled hypothesis proliferation). Proposes Buddhi as a branch-selection/branch-control operator B(P,H)->H*, where H is the hypothesis space and H* the currently admissible branch set -- explicitly warning Buddhi should NOT necessarily collapse all alternatives into one truth; it may instead produce labeled hypotheses {Primary, Alternative, Rejected, Unresolved}, compatible with the Zero/uncertainty model. Connects directly to Zero: if B(P)=QUALIFY/UNKNOWN then Zero(P)=1 (an epistemic gap).

a_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionQuality = f(Evidence,\,Rules,\,Context,\,Provenance,\,Buddhi)
a_rows_sample.statement: From 2.47 (right to duty, not to fruits) and 2.48 (samatva/equanimity toward success and failure): formalizes Decision validity != f(expected outcome); DecisionQuality = f(Evidence, Rules, Context, Provenance, Buddhi), with outcome recorded separately. Explicit warning against the outcome-based fallacy: a Kernel should not retroactively say 'the answer worked, therefore the reasoning was correct'. Assessed as R6 corroboration (not derivation) of the existing Command != Transformation / Action != Result distinction, consistent with Step 286 methodology.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \operatorname{Gate}(c,p)
a_rows_sample.statement: From 2.58's tortoise analogy (senses withdrawn and redeployed for particular purposes): proposes a channel-gating operator Gate(c,p) where c=channel, p=purpose/context, mapping to {OPEN,CLOSED,QUARANTINE,SUPPRESS}, e.g. Observation channel->OPEN, External distraction->CLOSED, Untrusted source->QUARANTINE, Irrelevant signal->SUPPRESS -- assessed as much more concrete than simply saying 'sense control'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: B_t \rightarrow Bias_t \rightarrow K_{t+1} \rightarrow Bias_{t+1}
a_rows_sample.statement: From 2.62's chain (contemplation -> attachment -> desire -> anger -> delusion -> loss of memory -> loss of intelligence): models an epistemic feedback-loop hazard, cautiously translated as repeated focus -> preference formation -> bias -> distorted evaluation -> bad state transition -> corrupted future decisions, formalized as B_t -> Bias_t -> K_{t+1} -> Bias_{t+1}. The kernel needs the ability to detect when its own previous state is improperly influencing current discrimination -- assessed as a significant research direction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal P(K_t) = (D_t,Q_t,S_t,-X_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines purification from 'increasing dimensions + increasing values' to a four-component vector P(K_t)=(D_t,Q_t,S_t,-X_t) where D_t=epistemic dimensional coverage, Q_t=quality/value of knowledge, S_t=stability of discrimination, X_t=epistemic distortion (subtracted). Illustrated by a worked example: five conflicting claims P,P',P'',P''',P'''' reduce in number after Buddhi labels them [supported]/[superseded]/[unsupported]/[contradicted]/[unknown], with the number of claims decreasing while epistemic quality increases -- reinforcing Knowledge growth != knowledge purification. Explicitly connects to but does not yet merge with the existing Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C), to avoid premature formulation-merging per Steps 285-287.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal{K}_{ernel} = (K_t,\ M_t,\ B_t,\ \delta,\ G_t,\ Z_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Concludes with candidate kernel K_ernel=(K_t,M_t,B_t,delta,G_t,Z_t) [knowledge state, mode/regime, Buddhi, transition, input/action gating, Zero detection] and fundamental cycle (K_t,M_t) --Observe--> O_t --Buddhi--> D_t --Gate--> A_t --delta--> K_{t+1} --Zero--> GAP_{t+1}. Explicitly designates this a 'Gita-derived research hypothesis', not canonical, pending testing against the eight primitives, Sigma, delta, Zero, Qualify, identity/equality, and the existing corpus. Proposes as the next intellectually important step deriving the smallest possible algebra of kernel operators (Buddhi, Gate, Discriminate, Qualify, Purify, Zero, Update, Mode-transition) across Chapters 2-18, explicitly checking which are genuinely derivable from KnowledgeOS vs purely Gita-inspired.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = \text{content} + \text{interpretation} + \text{relationships} + \text{epistemic condition}
b_rows_sample.statement: Expands K_t beyond 'what KnowledgeOS currently knows' to K_t = content + interpretation + relationships + epistemic condition, motivated by Arjuna having substantial information, observations, relationships and beliefs yet remaining unable to determine what to do -- his problem being conceptual gaps and an incomplete model, not merely missing facts. The kernel must operate on the quality and structure of knowledge, not simply its quantity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \operatorname{Reframe}(K_t) \rightarrow K'_t ... Knowledge\ transformation \neq Knowledge\ accumulation
b_rows_sample.statement: From the observation that Krishna progressively reframes Arjuna's conceptual model rather than merely supplying additional information: proposes Reframe(K_t)->K_t' as a potentially fundamental KnowledgeOS operation, where K_t={P_1,P_2,P_3} becomes K_t'={P_1',P_2',P_3'} with the same propositions interpreted under a different conceptual structure -- a knowledge state can change without adding new facts. Hence Knowledge transformation != Knowledge accumulation, added to candidate Buddhi operator set {Compare,Distinguish,Validate,Reject,Reframe,Determine}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z_t = \{ \text{unknown}, \text{uncertain}, \text{contradictory}, \text{unqualified}, \text{mis-modelled} \}
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends Zero's detected boundary types from missing-data-only to a five-category set Z_t = {unknown, uncertain, contradictory, unqualified, mis-modelled}, with 'mis-modelled' assessed as particularly important and new: a knowledge system may have many facts yet a wrong model (Arjuna's unknowns that he does not recognize as unknowns, more dangerous than ordinary missing information). Hence Zero != missing-data detector only; it becomes an epistemic boundary detector. Gives the chain (K_t,Z_t) --Buddhi--> D_t, and Knowledge != Decision != Action != Result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Buddhi(K_t,Z_t,M_t) \rightarrow D_t ... Unrecognized ignorance
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends Buddhi to include the operating mode: Buddhi(K_t,Z_t,M_t)->D_t, giving 'the same Knowledge State can produce different processing trajectories depending on the kernel's operating mode' as a testable hypothesis. Tamas failure mode: kernel encounters Z_t not-empty but behaves as though Z_t=empty, producing unrecognized ignorance; Rajas failure mode: continuous action Action_1->Action_2->Action_3 without sufficient discrimination -- the kernel needs self-regulation, connecting Chapter 6's discipline material to kernel architecture rather than mere commentary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal N\notin K_t ... The kernel is therefore not the Ātman.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly preserves and reaffirms N notin K_t (the Knower is not inside the current knowledge state) in the combined KOS_t=(K_t,Z_t,B_t,M_t,O_t,delta) model: N -> Kernel -> K_t but N notin K_t; the kernel is not the Atman. The mind/kernel analogy is useful because the kernel performs functions the philosophical model attributes to mind/buddhi, but the analogy must not become an ontological claim.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What is the smallest algebra of operations required for this kernel to reproduce the epistemic dynamics identified across Chapters 2–18?
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes stopping independent chapter analysis and instead deriving the smallest algebra of operations O_K={o_1,...,o_n} required to reproduce the epistemic dynamics identified across Chapters 2-18, testing each operator against 10 questions: input state, output state, preconditions, invariants, whether it changes K, whether it changes Sigma, whether it consumes evidence, whether it produces an Observation/Event/Action, whether Buddhi is required, whether the operator is mode-dependent. Explicitly framed as achievable without letting the Gita dictate the architecture: the Gita supplies the hypothesis, mathematics/DDD/the existing corpus determine whether the operator belongs.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'hpa-gita-chapter2-kernel-level-refinement-reframe-operator' POSSIBLY relates to 'hpa-gita-chapter2-branching-gating-purification-model' (batch B0054). Note: A second, distinct hpa treatment of Chapter 2 (companion to S2255), explicitly framed as a KERNEL-LEVEL REFINEMENT rather than a new layer. Expands K_t=content+interpretation+relationships+epistemic condition (from Arjuna having facts but an incomplete conceptual model). Introduces Reframe(K_t)->K_t' as a legitimate knowledge transformation distinct from accumulation (Knowledge transformation != Knowledge accumulation), motivated by Krishna progressively reframing Arjuna's conceptual model rather than adding facts. Extends Zero's boundary types to five: {unknown,uncertain,contradictory,unqualified,mis-modelled}, the last being a genuinely new category (many facts + wrong model). Gives the chain Knowledge != Decision != Action != Result. Reaffirms N notin K_t (the Knower remains outside the kernel) as an explicit architectural constraint. Proposes final candidate kernel (fraktur K)_t=(K_t,Z_t,M_t,B,O,delta) and a 10-question operator-testing checklist (input/output state, preconditions, invariants, whether it changes K or Sigma, whether it consumes evidence, whether it produces Observation/Event/Action, whether Buddhi is required, mode-dependence) as the concluding research direction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal K \neq \text{all individual knowledge statements} ... \mathcal K = D_1\times D_2\times \cdots \times D_n
a_rows_sample.statement: From Gita Chapter 10 (vibhutis, manifestations through which underlying reality is recognized): K (Knowledge Space) is not all individual knowledge statements but manifests through {manifestations/dimensions/forms}, motivating a structural question 'what are the fundamental dimensions through which knowledge manifests?' and a candidate structuring K = D_1 x D_2 x ... x D_n (each D_i a knowledge dimension), with K_t subset K, or equivalently the existing five-axis Sigma_t=(A_t,S_t,R_t,V_t,C_t) -- explicitly not claiming the answer is exactly five dimensions; that remains open.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sentence \rightarrow \text{Observation/Proposition} ... Dimension \rightarrow \text{independent axis along which propositions can vary}
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines the earlier 'can one sentence be a dimension of knowledge' question: a sentence is not necessarily a dimension; Sentence -> Observation/Proposition, while Dimension -> an independent axis along which propositions can vary. Worked example: 'System X runs on Tuesday' is a Proposition instantiating the dimensions Entity (X) and Time (Tuesday) -- the sentence instantiates dimensions, it does not itself constitute one.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A Zero does not necessarily mean "Nothing exists." It may mean "Nothing is represented in the currently observed projection."
a_rows_sample.statement: From Chapter 11's Visvarupa (universal form): a kernel may see only a local projection pi_X(K) while the theoretical whole is K, giving local knowledge != knowledge space as a whole. Reinterprets Zero accordingly: rather than meaning 'nothing exists', a Zero detection may mean 'nothing is represented in the currently observed projection' -- proposed as a much stronger formal interpretation, potentially important for the Zero theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \mathsf{Yoga}=\{\mathcal Y_1,\mathcal Y_2,\ldots,\mathcal Y_m\}
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines Yoga from a single operator into a family: Yoga = {Y_1,Y_2,...,Y_m}, where each Y_i is a transformation or discipline applied to an epistemic state, K_{t+1}=Y_i(K_t,O_t). Poses the research question: what transformations are permitted, and what properties must they preserve?

a_rows_sample.anchor: Buddhi \neq unrestricted inference ... Governance becomes structurally distinct from the kernel
a_rows_sample.statement: Explains the 'kernel can become its own enemy' worry: if the kernel transforms its own state without constraints (K_t ->F-> K_{t+1} ->F-> K_{t+2}...), it can create self-reinforcing errors, circular reasoning, confirmation loops, unjustified certainty, loss of provenance, and contradiction propagation. Therefore Buddhi != unrestricted inference; it needs constraints, and this is where Governance becomes structurally distinct from the kernel. Also refines Buddhi's codomain away from TRUE/FALSE toward {supported, contradicted, unknown, insufficient evidence, conflicting}, framed as more compatible with the Zero/uncertainty/qualification theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Is the KnowledgeOS kernel fundamentally a knowledge-storage mechanism, or is it a discriminative epistemic machine operating on changing knowledge states? ... Kernel \neq K_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses the culminating research question of Chapters 10-14: is the KnowledgeOS kernel fundamentally a storage mechanism, or a discriminative epistemic machine operating on changing knowledge states -- the Gita lens strongly points toward the latter. Formalized: Kernel != K_t; instead Kernel:(K_t,O_t,C_t)->K_{t+1}, with Buddhi subset-of Kernel capability and K_t = state operated upon. Connects this to Step 285's finding that the kernel itself is still not formally selected, keeping this as a new Gita-derived research hypothesis, not canonical. Proposes next step: derive a candidate formal algebra of the Kernel from Chapters 10-14 together, identifying which operations belong to Buddhi vs Mind/Kernel vs transform K_t vs must remain outside the kernel (Governance, authority, provenance).

b_rows_sample.anchor: \Omega = \text{epistemic horizon} ... Not: \Omega=\text{God} ... and not: \Omega=\mathcal K
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces Omega = epistemic horizon, representing the horizon against which the finite knowledge state is situated -- explicitly refusing the identities Omega=God and Omega=K (Knowledge Space), calling both unjustified architectural identities. Gives K_t != K even if |K|=infinity, protecting the theory from defining Moksha merely as 'infinite knowledge'. Extends the Chapter-13 Kshetra!=Kshetrajna separation with a four-way conceptual separation N != K_t != K != Omega (Knower, current state, whole knowledge space, horizon), explicitly conditioned on subsequent research confirming these distinctions are genuinely useful and non-redundant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Perspective(K_t) \rightarrow Perspective(K_{t+1}) ... Knowledge growth \neq fact accumulation
b_rows_sample.statement: Beyond ordinary growth K_t subset K_{t+1}, Chapter 11 suggests Perspective(K_t) -> Perspective(K_{t+1}): the system may restructure its relationship to existing facts (e.g. discovering relationships among A, B, C previously poorly understood) rather than merely acquire more facts. Hence Knowledge growth != fact accumulation, and epistemic transformation != simple state enlargement.

b_rows_sample.anchor: epistemic limitation = f(K_t,G_t) ... epistemic expansion = f(K_t,\Omega)
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a tension between two directions: Chapter 11's expansion (perspective toward the whole, epistemic expansion = f(K_t,Omega)) versus Chapter 14's conditioning (knowing conditioned by G_t, epistemic limitation = f(K_t,G_t)). Proposes the kernel continuously works between its current bounded state and an epistemic horizon that exceeds that state, closer to KnowledgeOS as a continuously active system.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Perceive / receive ... 5. Orient
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes the KnowledgeOS kernel may need five fundamentally different classes of work: (1) Perceive/receive O_t; (2) Represent O_t->K_t; (3) Discriminate B_t(K_t,O_t)->d_t; (4) Transform delta(K_t,d_t)->K_{t+1}; (5) Orient rho_t(K_t,Omega). The fifth (Orient) is said to become much more visible once Chapter 11 (the horizon Omega) is added to the model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: M\neq K_{\max} ... M\neq |\mathcal K|\rightarrow\infty ... M\sim\text{transformation of the relationship between Knower, Field and Horizon}
b_rows_sample.statement: With Chapters 11-14 combined, refuses modeling Moksha as the final Knowledge State: M != K_max and M != |K|->infinity. Proposes instead M ~ transformation of the relationship between Knower, Field and Horizon, combined with Chapter 14's transcendence of ordinary conditioning; the theoretical transition is not simply K_0->K_1->K_2->... but (N,K_t,rho_t,G_t,Omega) -> different epistemic regime.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel \neq Knowledge State ... Kernel \neq Knowledge Space ... The Knower is a philosophical abstraction.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reasserts the kernel must not be confused with the Knower: Kernel != Knowledge State and Kernel != Knowledge Space. Full research-model vocabulary listed: K=Knowledge Space, K_t=Knowledge State, N=Knower, Omega=Epistemic Horizon, rho_t=Epistemic Orientation, B_t=Discrimination/Buddhi, G_t=Operating Condition, delta=Knowledge-State Transformation, combined as (K_t,O_t,rho_t,G_t,Omega) --B_t--> d_t --delta--> K_{t+1}. Explicit correspondence-strength classification: strong correspondence (Kshetra/Kshetrajna<->Field/Knower); strong conceptual candidate (Buddhi<->Discrimination); interesting research hypotheses (Guna<->Operating condition; Chapter12<->Epistemic orientation); new research hypothesis (Chapter11<->Epistemic horizon); explicitly NOT established: Omega/rho/G/B are KnowledgeOS primitives; Omega=K; Moksha=K_max.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Is "Moksha" mathematically a fixed point, boundary, quotient, or **change of state space altogether**?
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses 'can a KnowledgeOS kernel be formally modeled as a discriminating dynamical system?' with X_{t+1}=F(X_t,O_t), X_t=(K_t,Sigma_t,G_t,rho_t), F=delta o B, and 14 concrete research questions: what are the primitive kernel operations; what is the algebra of Buddhi/discrimination; which operations are idempotent/commutative/monotonic; which create vs only transform information; which reduce vs introduce uncertainty; what exactly constitutes purification; can purification be an order on Sigma; is there a fixed point; is there a limit; is Moksha mathematically a fixed point, boundary, quotient, or a change of state space altogether. Flags the last as particularly interesting: Moksha might not be a state in the existing algebra but a transition to a different epistemic regime -- if that survives mathematical/DDD testing it would be a genuine theoretical contribution, not merely a Gita analogy.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(K_t,H_t) = \text{the detectable discrepancy between represented knowledge and the current epistemic horizon}
b_rows_sample.statement: Upgrades the Zero hypothesis from Zero(K_t)=what is missing to Zero(K_t,H_t) = the detectable discrepancy between represented knowledge and the current epistemic horizon H_t: Z_t = H_t minus K_t (only if horizon and state are sets over the same typed universe) or more safely Z_t=Delta(K_t,H_t). Motivated by the tree metaphor's point that what is visible is not the whole structure; also connects verse 15.17 (Supreme Person entering/supporting the three worlds) to a Knowledge Horizon concept where the kernel need not contain all knowledge, K_t subset K with a reachable horizon H_t, so Zero(K_t,H_t) can report 'outside the current epistemic horizon' rather than 'does not exist'.

a_notations: K = D_1 x D_2 x ... x D_n

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'hpa-gita-chapters10-14-manifestation-vibhuti-model' POSSIBLY relates to 'hpa-gita-chapters11-14-horizon-model' (batch B0054). Note: Adds Chapter 10 (Vibhuti, manifestations) beneath the Chapters 11-14 model, giving a five-chapter research model: manifestation(Ch10) -> observation(Ch11) -> Yoga-as-operator-family(Ch12) -> Ksetra/Ksetrajna field-knower(Ch13) -> guna state dynamics(Ch14). Proposes K != all individual knowledge statements but K -> {manifestations/dimensions/forms}, structuring K as a dimension product D_1 x ... x D_n; refines Sentence!=Dimension (sentence instantiates dimensions, e.g. Entity+Time, rather than being one); reinterprets Zero via local projection pi_X(K) so absence means 'not represented in the currently observed projection' rather than 'does not exist'; models Yoga as an operator family {Y_1,...,Y_m} rather than one operator; and argues Buddhi must not be unrestricted inference, requiring Governance as structurally distinct from the kernel to prevent self-reinforcing errors, circular reasoning, confirmation loops, and contradiction propagation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: IdentityMerge should be treated as a governed transition. ... Risk(identityMerge) > Risk(attributeUpdate).
a_rows_sample.statement: Identity merge is a high-impact, specially-governed transition because a wrong merge can contaminate History, Evidence, Decisions, Ownership, Compliance, and Causality all at once, effectively rewriting the meaning of the knowledge graph -- a much higher risk than a simple wrong attribute update.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I_50: Identity merge, split, and reassignment must be explicitly represented and lineage-preserving.
a_rows_sample.statement: New invariant I_50, flagged as likely constitutional-level: identity merge, split, and reassignment must be explicitly represented and lineage-preserving.

a_rows_sample.anchor: x \xrightarrow{resolvedAs} \{y,z\}. Historical records referring to x remain historically valid as references to the former representation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identity split example: when one entity x is discovered to have actually represented two distinct entities y and z, the correct model is x-resolvedAs->{y,z}, never a silent edit of x, so historical records referencing x remain historically valid references to the former (now-split) representation -- another instance of non-destructive correction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G_I=(V,E_I). ... sameAs, replaces, represents, hosts, derivedFrom, renamedTo. ... It is an identity/continuity graph.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a separate typed IdentityGraph G_I=(V,E_I) with edge types sameAs, replaces, represents, hosts, derivedFrom, renamedTo -- distinct from a generic knowledge graph, and itself requiring temporal qualification (e.g. NameAssignment(nexus,x,[t0,t1]) then NameAssignment(nexus,y,[t1,t2])) since Name->Identity is a temporal relation; replacement causality (DecisionToReplace->ReplacementAction) is likewise kept separate, since Replacement itself does not establish sameAs.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity equivalence must be transitive within a defined identity context.
b_rows_sample.statement: Resolves the standing transitivity problem for identity equivalence (cong_I), flagged unsafe by five independent loci (25J.27, 25S.6, 25S.29, 38.16, 38.47), via context-relativization: step-195's invariant I_48 states identity equivalence must be transitive within a defined identity context, justified by 38.6/38.7/38.81's principle that RealWorldIdentity != DomainObjectIdentity and identity is contextual (KnowledgeOS must not globally impose a GlobalEntityIdentity where a domain has intentionally separate identities). Conclusion: cong_I is an equivalence relation within an identity context and is NOT one across contexts, so quotients exist per-context and are undefined globally -- described as the first genuine closure recorded on the equality axis by this research programme. Two provisos: (1) this resolves identity equivalence cong_I, not semantic equality (whether semantic equality is transitive within a semantic context remains open, though 25I.11's context-indexed relation is the same move); (2) 'identity context' itself is nowhere defined, so I_48 is well-formed with an unbound parameter, the same defect shape as other unbound relevance/observation parameters elsewhere in the programme. Step 195.15 also names the violation pattern A cong B and B cong C and A not-cong C as an 'identity consistency violation', proposed as a candidate checkable invariant.

type_signature.domain: reference x reference (within a fixed identity context)

b_rows_sample.anchor: three concepts, three questions, three answers ... Continuity appears in NONE of the five registers reconciled in Step 288
b_rows_sample.statement: Recovers 'Continuity' as a sixth relation absent from every register the programme had reconciled: Identity ('is it the same entity?'), Continuity ('does the history of one connect meaningfully to the other?'), and Similarity ('how much does it resemble the other?') are three distinct, non-collapsible concepts (195.21), with Similarity always evidence FOR identity or continuity, never either itself (195.21, 38.77: Similarity != Identity). Continuity is functionally defined: Continuity(x,y) = f(IdentityRelation, TransitionLineage, DomainRules, Evidence) (195.51) -- a relation between entities across a lineage, distinct from history-relating relations and reference-relating relations. 195.24 (boxed): Identity and Lineage are ORTHOGONAL (same identity/different states; different identity WITH continuity; different identity/no continuity), agreeing independently with a separately-cited Step 261.9 finding that Identity and Provenance equality are independent dimensions. Consequence: the equality-family register is nine relations, not eight, and Continuity is unique in having a functional definition rather than a predicate one.

type_signature.codomain: UNSTATED (functional composition of IdentityRelation, TransitionLineage, DomainRules, Evidence)

b_rows_sample.anchor: Without locale/context, normalization is ambiguous -> Normalization is itself an epistemic operation ... Canonicalization must follow evidence, not precede it
b_rows_sample.statement: Downgrades structural equality's decidability: Step 288 had placed '=' at Level 5 (decidable) throughout, qualified only by the id/mutable-state contradiction. Three loci show the decidability is itself conditional: 38.53 gives an ambiguous date string ('03/04/2026', 3 April or 4 March) showing normalization is itself an epistemic operation requiring locale/context; 38.85 states canonicalization must follow evidence, not precede it; 012 section 27 states canonicalization is not truth. Conclusion: '=' is decidable only relative to a fixed canonicalization, which the corpus forbids fixing a priori; the same defect applies to exact equality (defined as canonical serialization plus hash, 25J.2). Corrected count: zero state-level relations are unconditionally at Level 5, more severe than Step 288's own prior claim that one relation reaches Level 5.

b_rows_sample.anchor: G-62 Compare undefined ... 012 section 46 defines it: Compare: P x P x C x Omega -> Q, with two companions, both partial: Resolve, Normalize
b_rows_sample.statement: Closes (narrows, not fully) the standing gap G-62 'Compare undefined': step-012 section 46 supplies a signature, Compare: P x P x C x Omega -> Q with Q = {Equivalent, Compatible, Contradictory, Related, Independent, Unknown}, plus two partial companion functions Resolve: R x C -\-> X and Normalize: R x Omega -\-> P. G-62 moves from OPEN-undefined to DEFINED(signature)-body-still-absent -- a signature is Level 3, not Level 6, so the gap narrows rather than closes. This reframes the programme's single named blocker 'Qualify' as one instance of a family of four partial epistemic functions (Qualify, Resolve, Normalize, Compare), all partial, all typed, none with bodies -- a better-posed problem (a discipline for partial epistemic functions) than a lone blocker.

type_signature.domain: Proposition x Proposition x Context x Ontology

b_rows_sample.anchor: Semantic equivalence is generally not fully decidable ... equiv can NEVER reach Level 5 in the Boolean sense. This is a theorem-shaped limit, not a work item.
b_rows_sample.statement: Strengthens the Level-5 verdict on semantic equality (previously marked undecidable only for the weak reason 'no procedure specified'): step-012 section 35 gives the strong reason -- for arbitrary natural language, semantic equivalence P1≡P2 is not generally decidable, so KnowledgeOS cannot promise it will always determine whether two arbitrary sentences mean the same thing. This is framed as a theorem-shaped limit, not a work item: semantic equality can never reach a total Boolean decision procedure. Section 35 draws the corollary that the system must be able to say 'I don't know whether these mean the same thing' as a feature, not a failure -- the same rule independently found at three other loci (Step 224.11, 25S.4, 38.22), now four independent loci agreeing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: FOUR rival codomains ... The relation itself should not be confused with its epistemic certainty. ... SC = (P1,P2,Relation,Context,Basis,Status)
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a prior count of two rival equality-decision codomains to four: 25S.3 {Same,Different,PossibleSame,Unknown}; 38.10 {Unknown,Candidate,Probable,Confirmed,Rejected,Contextual}; 012 section 35 {Determined,Supported,Candidate,Unknown}; 012 section 36/46 {Equivalent,Compatible,Contradictory,Related,Independent,Unknown}. Step 012 section 36 supplies the sorting principle: 'the relation itself should not be confused with its epistemic certainty' -- distinguishing a Relation dimension (what holds) from a Status dimension (how well we know it); 25S.3 is flagged as conflating the two (Same/Different are relations, PossibleSame/Unknown are statuses). Corpus product forms are recovered (012 section 36/47): SC=(P1,P2,Relation,Context,Basis,Status), ComparisonResult=(Relation,Basis,Confidence,Context,Provenance), ResolutionResult=(CandidateEntity,Status,Evidence,Provenance) -- equality decisions return epistemic objects, not verdicts. A non-corpus reconciliation is offered (marked DERIVED, not corpus, not adopted): Decide_equiv: K x K -> (Relation x Status), noting three of the four corpus codomains are flattenings of this product -- the same defect shape independently noted for Sigma's ten-value flattening of five axes, a second (still unpromoted) occurrence of that pattern.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 038 treats equality as a classification problem with asymmetric loss ... Cost(FalseMerge) != Cost(FalseSplit) ... identity thresholds should be domain-specific
b_rows_sample.statement: Recovers a decision-theoretic layer entirely absent from Step 288: identity/equality resolution is framed as classification under asymmetric loss -- false merge (38.18: wrong evidence aggregation, false conflicts, contaminated statistics) versus false split (38.19: duplicated knowledge, missed contradictions, fragmented provenance), with Cost(FalseMerge) != Cost(FalseSplit) implying identity thresholds should be domain-specific (38.20), a precision/recall tradeoff favoring conservative (high-precision) identity policies (38.21), and two invariants: UnknownIdentity should generally remain Unknown rather than being silently merged (38.22), and probabilistic identity must not silently become confirmed identity (38.23, 38.80). Explicitly flagged as well-posed but entirely unparameterized: no loss function, threshold, or calibration is specified, and it inherits the standing gap of no probability space (Omega, F, P) (G-22/MT-1), so a stated posterior like 'P(Same)=0.98' (38.23) has no measure-theoretic referent in this theory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: UniqueIdentifier should be treated as strong evidence, not metaphysical truth ... My grantId collision is an instance of a corpus-named failure class, not a novel finding.
b_rows_sample.statement: The author's own 'two authority acts colliding on one grantId' counterexample is reclassified as an instance of a corpus-anticipated failure class rather than a novel finding: 38.26 anticipates identifier collisions from misconfiguration, reuse, environment copies, and cloned test data, giving the principle UniqueIdentifier should be treated as strong evidence, not metaphysical truth -- reinforced by 195.29 (don't confuse technical ID with domain identity), 195.49/I_49 (identifier reuse does not establish identity continuity), and 195.53/I_51 (domain identity must be defined by domain semantics, not inferred from technical representation). The defect's status as real is unchanged; only the credit for identifying the failure class moves to the corpus.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 38.41-42 — a closure operation absent from my O discussion: Closure(Identity) ... KnowledgeOS = G_K + G_P + G_I + TemporalState + EpistemicControl (38.88)
b_rows_sample.statement: Two further recoveries: (1) an identity closure operation absent from the operation discussion, Closure(Identity) computing AffectedKnowledge(x) (38.41-42), with identity merge/split/reassignment required to preserve lineage (195.53/I_50) and identity merge called 'a high-impact transition' (195.36), split called 'epistemically expensive' (38.40); (2) the kernel is architecturally a graph federation, not one graph: KnowledgeOS = G_K + G_P + G_I + TemporalState + EpistemicControl (38.88), with G_I/G_T/G_E/G_C/G_G forming 'a federation of semantic graphs over a common lineage model' that must interact but must not be collapsed (195.43, 38.87/38.88). This conflicts with the canonical kernel's single relational structure R (already reduced to 3 fields elsewhere in the programme): either R is a union of graphs the theory forbids collapsing, or the kernel is missing a component -- recorded as a structural question outside this step's scope, with an explicit caution (195.44) against reading this as a mandate for five separate graphs (risk of over-engineering).

b_rows_sample.anchor: | transitivity unestablished -> quotients may not exist | RESOLVED for cong_I ... | | NINE — Continuity ... | zero unconditional Level-5 state relations
b_rows_sample.statement: Net-effect summary on Step 288: transitivity RESOLVED for identity equivalence within a context (I_48, still open for semantic equality); relation count corrected from eight to NINE (Continuity was missing); '=' reaches Level 5 DOWNGRADED to conditional on an unestablished canonicalization, leaving zero unconditional Level-5 state relations; semantic-equality undecidability STRENGTHENED from 'no procedure specified' to 'not fully decidable, never reachable in the Boolean sense'; rival codomains corrected from two to FOUR, sorted by the Relation-vs-Status principle; 'Qualify is the irreducible blocker' REFRAMED as one of four partial epistemic functions; G-62 Compare NARROWED (signature given, body absent); the five-notion identity matrix gains contextual scoping and orthogonality to lineage; the grantId collision reclassified as corpus-anticipated; a new decision-theoretic layer and a new Closure(Identity)/G_I graph requirement are added. One thing is explicitly recorded as having gotten worse: '=' no longer reaches Level 5 unconditionally.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ✅ **This is the one place the equality/identity problem admits a real narrowing:** `≅_I` **is** an equivalence relation within an identity context and **is not** one across contexts. Quotients exist per-context.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates and situates I_48 within the identity register: identity is context-scoped (38.6/38.7/38.79/38.81: RealWorldIdentity != DomainObjectIdentity; KnowledgeOS must not globally impose GlobalEntityIdentity; identity is contextual), giving I_48 (195.16) as the one place in the whole equality/identity programme that admits a real narrowing -- cong_I is an equivalence relation within an identity context and not one across contexts, so quotients exist per-context. Explicitly flags this as BOUNDED, not established, since 'identity context' is defined nowhere, and notes I_48-I_51 are numbered invariants in a research step with no adoption record.

b_rows_sample.anchor: `38.76`: $\boxed{Identity\ is\ itself\ knowledge}$ ... `38.88`/`195.43` **`G_I` is a SEPARATE graph** that *"must not be collapsed"* — yet the canonical kernel has one `ℛ`, reduced to 3 fields.
b_rows_sample.statement: Recovers that identity is itself a form of knowledge requiring its own epistemic machinery (38.76), with a status codomain IdentityStatus in {Unknown, Candidate, Probable, Confirmed, Rejected, Contextual} (38.10), a non-silent-promotion invariant (38.80: probabilistic identity must not silently become confirmed identity; 38.22: unknown identity should remain unknown), and an identity closure operation Closure(Identity) with AffectedKnowledge(x) (38.42). Notes the tension (also recorded in the identity-continuity seam) between G_I as a required separate graph (38.88/195.43, 'must not be collapsed') and the canonical kernel's single, three-field relational structure ℛ.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ## §15 THE RESULT DOMAIN — "decidable" vs "always returns a decision" ... $$\boxed{\text{A procedure that answers } Unknown \text{ is NOT a complete equality decision procedure.}}$$
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the four rival result-domain codomains (25S.3, 38.10, 012 §35, 012 §36/46) and the Relation-vs-Status sorting principle (012 §36), applying the mandate's own distinction between 'decidable relation' (a total procedure that returns TRUE/FALSE correctly) and 'procedure that always returns a decision' (a total procedure may legitimately answer Unknown without deciding); boxes the resulting principle that an Unknown-returning procedure is NOT a complete equality decision procedure, and reiterates 012 §35's theorem-shaped result that semantic equality can never reach a total Boolean procedure, agreeing with three other independent loci (224.11, 25S.4, 38.22) that this is a feature, not a failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The platform cannot attest a specified session execution. identity binding must NOT be placed inside C-10's authoritative state, because C-10 cannot establish it. It is C-5-shaped
a_rows_sample.statement: The sharpest finding in the D3 prep: a C-10 receipt's binding to a specific session execution can never be stronger than what INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2 permit (self-declared, not attested), so identity binding cannot be placed inside C-10's authoritative state -- it is C-5-shaped, and C-5 owns no attestation record either.

a_rows_sample.anchor: M4 must be classified NOT ATTESTED -- never MISSING. ... Calling it MISSING asserts "no receipt", which the evidence does not support. Calling it present asserts a binding the platform cannot make.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extension of the NOT-ATTESTED-never-PASS discipline to condition classification: a receipt that exists but cannot be bound to its executing session (M4) must be classified NOT ATTESTED, since calling it MISSING or VALID would each assert something the platform cannot establish.

a_rows_sample.anchor: two residues no selection resolves ... knowledge versions K ... all three new propositions are silent on it ... S is unattestable. INV-ATTR-1 -- no gate reads identity ... E2 must mark the session-execution reference RECORDED, NOT ATTESTED.
a_rows_sample.statement: Two residues survive any D1 selection unresolved: whether 'knowledge versions K' remains a required receipt property (silently dropped by all three new propositions), and that the session-execution reference S must be marked RECORDED-NOT-ATTESTED per INV-ATTR-1/D4.3's M4 finding, both flagged for E2 (receipt completeness) to settle.

a_rows_sample.anchor: recording session identity != attesting session identity ... recording an applicability reference != attesting correctness of applicability
a_rows_sample.statement: D3 formalises two non-equivalences carrying the decision: recording session identity is not attesting session identity, and recording an applicability reference is not attesting the correctness of applicability -- the platform cannot attest 'a specified session execution' (INV-ATTR-1/2), so identity binding is placed outside C-10's boundary entirely.

a_rows_sample.anchor: One prohibition, three surfaces: an unresolved status may never be laundered into a resolved one.
a_rows_sample.statement: A single cross-cutting prohibition is observed recurring in three independent places in the estate's governance (independence classification, C-5 separation dimensions, D4.1 compensating controls, later a fourth at D4.3 M4): an unresolved epistemic status must never be laundered into a resolved one -- recorded as an observation bearing on, but distinct from, the canonical unifying-invariant candidate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: THE REVIEWER MUST BE A FRESH INDEPENDENT ARCHITECTURE PROCESS ... Satisfied on the measurement in §2.2: this is a process with no registered role in the chain.
a_rows_sample.statement: Demonstrates the independence-verification method in practice: enumerate every process occurrence across all transitions and grants in the aggregate plus a whole-repository grep, and treat zero occurrences as the only admissible basis for eligibility.

a_rows_sample.anchor: independence is not transferable: an assignment whose recorded evidence names a8ce5a39 cannot be discharged by 8a525719 without the record asserting something false about who did the work.
a_rows_sample.statement: Names a second-order independence failure distinct from personal ineligibility: a genuinely independent process cannot discharge a review under a workflow lane whose registered execution context names a different process, since INV-ATTR-1 means the engine itself would never detect the substitution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I will not adopt another process's identity in order to become operable.
a_rows_sample.statement: States a refusal principle: a process must not adopt a different, already-registered process's self-declared identity merely to satisfy a commission's addressee field and become operable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: you may self-bind identity; you may never self-choose role, scope, work item, or authority.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the governing invariant for the candidate-declaration mechanism: a process may discover and declare its own runtime identity, but may never self-select the role, scope, work item, or authority it is to hold -- those must come from the authoritative commission (AST-018 next-actor), with a MISMATCH between the prompt's claimed role and the commission's role forcing STOP (GO-08).

a_rows_sample.anchor: F-3 is disclosed as aggravating, not exculpatory: producing this record adds a further participating act by 77b85fa3 on this work item. If the PO/ARB's ruling turns on 'has this process already acted here,' this record is itself part of the evidence against it.
a_rows_sample.statement: A candidate for an independence-sensitive review role discloses that the very act of writing its own declaration record is itself a further participating act that could count against its own independence, explicitly refusing to treat its own record-production as exculpatory -- an instance of radical self-disclosure over self-serving interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not decide for yourself that read-only orientation is or is not participation if the governing policy is ambiguous. Report the factual evidence. The candidate therefore returned UNDETERMINED and stopped, rather than self-certifying under reading B.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes a governance behavioral principle: when a governing policy is deliberately left as a placeholder and genuinely ambiguous, the correct response for a self-assessing process is to report factual evidence and return UNDETERMINED rather than adjudicate the ambiguity in its own favor, escalating the open question to the PO/ARB with named legitimate dispositions instead of a recommendation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: role != process identity, identity != eligibility, eligibility != appointment, appointment != activation, activation != authorization ... A process identity is DISCOVERED FROM THE RUNTIME -- never invented by the human, copied from another session, inferred from prompt text, or chosen from a human-entered UUID.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a six-link non-collapse chain of governance-identity concepts (role != process identity != eligibility != appointment != activation != authorization), each a genuinely separate step, and the rule that process identity is always discovered from the runtime, never supplied, copied, inferred, or human-chosen.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Basis: PROVENANCE ATTRIBUTION -- not self-declaration. The producer never declared this identity in any governed artifact. It is attributed here by a third party from runtime evidence. ... Every prior identity in this estate was declared by the process itself. This one is attributed by a third party from evidence the producer never confirmed. That is a new act type here.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces provenance-attributed identity as a genuinely new act type in this estate's governance model, distinct from the previously universal rule (INV-ATTR-1/2, G-2) that process identity is always self-declared and never attestable by others: here Governance attributes a producer identity to a third-party process from transcript timestamp/content evidence the producer itself never confirmed, bounded explicitly as barring-only (never enabling), evidentially grounded in operator-side transcripts outside the governed repository store, and remaining falsifiable/supersedable if contradicting evidence appears.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A previous candidate on the parent work item read the material first and declared afterwards. Its own reading then became prior participation ... Do not repeat that. Establish your identity FIRST. Check the bars FIRST. Read ONLY the authoritative state ... Declare. Then STOP.
a_rows_sample.statement: Institutionalizes a corrective procedural step ('declare before you orient') directly caused by the S0375 episode where a candidate's own pre-declaration reading became disqualifying prior participation with no policy able to resolve it; the fix reorders the candidate protocol (identity first, bars first, then only the minimal authoritative state, then declare and stop) without deciding the underlying open independence-policy question, which remains open.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The appointment names a ROLE, not a process. It deliberately contains no session identifier, and none was invented. Appointee identity: NOT DECLARED -- it comes from the runtime of the fresh session the PO/ARB starts.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reconfirms, in a concrete appointment act, that a governed appointment names only a role and never invents or pre-selects a process identity -- the appointee's identity is discovered later from the runtime of whichever fresh session the human actually starts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: process context continuity != workflow session identity continuity ... A Claude restart can produce a different CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID while retaining essentially the same working conversation and context. ... This is the temporal extension of INV-ATTR-1/2, not a new subject.
a_rows_sample.statement: States observation O-5: process context continuity is not the same as workflow session identity continuity -- a Claude restart can yield a new CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID while the same working context persists, so process identity is not only self-declared and unattestable (INV-ATTR-1/2) but also temporally unstable across restarts, and this instability is itself a temporal extension of INV-ATTR-1/2 rather than a separate subject.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Direction A -- false independence (the dangerous one; the one that actually materialised). ... Nothing malicious is required. A restart is enough. ... Direction B -- lost continuity (the tolerable one). ... The rule below deliberately errs toward Direction B. A wrongly-barred process needs one governed act to be re-established. A wrongly-admitted one cannot be repaired at all.
a_rows_sample.statement: Analyzes the O-5 instability as producing two asymmetric failure directions: (A) false independence -- a restarted process presenting a clean UUID could be wrongly admitted as independent while carrying the complete prior context of the very work it should be excluded from, destroying the independence guarantee retrospectively with a record that looks clean; (B) lost continuity -- a legitimately continuing process cannot prove it is the registered lane holder and must be re-established, a merely tolerable cost. States the governing principle that any remedy must err toward B, since a wrongly-barred process is one governed act away from repair while a wrongly-admitted one can never be repaired because its check was never actually independent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Independence must be declared and assessed on PRIOR PARTICIPATION, not on identity difference. A different UUID is necessary but not sufficient evidence of independence. ... A restarted process is a new candidate until Governance explicitly establishes its participation.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the corollary that carries the load: independence must be assessed on disclosed prior participation, never merely on identity difference, since a different UUID is necessary but not sufficient evidence of true independence; the resulting safe rule is that a restarted process is treated as a new candidate until Governance explicitly re-establishes its participation, explicitly rejecting as dangerous the alternative of treating UUIDs as durable, permanent identities.

a_rows_sample.anchor: That process authored ASD-001, scoped REPAIR-001, recorded the CONTINUATION (seq 5) and the grant G-REPAIR-001, and wrote the candidate-declaration prompt. Appointing it would collapse the separation between Governance analysis and Implementation ... The mechanism would not have caught this. AST-018 appoint might well have accepted e40f3fd0.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms O-5's abstract danger with a concrete live instance: the governance-recording process that scoped and authorized REPAIR-001 reappeared under a new runtime identifier (e40f3fd0) after a restart, which appears on no identity bar list, so the mechanical appointment check (AST-018 appoint) would have accepted it as independent -- the bar had to be applied manually by the PO/ARB on participation grounds since the mechanism itself would not have caught it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This process added itself to the implementer bar the moment it recorded §2-§6. Governance-recording is not a lane, but it is participation.
a_rows_sample.statement: States that a process recording a governance decision, though holding no formal workflow lane, is itself a participation act that self-bars that process from later filling an independence-sensitive role on the same matter -- governance-recording capacity is explicitly not exempt from participation-based exclusion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-4/C-7: ADDRESSED BUT NOT CLOSED ... DV-1 — the one unsafe-direction gap ... the durable copy is written twice after its last all-or-nothing verification ... and re-verified nowhere.
b_rows_sample.statement: AMD6's independent review finds a genuine safety gap (DV-1) in the durability migration plan: the durable authoritative copy is written after its last all-or-nothing verification and never re-verified before the source is removed, so Phase 7's gate could report success while the durable copy is silently incomplete.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'the FIRST record in the authoritative store' is false under the plan's own record vocabulary ... Truth is 'first governance append after the writer switch'
b_rows_sample.statement: Names DV-3: the migration plan's acceptance criterion 17 uses an inaccurate phrase ('first record in the authoritative store', which is literally false because Phase 3 already copied records into it) and must be replaced by 'first governance append after the authority transfer.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Phase 5 remains prohibited ... DV-1 is the critical one because it creates an unsafe path to Phase 7.
b_rows_sample.statement: Prescribes the next lawful sequence after the DV-1..DV-7 findings: register/route a new Architecture correction commission only (not a Governance decision document), then Architecture authors the fix, then a fresh independent Architecture review, then Governance's bounded review, then PO/ARB; Phase 5 must not execute until DV-1 is repaired and reviewed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The durability migration chain (AMD3→AMD6) is literally the test corpus the assurance checker is being built to back-test against, and the checker's job list is literally the migration's own mandated pre-delivery verification.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finds that the two seemingly separate work items (cost-optimization/deterministic-assurance, and the durability migration) already share the same evidence base and back-test corpus, so integration is a sequencing/authority problem rather than a new architecture problem; the checker must remain warn-only through Phase 1 to avoid itself becoming a governance object requiring authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DV-1 = UNSAFE ... Business: Migration must not start yet because there is still a real risk of losing governance evidence.' Not: Migration is almost finished.
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked counterexample showing what an incorrect over-simplified business translation would say versus the correct uncertainty-preserving translation of the DV-1 durability finding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Decision status is graded, not monolithic: ADR artifact = PROPOSED ('recommends an architecture and decides nothing'); a separate PO/ARB DECISION ACT (2026-08-19) = DECIDED: D1 = B′ adopted, D2 = R-CONFLICT adopt, D3 = existing placement governance.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that decision status must be read as a graded record: an ADR document being PROPOSED does not contradict a separate PO/ARB decision act having already DECIDED specific numbered items from it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D9 | Separation: source of execution vs evidence of execution vs authoritative decision record (B′ relocation, R-CONFLICT) | DECIDED (PO/ARB 2026-08-19, D1–D2) — recorded, not re-decided here
b_rows_sample.statement: Reconciliation-document claim register entry D9: the three-way separation and B′/R-CONFLICT decisions are recorded here as already DECIDED by a separate PO/ARB act, never re-decided by this reconciliation document itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1 RE-HASH ... 1b RECONCILE/DISPOSE DELTA ... 2 READERS ... 3 THE WRITER ← THE AUTHORITY-TRANSFER INSTANT ... 4 RUNTIME DEMOTION MARKER ... 5 STAGING MARKER RETRACTION
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the single canonical Phase-5 slot sequence (1, 1b, 2, 3, 4, 5) with slot 1b's three outcomes (no delta/continue, reconcilable delta/continue, unreconcilable delta/freeze-violation-STOP), replacing two previously-competing enumerations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A MOVE is refused because it would LAUNDER THE QUARANTINE — a post-demotion record lies OUTSIDE the enumeration by definition, so moving it out HIDES the quarantined evidence, makes the source SPURIOUSLY SATISFY criterion 12.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects an earlier, inverted justification for forbidding a quarantined record's relocation (previously reasoned as 'would alter the demoted store'); the true reason is that moving it would make a failing Phase-7 comparison spuriously pass.

b_rows_sample.anchor: OPEN-M7 — quarantine disposition — the disposer AND the path ... The one open item that can block the migration's COMPLETION indefinitely.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies that the workflow mechanism has an act class for disposing a quarantine (a governance act) but literally no DISPOSE transition type, so an undisposed quarantine can block migration completion indefinitely by design, not by oversight.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A quarantine is a DOMAIN STATE with a business consequence, not a directory condition. The block is not a tooling limitation to engineer away — it is the aggregate refusing an invalid transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes quarantine-blocking-completion as a DDD invariant (an aggregate refusing an invalid state transition) rather than a filesystem/tooling limitation to be worked around.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the switch-over record is the FIRST GOVERNANCE APPEND AFTER THE AUTHORITY TRANSFER (⛔ superseded wording: 'that store's first record' — false, not merely imprecise: Phase 3 has already copied governance records into that store.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the acceptance-criterion phrase describing the authoritative store's identifying record: it must read 'first governance append after the authority transfer', not 'that store's first record', because prior copied records already exist there.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the grant count moved 110 → 114 since AMD5, and it is C-4's premise observed live: those four grants are AMD6's OWN commission, appended by P-1 into the corpus the migration freezes and hashes.
b_rows_sample.statement: A self-referential observation: the ongoing governance work authorizing this very amendment is itself appended to the corpus the migration plan proposes to freeze, meaning a literal freeze would have had to prohibit the act that authorized the amendment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ELIGIBILITY OUTCOME AS RECORDED: bc1b47ef - AUTHORING ELIGIBLE, REVIEWING BARRED, ACCEPTING BARRED ... A FRESH INDEPENDENT ARCHITECTURE PROCESS - REVIEWING ... REQUIRED.
b_rows_sample.statement: A registered grant explicitly restores a producer's authoring eligibility while permanently barring it from reviewing or accepting its own amendment (AMD6), which the reviewer here reads directly from the record rather than inferring.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A reviewer checking only the two names it was handed would have PASSED this gate and proceeded ... this is exactly why the same commission forbids hand-copied grant lists: the chat-supplied exclusion set was narrower than the governed one.
b_rows_sample.statement: Demonstrates the failure mode of trusting a prompt-supplied exclusion list rather than the governed record: the chat-supplied set of two barred names missed a fourth clause that fires on a registered grant covering the same performer under a different role in this same chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1 PO/ARB starts a FRESH Architecture session ... 2 that session DECLARES its own identity ... 3 GOVERNANCE ... appends REGISTER ... then HANDOFF ... 4 START recorded with THIS PO/ARB act as its humanAct ... 5 the fresh reviewer consumes G-…-DV-CORRECTION-READING-ORDER as its index
b_rows_sample.statement: Prescribes the exact five-step lawful sequence that would unblock the deadlocked reviewer-appointment problem without a barred process appointing its own judge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: THE REVIEWER MUST BE A FRESH INDEPENDENT ARCHITECTURE PROCESS ... Satisfied on the measurement in §2.2: this is a process with no registered role in the chain.
b_rows_sample.statement: Demonstrates the independence-verification method in practice: enumerate every process occurrence across all transitions and grants in the aggregate plus a whole-repository grep, and treat zero occurrences as the only admissible basis for eligibility.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the reviewer must not be its own registrar — the same reason bc1b47ef refused to appoint its own judge, applied to the other end of the same edge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the 'a barred process must not appoint its own judge' principle to its symmetric case: an eligible candidate reviewer must also not register/hand-off its own assignment, since separation is the entire point of the lane.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the eligibility set keeps narrowing — every candidate reviewer that declares eligibility and is then not started adds one more name to it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Observes a structural risk pattern: repeatedly declaring and abandoning candidate reviewers without recording a START permanently shrinks the pool of processes still eligible to review, since each attempt itself becomes a disqualifying prior-participation fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The document is a good consolidation, but I would NOT ratify it as 'KnowledgeOS Kernel Theory v1.3 fully closed and complete.' ... it correctly identifies the earlier over-claims, but then reintroduces essentially the same problem at CLOSURE-3/4/5: a small executable demonstration is being promoted into a mathematical/architectural proof.
a_rows_sample.statement: Overall verdict: accepts the CLOSURE consolidation's Section-1 downgrades as sound but refuses to ratify the whole document as complete, identifying that CLOSURE-3/4/5 repeat the exact same error-pattern the earlier sections corrected -- promoting a small executable demonstration into a mathematical/architectural proof.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CLOSURE-5 is where the document fails the strongest test ... the EA test is not actually testing the stated predicates. Soundness: the declared requirement is forall d in R_req: Preserve(d,...)=true. But the implementation only checks 'provenance' in node for active nodes ... required_distinctions=['provenance','isolation_boundary'] but does not actually verify both distinctions. So: Declared R_req != Tested R_req. That invalidates the claimed general soundness result.
a_rows_sample.statement: Audits the CLOSURE-5 Soundness test's implementation against its stated predicate and finds a mismatch: the code passes a required_distinctions list of two items (provenance, isolation_boundary) but the check_adequacy implementation only tests presence of a 'provenance' key on active nodes, never actually checking the second declared distinction -- Declared R_req != Tested R_req, invalidating the claimed general soundness result for that test.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Isolation test is effectively tautological ... It checks whether a node that is not the firewall target is also in the firewall set. It does not actually execute Det(EVal(K_isolated,q,Gamma)) and verify that the clean node remains determinable. So the mathematical requirement q not-in Scope(Contr(p),Gamma) implies Actionability != BLOCKED is not what the test implements. It tests a much weaker structural property.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies that the CLOSURE-5 Psi_Isolation test is tautological: it merely checks that a non-firewall-target node is not itself in the firewall set (structurally true by construction), and never actually calls Det(EVal(...)) to verify the clean node remains determinable with non-BLOCKED actionability -- the implemented check is strictly weaker than the stated mathematical requirement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The termination test is not a complexity proof ... T <= C(|V|+|E|) but the implementation checks elapsed<0.05 ... A 50ms runtime on one small graph cannot establish O(|V|+|E|). Complexity requires analysis of the algorithm or systematic scaling experiments. Therefore: Termination: NOT VERIFIED. At most: implementation completed within the selected benchmark timeout.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies that the CLOSURE-5 Psi_Termination test (a single 50ms wall-clock timeout check on one small graph) does not and cannot establish the claimed asymptotic bound T<=C(|V|+|E|); asymptotic complexity requires algorithmic analysis or systematic scaling experiments across graph sizes, neither of which is present. Downgrades the finding to 'implementation completed within the selected benchmark timeout', marking Termination NOT VERIFIED.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Determinism test is the strongest CLOSURE-5 result ... Replay of the same operations from the same initial state gives the same state hash ... But even here, it proves determinism of that implementation, not determinism of ABK-1 as a mathematical architecture. ... Replay determinism: tested. Constitutional determinism: candidate.
a_rows_sample.statement: Judges the CLOSURE-5 Psi_Determinism test the strongest of the four (replaying the same operation sequence from the same initial state reproduces the identical state hash), but scopes the result carefully: it proves determinism of that specific implementation, not of ABK-1 as a mathematical architecture in general, and notes deterministic hashing depends on canonical serialization -- classifying Replay determinism as tested but Constitutional determinism only as candidate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Unique minimal' ABK-1 is not demonstrated ... The candidate table compares four representations. That can establish at most: ABK-1 was the only candidate among these four tested candidates that passed the declared test suite. It cannot establish: ABK-1=unique minimal architecture unless you have [7 listed requirements]. None of those are demonstrated. So: ABK-1 SELECTED FROM TESTED CANDIDATES may be defensible later. But: ABK-1 mathematically proved uniquely minimal is not.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the 'ABK-1 is the unique minimal Kernel Architecture' claim as unsupported: the four-candidate comparison establishes at most that ABK-1 was the only one of these four tested candidates to pass the declared test suite, which is not the same as mathematical uniqueness-and-minimality, which would require a defined candidate space, an explicit minimality ordering, exhaustive or justified candidate coverage, valid adequacy predicates and implementations, independent test scenarios, and no hidden favoritism toward ABK-1 -- none of which are demonstrated. Proposes the defensible restatement 'ABK-1 SELECTED FROM TESTED CANDIDATES'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: There is also a serious circularity in CLOSURE-5 ... the candidate being evaluated is already defined with: nodes, edges, firewalls, provenance. And the EA tests require: provenance, isolation. So the candidate is structurally equipped with the exact properties the test asks for. This creates a potential representation-selection circularity: ABK-1 -> defines tested distinctions -> EA -> ABK-1 passes. rather than: R_req -> independent adequacy criteria -> candidate comparison -> selection.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a representation-selection circularity in the CLOSURE-5 kernel-selection process: ABK-1's own data structure (nodes/edges/firewalls/provenance) already contains exactly the fields the Executable Adequacy test checks for, so the process runs ABK-1 -> defines tested distinctions -> EA -> ABK-1 passes rather than the intended independent chain R_req -> independent adequacy criteria -> candidate comparison -> selection; warns this is a structural risk regardless of whether it was deliberate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would reduce the remaining work to four decisive packages. C1 -- Determination semantics ... No Actionability inside Determination. C2 -- Operations + delta ... C3 -- Composition + equivalence ... define approx_{Q,Gamma,O} as observational equivalence first. Only promote it to semantic equivalence if a bridge is established. C4 -- Independent kernel selection ... The test must be candidate-independent. R_req -> Adequacy Criteria -> Independent Test Suite -> Candidate Architectures -> Evidence -> Selection. I would still avoid 'unique minimal' unless we formally prove minimality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reduces remaining closure work to four decisive packages: C1 Determination semantics (excluding Actionability); C2 Operations+delta (per-operation Pre/Input/Post/Invariants/Provenance/Failure/Partiality, then test delta against identity/persistence/retraction/supersession/invalidation/isolation/provenance); C3 Composition+equivalence (establish composition-algebra properties, define observational equivalence FIRST and only promote to semantic equivalence if a bridge is separately established); C4 Independent, candidate-blind kernel selection following the chain R_req->AdequacyCriteria->IndependentTestSuite->CandidateArchitectures->Evidence->Selection, still avoiding 'unique minimal' language unless minimality is formally proven.

b_rows_sample.statement: Formally reclassifies every execution-harness test in the preceding closure packages as Category C (Implementation Obligation) or Category D (Empirical Obligation), explicitly rejecting the claim that test-harness execution constitutes mathematical proof -- directly resolving the recurring test-vs-proof conflation criticized across multiple earlier reviews in this batch.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Eradication of the False 'Unique Minimality' Theorem ... We permanently abandon the 'Unique Minimal' overclaim. b_rows_sample.statement: Permanently abandons the 'ABK-1 is the unique minimal KnowledgeOS kernel' overclaim, replacing it with 'ABK-1 is a validated, candidate-adequate kernel architecture for the target problem class', while explicitly designating global minimality across all uncharacterized representation spaces OPEN BY DESIGN (a deliberate, permanent non-closure rather than a pending gap) -- resolving the representation-selection circularity concern by simply not claiming what the circularity would have needed to support.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Frozen Constitutional Axioms: Axiom 1 (Pipeline Separation) ... Axiom 2 (Non-Explosion under Contradiction) ... Axiom 3 (Representation Adequacy): Adequate(K,Q,Gamma) iff R_req(Q,Gamma) subseteq Distinctions(K) ... Axiom 4 (History-Preserving State Evolution) ... Axiom 5 (Existential Query Sensitivity) ... Axiom 6 (Governance Boundary Decoupling): Determination = <Status,DeterminationBound,RiskProfile>. The core determination entity contains zero governance operational flags.
b_rows_sample.statement: Freezes six constitutional axioms as 'the unalterable core of KnowledgeOS Kernel Theory v1.3': (1) Pipeline Separation across Truth/EVal/Det/GovernanceAction; (2) Non-Explosion (a local contradiction does not license deriving every proposition); (3) Representation Adequacy (Adequate(K,Q,Gamma) iff R_req(Q,Gamma) subseteq Distinctions(K)); (4) History-Preserving State Evolution (V and H monotonic under every O_core operation); (5) Existential Query Sensitivity (every valid state has at least two queries yielding different determinations); (6) Governance Boundary Decoupling (Determination carries zero governance/Actionability fields).

b_rows_sample.anchor: You have completed the constitutional theory closure at the explicitly declared scope. b_rows_sample.statement: The follow-up review's central finding, and the first largely affirmative verdict in this batch's whole closure-critique lineage: the constitutional theory closure at the explicitly declared scope IS legitimately completed, distinct from (and not claiming to be) a mathematically complete theory of all EVal/Determination/operation/composition semantics -- judged a legitimate way to close a theory once 'closed' is formally defined via the A-E criticality classification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: three technical issues I would fix before signing ... Issue 1 -- the confidence interval is still mathematically problematic ... b_rows_sample.statement: Notes the ConfidenceInterval-vs-DeterminationBound terminology fix is already correctly reflected in the frozen Axiom 6, but recommends ensuring it is applied consistently everywhere (including in any remaining implementation code) since the underlying arithmetic (net +- mu) still does not constitute a genuine statistical confidence interval without a measurement model; classifies this as a terminology correction, not a new open research question.

b_rows_sample.anchor: are we finished? ... Discovery: CLOSED. Yes ... Constitutional Kernel Theory: CLOSED AT DECLARED SCOPE. Yes. b_rows_sample.statement: States the three-tier final verdict distinguishing scope: (1) Discovery -- CLOSED; (2) Constitutional Kernel Theory -- CLOSED AT DECLARED SCOPE, accepted conditional on the listed wording corrections; (3) a Complete mathematical theory of all KnowledgeOS behavior -- explicitly NOT CLOSED AND DOES NOT NEED TO BE, listing eight items (concrete evidence aggregation, application-specific contradiction scope, statistical measurement models, implementation complexity, production scaling, complete operation algebra, all possible representations, global minimality) as deliberately outside the constitutional closure boundary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: My recommended final status ... KnowledgeOS Kernel Theory v1.3 -- THEORETICALLY CLOSED AT DECLARED CONSTITUTIONAL SCOPE. Not: 'Fully complete.' And not: 'All mathematical semantics are solved.' ... Final decision: YES -- we can now close KnowledgeOS Kernel Theory v1.3, but only with the qualifier 'at declared constitutional scope.' b_rows_sample.statement: Final decision of this review and, functionally, of the whole closure-cascade lineage in this batch: YES, KnowledgeOS Kernel Theory v1.3 can be closed, but only with the qualifier 'at declared constitutional scope' (never 'fully complete' or 'all mathematical semantics are solved'); explicitly declines to open a further 'CLOSURE-6' iteration, recommending only a small editorial/terminology normalization pass (the five corrections listed) before final sign-off.

a_rows_sample.statement: The decisive convergence finding: three independent methods (executed regex over 182 sources finding I*={Provenance}; executed role-comparison finding Provenance in only 5/9 kernels, absent from BOTH current kernels 230v1 and 232v2; and the formal counterexample showing L=History(T) fails to derive external provenance at t=0) converge on the sharpest structural finding of the reconciliation gate: the history's only universal invariant is absent from the kernel claiming to reconstruct that history, and the argument for its absence (L=History(T)) does not itself hold.

a_rows_sample.anchor: transformation 8/9 <- the only near-universal primitive. policy 6/9. ... transformation is the only role appearing in 8 of 9 kernels. If any single primitive is historically warranted, it is that one.
a_rows_sample.statement: Executed role-coverage count across all nine kernels: transformation appears in 8/9 (the only near-universal primitive), policy 6/9, {event,provenance,artifact,invariant,state,type} 5/9 each, {context,evidence,authority} 4/9, {status,identity,lineage} 2/9, {graph,temporalvalidity,observation,decision,assessment,action} 1/9 -- transformation being the one role historically warranted as a primitive is consistent with the corpus's own headline 'KnowledgeOS approx Governed Knowledge State Transformation System'.

a_rows_sample.statement: A systemic finding: Step 236 (primary corpus, written 10:13:01) reproduces this verification programme's own prior findings (from an artifact written 09:00:36) nearly verbatim -- the '6 of 182 steps named, 0 quoted, 176 absent' finding, the 'EL=empty set' notation, the 'four-to-five-step deferral chain' phrase -- attributing them anonymously to 'one of the audit artifacts'/'the corpus audit' without naming this verification programme.

a_rows_sample.statement: Circularity-hazard response: the verifier explicitly declines to treat Step 236 as independent corroboration of its own prior findings, since doing so would merely confirm its own analysis reflected back at itself -- Step 236 is instead recorded as a corpus RESPONSE to this audit, not as evidence FOR it.

a_rows_sample.statement: Evidence-class inflation is found: Step 236 labels the reproduced findings 'direct evidence', but the verifier's own findings are evidence class D (reasoned conclusions from textual analysis) -- not direct evidence and not empirical evidence about any software; the Reconciliation Gate's own SS11 explicitly forbids exactly this kind of evidence-class upgrade.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A -- ESTABLISHED: Nine candidate kernels exist; 27 of 36 pairs compete ... B -- PROVEN UNDER EXPLICIT ASSUMPTIONS ... C -- PLAUSIBLE/PROPOSED: That the two lineages could be unified via artifact->state and invariant->policy. No document proposes this; it is my conjecture. D -- REFUTED/UNDER-SPECIFIE
a_rows_sample.statement: Final 4-class verdict per the gate's own mandated schema: (A) ESTABLISHED -- 9 kernels exist with 27/36 competing pairs, two disjoint never-reconciled lineages, Step 232's two incommensurable structures, the partial closure repair, transformation as the sole near-universal primitive, Provenance as I* yet absent from both current kernels; (B) PROVEN UNDER EXPLICIT ASSUMPTIONS -- L=History(T) holds for internal lineage only; (C) PLAUSIBLE/PROPOSED -- the two lineages COULD be unified via artifact->state and invariant->policy mappings, explicitly labeled the verifier's own unestablished conjecture, proposed by no corpus document; (D) REFUTED/UNDER-SPECIFIED -- 070's minimality (REFUTED via TV-F-043), 230/232's minimality (UNPROVEN), mathbb K's well-typedness (UNDER-SPECIFIED), kernel independence (REFUTED for both 230 and 232), and 'one evolving theory' itself (REFUTED -- two competing lineages).

a_rows_sample.anchor: I have not chosen a kernel. All nine remain live. ... I have not repaired K's typing, ⊨'s semantics, or the independence failure. Nothing here is empirically validated. Corpus record: 494 files, 238 steps, zero empirical acts.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit discipline statement of what must NOT be concluded from this reconciliation: no kernel has been chosen (all nine remain live), the two lineages have not been merged (the unification conjecture is explicitly the verifier's own, not established), Step 236 has not been treated as corroboration, and nothing here is empirically validated -- corpus record at this point: 494 files, 238 steps, zero empirical acts.

b_rows_sample.statement: Step 242's executive result (independently citing and matching the verification programme's KERNEL-RECONCILIATION-230-236 executed pairwise result): there is not one historical sequence of kernel refinements but at least two competing lineages among nine materially different kernel candidates (0 equivalent, 7 conservative extensions, 27 competing, 2 incomparable) -- the corpus must not force these nine structures to look like one smooth evolution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Lineage A -- artifact-oriented: Artifact, Type, Event, Invariant, Provenance, Transformation, Policy. Lineage B -- state-transformation-oriented: State, Context, Transformation, Evidence, Authority, Policy. ... Equivalence = UNPROVEN.
b_rows_sample.statement: Two historical lineages are confirmed within the primary corpus itself: Lineage A (artifact-oriented: K0 subset K_OS; K_L subset Amended-K subset 201-A-freeze) with vocabulary Artifact/Type/Event/Invariant/Provenance/Transformation/Policy, and Lineage B (state-transformation-oriented: K230v1 subset K232v2) with vocabulary State/Context/Transformation/Evidence/Authority/Policy -- sharing only Transformation and Policy, with equivalence classified UNPROVEN and formally COMPETING.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_8=(E,S,T,O,P,R,\Pi,A) ... Evidence=QualifiedObservation, Claim=Proposition, Identity=EntityIdentityRelation, Provenance=TypedDependencyRelation, Causality=TypedCausalRelation, Decision=PolicyConstrainedActionSelection.
b_rows_sample.statement: K8 is characterized as fundamentally ONTOLOGICAL (answering 'what kinds of things must exist'), with a candidate derivation scheme building higher concepts from its 8 primitives: Evidence=QualifiedObservation, Claim=Proposition, Identity=EntityIdentityRelation, Provenance=TypedDependencyRelation, Causality=TypedCausalRelation, Decision=PolicyConstrainedActionSelection -- a coherent candidate ontology, though several 'derived' definitions still require formal construction.
